```py
                old = slp_render(v, state.strings) if v else ""
                tag = state.edit_tag if state.edit_tag is not None else (v.tag if v else None)
                label = f" new {slp_type_name(tag)} (was {old}): "
            else:
                which = "KEY" if state.add_stage == "key" else "VALUE"
                label = f" new {which} ({slp_type_name(state.edit_tag)}): "
            return input_bar(label, state.buf, state.cur)
        return [(HINT_STYLE,
                 " ↑↓ element   Enter edit   a add   d remove last   "
                 "PgUp/PgDn scrolls   ^X save/exit ")]

    def _bar2():
        if state.edit_err:
            return [(ERR_STYLE, "  " + state.edit_err)]
        if state.mode == "exit_ask":
            return [(HINT_STYLE,
                     "  Y re-encodes and applies to the image (integrity check) · "
                     "the .hbc is written by `patch`")]
        if state.mode in ("type_pick", "add_type_pick"):
            return [(HINT_STYLE, "  <-> choose type - Enter confirms · Esc cancels")]
        if state.mode == "edit":
            return [(HINT_STYLE,
                     "  Enter confirms · Esc cancels · ^T change type (incl. Null/True/False)")]
        if state.mode == "add_edit":
            return [(HINT_STYLE, "  Enter confirms · Esc returns to type")]
        if state.keys is not None:
            return [(HINT_STYLE, "  keys are read-only - only values are editable")]
        return [("", "")]

    kb = KeyBindings()
    in_nav = Condition(lambda: state.mode == "nav")
    in_edit = Condition(lambda: state.mode == "edit")
    in_type_pick = Condition(lambda: state.mode == "type_pick")
    in_ask = Condition(lambda: state.mode == "exit_ask")
    # add_type_pick / add_edit reuse the type_pick / edit navigation; only
    # Enter and Esc dispatch to different methods.
    in_add_type_pick = Condition(lambda: state.mode == "add_type_pick")
    in_add_edit = Condition(lambda: state.mode == "add_edit")
    in_text_entry = Condition(lambda: state.mode in ("edit", "add_edit"))
    in_any_type_pick = Condition(lambda: state.mode in ("type_pick", "add_type_pick"))

    bind_abort(kb, state)

    @kb.add("q", filter=in_nav)
    @kb.add("c-x", filter=in_nav)
    def _q(event):
        state.request_exit(event)

    @kb.add("up", filter=in_nav)
    def _up(event):
        state.move(-1); event.app.invalidate()

    @kb.add("down", filter=in_nav)
    def _down(event):
        state.move(+1); event.app.invalidate()

    @kb.add("pageup", filter=in_nav)
    def _pgup(event):
        state.move(-view_height()); event.app.invalidate()

    @kb.add("pagedown", filter=in_nav)
    def _pgdn(event):
        state.move(+view_height()); event.app.invalidate()

    @kb.add("enter", filter=in_nav)
    def _open_edit(event):
        state.begin_edit(); event.app.invalidate()

    @kb.add("a", filter=in_nav)
    def _add(event):
        state.begin_add(); event.app.invalidate()

    @kb.add("d", filter=in_nav)
    def _remove_last(event):
        state.request_remove_last(); event.app.invalidate()

    @kb.add("escape", filter=in_edit)
    def _cancel(event):
        state.cancel_edit(); event.app.invalidate()

    @kb.add("enter", filter=in_edit)
    def _commit(event):
        state.commit_element(); event.app.invalidate()

    @kb.add("escape", filter=in_add_edit)
    def _cancel_add_edit(event):
        state.cancel_add_edit(); event.app.invalidate()

    @kb.add("enter", filter=in_add_edit)
    def _commit_add_field(event):
        state.commit_add_field(); event.app.invalidate()

    bind_text_input(kb, state, in_text_entry)

    @kb.add("c-t", filter=in_edit)
    def _open_type_pick(event):
        state.open_type_pick(); event.app.invalidate()

    @kb.add("left", filter=in_any_type_pick)
    def _tp_left(event):
        state.type_pick_move(-1); event.app.invalidate()

    @kb.add("right", filter=in_any_type_pick)
    def _tp_right(event):
        state.type_pick_move(+1); event.app.invalidate()

    @kb.add("enter", filter=in_type_pick)
    def _tp_confirm(event):
        state.type_pick_confirm(); event.app.invalidate()

    @kb.add("escape", filter=in_type_pick)
    def _tp_cancel(event):
        state.type_pick_cancel(); event.app.invalidate()

    @kb.add("enter", filter=in_add_type_pick)
    def _atp_confirm(event):
        state.add_type_pick_confirm(); event.app.invalidate()

    @kb.add("escape", filter=in_add_type_pick)
    def _atp_cancel(event):
        state.add_type_pick_cancel(); event.app.invalidate()

    bind_exit_prompt(kb, state, in_ask, cancel_mode="nav")

    run_screen(_title, _body, _status, _bar1, _bar2, kb, _input=_input, _output=_output)
    return state

```

`cli/editor/common.py`:

```py
"""Shared pieces of the three full-screen editors (instructions, strings,
array/object literals): styles, text buffer, prompts and the screen runner."""

from __future__ import annotations

import shutil

from prompt_toolkit import Application
from prompt_toolkit.filters import Condition
from prompt_toolkit.key_binding import KeyBindings
from prompt_toolkit.layout import Layout
from prompt_toolkit.layout.containers import HSplit, Window
from prompt_toolkit.layout.controls import FormattedTextControl

GUTTER_STYLE = "fg:ansibrightblack"
MNEMONIC_STYLE = "bold fg:ansiyellow"
INFO_STYLE = "fg:ansibrightblack"
CURSOR_STYLE = "reverse"
ERR_STYLE = "fg:ansired"
HINT_STYLE = "fg:ansibrightblack"
SEL_STYLE = "reverse"
EMPTY_STYLE = "bold fg:ansired"
DIRTY_MARK_STYLE = "bold fg:ansiyellow"      # modified line (not an error)
INCOMPLETE_MARK_STYLE = "bold fg:ansired"    # line with empty slots to fill in


def fmt_num(x: float) -> str:
    return str(int(x)) if float(x).is_integer() else repr(x)


def strip_kind_suffix(s: str) -> str:
    """Drops the " [identifier]" / " [string]" suffix of a resolved string."""
    for suffix in (" [identifier]", " [string]"):
        if s.endswith(suffix):
            return s[: -len(suffix)]
    return s


def view_height() -> int:
    return max(3, shutil.get_terminal_size().lines - 4)


class TextBufferMixin:
    """Single-line text buffer (`buf`, cursor `cur`) with the usual editing
    keys. Any edit clears `edit_err`."""

    buf: str
    cur: int
    edit_err: str

    def edit_insert(self, ch: str):
        self.buf = self.buf[:self.cur] + ch + self.buf[self.cur:]
        self.cur += len(ch)
        self.edit_err = ""

    def edit_backspace(self):
        if self.cur > 0:
            self.buf = self.buf[:self.cur - 1] + self.buf[self.cur:]
            self.cur -= 1
            self.edit_err = ""

    def edit_delete(self):
        if self.cur < len(self.buf):
            self.buf = self.buf[:self.cur] + self.buf[self.cur + 1:]
            self.edit_err = ""

    def edit_move(self, delta: int):
        self.cur = max(0, min(len(self.buf), self.cur + delta))

    def edit_home(self):
        self.cur = 0

    def edit_end(self):
        self.cur = len(self.buf)


def input_bar(label: str, buf: str, cur: int):
    """Fragments of a one-line input with a block cursor."""
    cur_ch = buf[cur:cur + 1] or " "
    return [(HINT_STYLE, label), ("", buf[:cur]), (CURSOR_STYLE, cur_ch), ("", buf[cur + 1:])]


def apply_discard_cancel_bar(prompt: str):
    """Fragments of the Y / N / Esc prompt shared by the string and array editors."""
    return [
        (DIRTY_MARK_STYLE, prompt),
        ("bold", " Y "), (HINT_STYLE, "apply  "),
        ("bold", " N "), (HINT_STYLE, "discard  "),
        ("bold", " Esc "), (HINT_STYLE, "cancel "),
    ]


def bind_text_input(kb: KeyBindings, state, active: Condition) -> None:
    """Left/Right/Home/End/Backspace/Delete and typing on `state` (a
    TextBufferMixin) while `active`."""
    def edit(method):
        def handler(event):
            getattr(state, method[0])(*method[1:])
            event.app.invalidate()
        return handler

    kb.add("left", filter=active)(edit(("edit_move", -1)))
    kb.add("right", filter=active)(edit(("edit_move", +1)))
    kb.add("home", filter=active)(edit(("edit_home",)))
    kb.add("end", filter=active)(edit(("edit_end",)))
    kb.add("backspace", filter=active)(edit(("edit_backspace",)))
    kb.add("delete", filter=active)(edit(("edit_delete",)))

    @kb.add("<any>", filter=active)
    def _typed(event):
        if event.data and event.data.isprintable():
            state.edit_insert(event.data)
            event.app.invalidate()


def bind_exit_prompt(kb: KeyBindings, state, in_ask: Condition, cancel_mode: str) -> None:
    """Y commits and exits, N discards and exits, Esc goes back to `cancel_mode`."""
    @kb.add("y", filter=in_ask)
    @kb.add("Y", filter=in_ask)
    def _yes(event):
        state.commit = True
        event.app.exit()

    @kb.add("n", filter=in_ask)
    @kb.add("N", filter=in_ask)
    def _no(event):
        state.commit = False
        event.app.exit()

    @kb.add("escape", filter=in_ask)
    def _cancel(event):
        state.mode = cancel_mode
        state.edit_err = ""
        event.app.invalidate()


def bind_abort(kb: KeyBindings, state) -> None:
    """Ctrl+C: always exits without committing."""
    @kb.add("c-c")
    def _cc(event):
        state.commit = False
        event.app.exit()


def run_screen(title, body, status, bar1, bar2, kb: KeyBindings, *, _input=None, _output=None) -> None:
    """Runs the full-screen layout shared by the editors: title, body, status
    line and two bars. `_input`/`_output` are for headless tests only."""
    layout = Layout(HSplit([
        Window(FormattedTextControl(title), height=1),
        Window(FormattedTextControl(body), wrap_lines=False),
        Window(FormattedTextControl(status), height=1),
        Window(FormattedTextControl(bar1), height=1),
        Window(FormattedTextControl(bar2), height=1),
    ]))
    kwargs = {"layout": layout, "key_bindings": kb, "full_screen": True}
    if _input is not None:
        kwargs["input"] = _input
    if _output is not None:
        kwargs["output"] = _output
    Application(**kwargs).run()

```

`cli/editor/instructions.py`:

```py
"""Interactive bytecode editor (`edit func:<N>`).

Token-granularity cursor over a function's instructions. Edits happen in an
in-memory buffer: an operand takes a new value validated against its physical
type, a mnemonic can become any opcode with an identical operand signature
(same size). Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+R undo and redo, `R` restores the current line.
Ctrl+X exits, asking Y/N when the buffer changed.

On Y, a same-size edit is re-encoded by `encode_committed_lines` and applied
through `HermitProject.apply_patch`. Inserting (`o`/`O`) or deleting (Ctrl+K)
instructions changes the layout, so `assemble_committed_function` builds the
AsmInstr list for `HermitProject.apply_insertion` (`Module`: jump relocation,
branch relaxation, EH relocation). The `patch` command writes the new `.hbc`.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from types import SimpleNamespace

from prompt_toolkit.filters import Condition
from prompt_toolkit.key_binding import KeyBindings

import _libhbc
from cli.editor.common import (
    CURSOR_STYLE, DIRTY_MARK_STYLE, EMPTY_STYLE, ERR_STYLE, GUTTER_STYLE, HINT_STYLE,
    INCOMPLETE_MARK_STYLE, INFO_STYLE, MNEMONIC_STYLE, SEL_STYLE,
    bind_abort, bind_exit_prompt, fmt_num, run_screen, strip_kind_suffix, view_height,
)

_T = _libhbc.OperandType

_OP_STYLE = {
    _T.Reg8: "fg:ansicyan", _T.Reg32: "fg:ansicyan",
    _T.StringID: "fg:ansigreen",
    _T.Addr8: "fg:ansimagenta", _T.Addr32: "fg:ansimagenta",
    _T.Imm32: "fg:ansiyellow", _T.Double: "fg:ansiyellow",
}
_OP_KIND_NAME = {
    _T.Reg8: "Reg8", _T.Reg32: "Reg32", _T.UInt8: "UInt8", _T.UInt16: "UInt16",
    _T.UInt32: "UInt32", _T.Imm32: "Imm32", _T.Double: "Double",
    _T.Addr8: "Addr8", _T.Addr32: "Addr32", _T.StringID: "StringID",
}

# allowed ranges per physical type (min, max) inclusive; None = no integer constraint
_INT_RANGE = {
    _T.Reg8: (0, 0xFF), _T.UInt8: (0, 0xFF),
    _T.UInt16: (0, 0xFFFF),
    _T.Reg32: (0, 0xFFFFFFFF), _T.UInt32: (0, 0xFFFFFFFF),
    _T.Imm32: (-(2**31), 2**31 - 1), _T.Addr32: (-(2**31), 2**31 - 1),
    _T.Addr8: (-128, 127),
}


class _Slot:
    __slots__ = ("type", "value", "is_str_ref")

    def __init__(self, type_, value, is_str_ref):
        self.type = type_          # _libhbc.OperandType - PHYSICAL type
        self.value = value         # int (Reg/UInt/Imm/Addr/string index) | float (Double)
        self.is_str_ref = is_str_ref

    def clone(self):
        return _Slot(self.type, self.value, self.is_str_ref)

    def key(self):
        return (self.type, self.value, self.is_str_ref)


class _Line:
    __slots__ = ("nav", "offset", "mnemonic", "opcode", "slots", "dirty", "orig",
                 "note", "inserted", "jump_target")

    def __init__(self, nav, *, offset=None, mnemonic="", opcode=0,
                 slots=(), note="", inserted=False):
        self.nav = nav
        self.offset = offset           # func-relative byte offset; None if inserted
        self.mnemonic = mnemonic
        self.opcode = opcode
        self.slots = list(slots)
        self.dirty = False
        self.note = note
        self.inserted = inserted       # True = line added on insert (offset still unknown)
        self.jump_target = None        # for an INSERTED jump: nav-line index of the target
        self.orig = self._snapshot()

    def _snapshot(self):
        return (self.mnemonic, self.opcode, tuple(s.key() for s in self.slots))

    def matches_orig(self) -> bool:
        return self._snapshot() == self.orig

    def restore_orig(self):
        mn, op, slotkeys = self.orig
        self.mnemonic = mn
        self.opcode = op
        self.slots = [_Slot(t, v, r) for (t, v, r) in slotkeys]
        self.dirty = False

    def clone(self):
        c = _Line(self.nav, offset=self.offset, mnemonic=self.mnemonic,
                  opcode=self.opcode, slots=[s.clone() for s in self.slots],
                  note=self.note, inserted=self.inserted)
        c.dirty = self.dirty
        c.orig = self.orig
        c.jump_target = self.jump_target
        return c

    @property
    def n_tokens(self) -> int:
        return 1 + len(self.slots) if self.nav else 0

    @property
    def complete(self) -> bool:
        """True if every slot has a value (none cleared by an opcode change)."""
        return all(s.value is not None for s in self.slots)


def _op_value(op) -> object:
    t = op.type
    if t in (_T.Imm32, _T.Addr8, _T.Addr32):
        return op.i32
    if t == _T.Double:
        return op.f64
    return op.u32  # Reg*/UInt*/StringID(index)


def _build_lines(func, instrs, op_by_mn) -> list[_Line]:
    lines: list[_Line] = []
    for ins in instrs:
        desc = op_by_mn.get(ins.mnemonic)
        slots: list[_Slot] = []
        if desc is not None and len(desc.operands) == len(ins.operands):
            mask = desc.string_ref_mask
            for i, (ptype, op) in enumerate(zip(desc.operands, ins.operands)):
                slots.append(_Slot(ptype, _op_value(op), bool(mask & (1 << i))))
        else:
            # unknown or misaligned opcode: slots from the physical types seen by the disasm
            for op in ins.operands:
                slots.append(_Slot(op.type, _op_value(op), op.type == _T.StringID))
        lines.append(_Line(True, offset=ins.offset, mnemonic=ins.mnemonic,
                           opcode=ins.opcode, slots=slots))

    if not lines:
        lines.append(_Line(False, note="  (function with no bytecode)"))

    if func.hasExceptionHandler and func.exceptionHandlers:
        lines.append(_Line(False, note=""))
        lines.append(_Line(False, note="  Exception Handlers:"))
        for i, eh in enumerate(func.exceptionHandlers):
            lines.append(_Line(
                False,
                note=f"    [{i}]  try {eh.start:#06x}..{eh.end:#06x}"
                     f"  ->  catch @ {eh.target:#06x}",
            ))
    return lines


def _clone_lines(lines):
    return [ln.clone() for ln in lines]


class EditorState:
    def __init__(self, func, instrs, *, strings=None, opcodes=None, version=None):
        self.func = func
        self.version = version      # HBC version (for the encoder at commit time)
        self.commit = False         # outcome of the exit prompt: True = apply
        self.strings = list(strings) if strings is not None else []
        self.op_list = list(opcodes) if opcodes is not None else []
        self.op_by_mn = {d.mnemonic: d for d in self.op_list}
        self.by_sig: dict[tuple, list[str]] = {}
        for d in self.op_list:
            self.by_sig.setdefault(tuple(d.operands), []).append(d.mnemonic)
        for v in self.by_sig.values():
            v.sort()

        self.lines = _build_lines(func, instrs, self.op_by_mn)
        self.nav_indices = [i for i, ln in enumerate(self.lines) if ln.nav]
        self._orig_nav_count = len(self.nav_indices)   # to detect insert/delete
        self._orig_offsets = [self.lines[i].offset for i in self.nav_indices]  # snapshot
        self._insert_above = False
        # Shared bytecode - editing the bytes changes every function in the group.
        self.shared = bool(getattr(func, "shared", False))
        self.share_count = int(getattr(func, "shareCount", 1))
        self.edit_all = False   # answer to "apply to all?" (share_ask)
        self.ci = 0
        self.tok = 0
        self.top = 0
        mn_lens = [len(ln.mnemonic) for ln in self.lines if ln.nav]
        self.mn_width = min(20, max(mn_lens)) if mn_lens else 1

        self.mode = "nav"   # nav | edit_op | edit_mn | exit_ask | insert_pick | insert_target | share_ask
        self.edit_buf = ""
        self.edit_err = ""
        self.cand_all: list[str] = []
        self.cand_sel = 0

        self.undo: list = []
        self.redo: list = []
        self.quit_armed = False

    # --- current line / token ----------------------------------------------

    @property
    def cur_line_idx(self) -> int:
        return self.nav_indices[self.ci] if self.nav_indices else 0

    @property
    def cur_line(self):
        return self.lines[self.cur_line_idx] if self.nav_indices else None

    @property
    def cur_slot(self):
        ln = self.cur_line
        if ln and 1 <= self.tok <= len(ln.slots):
            return ln.slots[self.tok - 1]
        return None

    @property
    def dirty_count(self) -> int:
        return sum(1 for i in self.nav_indices if self.lines[i].dirty)

    # --- movement ----------------------------------------------------------

    def move_token(self, delta: int) -> None:
        ln = self.cur_line
        if ln:
            self.tok = max(0, min(ln.n_tokens - 1, self.tok + delta))

    def move_line(self, delta: int) -> None:
        if not self.nav_indices:
            return
        self.ci = max(0, min(len(self.nav_indices) - 1, self.ci + delta))
        self.tok = 0

    def move_line_to(self, ci: int) -> None:
        if not self.nav_indices:
            return
        self.ci = max(0, min(len(self.nav_indices) - 1, ci))
        self.tok = 0

    def ensure_visible(self, view_height: int) -> None:
        idx = self.cur_line_idx
        if idx < self.top:
            self.top = idx
        elif idx >= self.top + view_height:
            self.top = idx - view_height + 1
        self.top = max(0, min(self.top, max(0, len(self.lines) - view_height)))

    # --- undo / redo ---------------------------------------------------

    def _snapshot(self):
        return (_clone_lines(self.lines), self.ci, self.tok, self.top)

    def _restore(self, snap):
        lines, ci, tok, top = snap
        # IN-PLACE restore: keeps the identity of the list and of the _Line objects
        # (on a same-size edit the structure never changes - same count and same nav lines).
        if len(lines) == len(self.lines):
            for dst, src in zip(self.lines, lines):
                dst.nav, dst.offset = src.nav, src.offset
                dst.mnemonic, dst.opcode = src.mnemonic, src.opcode
                dst.slots = [s.clone() for s in src.slots]
                dst.dirty, dst.note, dst.orig = src.dirty, src.note, src.orig
                dst.inserted, dst.jump_target = src.inserted, src.jump_target
        else:
            self.lines = _clone_lines(lines)
        self.nav_indices = [i for i, ln in enumerate(self.lines) if ln.nav]
        self.ci = max(0, min(len(self.nav_indices) - 1, ci)) if self.nav_indices else 0
        self.tok = tok
        self.top = top
        ln = self.cur_line
        if ln:
            self.tok = max(0, min(ln.n_tokens - 1, self.tok))

    def push_undo(self):
        self.undo.append(self._snapshot())
        if len(self.undo) > 200:
            self.undo.pop(0)
        self.redo.clear()

    def undo_action(self):
        if not self.undo:
            return
        self.redo.append(self._snapshot())
        self._restore(self.undo.pop())
        self.quit_armed = False

    def redo_action(self):
        if not self.redo:
            return
        self.undo.append(self._snapshot())
        self._restore(self.redo.pop())
        self.quit_armed = False

    # --- edit mode -----------------------------------------------------

    def begin_edit(self):
        ln = self.cur_line
        if ln is None or not ln.slots and self.tok > 0:
            return
        # INSERTED jump, cursor on the Addr operand -> target selection (not typing a number)
        if ln.inserted and self.tok == 1 and self.is_jump_line(ln):
            self.begin_insert_target(ln)
            return
        self.edit_buf = ""
        self.edit_err = ""
        if self.tok == 0:
            if not self.op_by_mn:
                return
            self.cand_all = list(self.by_sig.get(tuple(s.type for s in ln.slots), []))
            if ln.mnemonic not in self.cand_all:
                self.cand_all.append(ln.mnemonic)
                self.cand_all.sort()
            try:
                self.cand_sel = self.cand_all.index(ln.mnemonic)
            except ValueError:
                self.cand_sel = 0
            self.mode = "edit_mn"
        else:
            self.mode = "edit_op"

    def cancel_edit(self):
        self.mode = "nav"
        self.edit_buf = ""
        self.edit_err = ""

    def filtered_candidates(self) -> list[str]:
        q = self.edit_buf.strip().lower()
        if not q:
            return self.cand_all
        pref = [m for m in self.cand_all if m.lower().startswith(q)]
        sub = [m for m in self.cand_all if q in m.lower() and m not in pref]
        return pref + sub

    def edit_type_char(self, ch: str):
        self.edit_buf += ch
        self.edit_err = ""
        if self.mode == "edit_mn":
            self.cand_sel = 0

    def edit_backspace(self):
        self.edit_buf = self.edit_buf[:-1]
        self.edit_err = ""
        if self.mode == "edit_mn":
            self.cand_sel = 0

    def edit_cycle(self, delta: int):
        cands = self.filtered_candidates()
        if cands:
            self.cand_sel = (self.cand_sel + delta) % len(cands)

    def commit_edit(self):
        if self.mode == "insert_pick":
            self.commit_insert()
            return
        if self.mode == "insert_target":
            self.set_insert_target()
            return
        ln = self.cur_line
        if ln is None:
            self.cancel_edit()
            return
        if self.mode == "edit_mn":
            self._commit_mnemonic(ln)
        elif self.mode == "edit_op":
            self._commit_operand(ln)

    def _commit_mnemonic(self, ln):
        cands = self.filtered_candidates()
        target = None
        buf = self.edit_buf.strip()
        if cands:
            target = cands[min(self.cand_sel, len(cands) - 1)]
        elif buf in self.op_by_mn and buf in self.cand_all:
            target = buf
        if target is None:
            self.edit_err = f"no opcode compatible with {buf!r}"
            return
        if target == ln.mnemonic:
            self.cancel_edit()
            return
        self.push_undo()
        ln.mnemonic = target
        ln.opcode = self.op_by_mn[target].opcode
        # opcode change -> operands need reconfirming: clear all slots
        # (the signature is identical, so the TYPES stay; only the values reset)
        for s in ln.slots:
            s.value = None
        ln.dirty = True
        self.tok = 1 if ln.slots else 0   # move the cursor to the first slot to fill in
        self.quit_armed = False
        self.cancel_edit()

    def _commit_operand(self, ln):
        slot = ln.slots[self.tok - 1]
        try:
            newval = _parse_operand(self.edit_buf, slot, self.strings)
        except _EditError as e:
            self.edit_err = str(e)
            return
        self.push_undo()
        slot.value = newval
        ln.dirty = not ln.matches_orig()
        self.quit_armed = False
        self.cancel_edit()

    def revert_line(self):
        ln = self.cur_line
        if ln is None or ln.matches_orig():
            return
        self.push_undo()
        ln.restore_orig()
        self.quit_armed = False

    # --- line insertion / deletion -----------------------------

    @property
    def structural_change(self) -> bool:
        """True if the instruction count changed (insert/delete) or there are
        inserted lines - requires the structural serialization path
        (`Module`), not the same-size patch."""
        return (len(self.nav_indices) != self._orig_nav_count
                or any(self.lines[i].inserted for i in self.nav_indices))

    def delete_line(self):
        """Delete the current instruction from the buffer. No check here -
        if the deletion breaks a jump or a handler, the error surfaces at commit."""
        if not self.nav_indices or len(self.nav_indices) < 2:
            self.edit_err = "you can't delete the function's last instruction"
            return
        self.push_undo()
        del self.lines[self.cur_line_idx]
        self.nav_indices = [i for i, ln in enumerate(self.lines) if ln.nav]
        self.ci = min(self.ci, len(self.nav_indices) - 1)
        self.tok = 0
        self.quit_armed = False

    def begin_insert(self, above: bool):
        if not self.op_by_mn:
            return
        self._insert_above = above
        self.edit_buf = ""
        self.edit_err = ""
        self.cand_all = sorted(self.op_by_mn)
        self.cand_sel = 0
        self.mode = "insert_pick"

    def commit_insert(self):
        cands = self.filtered_candidates()
        buf = self.edit_buf.strip()
        target = cands[min(self.cand_sel, len(cands) - 1)] if cands else (
            buf if buf in self.op_by_mn else None)
        if target is None:
            self.edit_err = f"unknown opcode: {buf!r}"
            return
        desc = self.op_by_mn[target]
        if target == "SwitchImm":
            self.edit_err = "SwitchImm cannot be inserted (attached jump table)"
            return
        if target.startswith("SaveGenerator"):
            self.edit_err = "generator opcodes are not supported"
            return

        self.push_undo()
        mask = desc.string_ref_mask
        slots = [_Slot(t, None, bool(mask & (1 << i))) for i, t in enumerate(desc.operands)]
        ln = _Line(True, offset=None, mnemonic=target, opcode=desc.opcode,
                   slots=slots, inserted=True)
        ln.dirty = True

        at = self.cur_line_idx if self._insert_above else self.cur_line_idx + 1
        self.lines.insert(at, ln)
        self.nav_indices = [i for i, x in enumerate(self.lines) if x.nav]
        self.ci = self.nav_indices.index(at)
        self.tok = 1 if slots else 0
        self.quit_armed = False
        self.cancel_edit()

    def is_jump_line(self, ln) -> bool:
        d = self.op_by_mn.get(ln.mnemonic)
        return bool(d) and d.jump_kind in ("Unconditional", "Conditional")

    def begin_insert_target(self, ln):
        """Target-selection mode for an INSERTED jump: the cursor moves
        freely, Enter sets the current line as the destination."""
        self._target_line = ln
        self.mode = "insert_target"
        self.edit_err = ""

    def set_insert_target(self):
        ln = getattr(self, "_target_line", None)
        if ln is None or not ln.slots:
            self.cancel_edit()
            return
        self.push_undo()
        ln.jump_target = self.ci        # index in nav_indices of the destination line
        ln.slots[0].value = 0           # placeholder: the assembler computes the displacement
        self._target_line = None
        self.cancel_edit()


class _EditError(Exception):
    pass


def _parse_operand(raw: str, slot: _Slot, strings: list) -> object:
    s = raw.strip()
    if not s:
        raise _EditError("empty value")
    t = slot.type

    if t == _T.Double:
        try:
            return float(s)
        except ValueError:
            raise _EditError("not a number")

    if t in (_T.Reg8, _T.Reg32) and s[:1] in ("r", "R"):
        s = s[1:]
    try:
        n = int(s, 0)
    except ValueError:
        raise _EditError("not an integer (use decimal or 0x…)")

    if slot.is_str_ref:
        if not strings:
            raise _EditError("string table not available")
        if not (0 <= n < len(strings)):
            raise _EditError(f"string index out of range (0–{len(strings) - 1})")
        width_max = {_T.UInt8: 0xFF, _T.UInt16: 0xFFFF}.get(t, 0xFFFFFFFF)
        if n > width_max:
            raise _EditError(f"index doesn't fit in {_OP_KIND_NAME.get(t, t)} (same-size edit doesn't widen)")
        return n

    rng = _INT_RANGE.get(t)
    if rng and not (rng[0] <= n <= rng[1]):
        raise _EditError(f"out of range for {_OP_KIND_NAME.get(t, t)} ({rng[0]}–{rng[1]})")
    return n


# Commit buffer -> bytes

def encode_committed_lines(state: "EditorState") -> dict[int, bytes]:
    """Re-encodes the modified lines, keyed by ABSOLUTE file offset
    (`func.offset + line.offset`). Each result must have exactly the length of
    the original instruction.

    Raises `ValueError` for an unknown opcode, `SwitchImm` (its jump table
    isn't relocated), empty slots, or an encoded length different from the original."""
    if state.version is None:
        raise ValueError("HBC version unknown to the editor - cannot encode")

    base = state.func.offset
    out: dict[int, bytes] = {}
    for i in state.nav_indices:
        ln = state.lines[i]
        if not ln.dirty:
            continue
        if not ln.complete:
            raise ValueError(
                f"line @{ln.offset:#06x} incomplete - fill it in or press R to restore it")

        desc = state.op_by_mn.get(ln.mnemonic)
        if desc is None:
            raise ValueError(f"line @{ln.offset:#06x}: unknown opcode {ln.mnemonic!r}")
        if desc.jump_kind == "Switch":
            raise ValueError(
                f"line @{ln.offset:#06x}: editing SwitchImm is not supported "
                f"(the attached jump table is not relocated)")

        orig_types = [t for (t, _v, _r) in ln.orig[2]]
        expected = 1 + sum(_libhbc.operand_size(t) for t in orig_types)

        enc = _libhbc.encode_instruction(
            state.version, ln.opcode, [s.value for s in ln.slots])

        if len(enc) != expected:
            raise ValueError(
                f"line @{ln.offset:#06x}: encoded {len(enc)} B ≠ expected {expected} B "
                f"- the edit is not same-size")

        out[base + ln.offset] = enc
    return out


# Structural commit -> Module (insert / delete)

_REG_TYPES = (_T.Reg8, _T.Reg32)


def assemble_committed_function(state: "EditorState"):
    """The buffer (inserts and deletes included) as the AsmInstr list for
    `Module.set_function_body`: `(func_idx, asm_instrs, frame_size, warnings, edit_all)`,
    where `warnings` are non-blocking.

    Raises `ValueError` for incomplete lines, unknown opcodes, SwitchImm, an
    inserted jump with no target, the target of a deleted jump, a deleted
    exception handler boundary, or a frameSize bump on a function with an
    exception handler."""
    if state.version is None:
        raise ValueError("HBC version unknown to the editor")

    nav = [state.lines[i] for i in state.nav_indices]
    warnings: list[str] = []

    # ORIGINAL byte offset -> index in nav, to resolve existing jump targets.
    byte_to_idx = {ln.offset: k for k, ln in enumerate(nav) if ln.offset is not None}

    # A deleted instruction must not be an exception handler boundary.
    if state.func.hasExceptionHandler:
        surviving = set(byte_to_idx)
        deleted = {o for o in state._orig_offsets if o is not None} - surviving
        if deleted:
            eh_bounds: set[int] = set()
            for e in state.func.exceptionHandlers:
                eh_bounds |= {e.start, e.end, e.target}
            bad = sorted(deleted & eh_bounds)
            if bad:
                raise ValueError(
                    "deleted an instruction that is an exception handler boundary "
                    f"(offset {[hex(b) for b in bad]}) - move the try/catch first")

    max_reg = -1
    asm = []
    for k, ln in enumerate(nav):
        if not ln.complete:
            raise ValueError(f"line {k}: incomplete instruction - fill it in or cancel")
        desc = state.op_by_mn.get(ln.mnemonic)
        if desc is None:
            raise ValueError(f"line {k}: unknown opcode {ln.mnemonic!r}")
        if desc.jump_kind == "Switch":
            raise ValueError(f"line {k}: SwitchImm not supported")

        operands = [float(s.value) for s in ln.slots]

        jt, ap = -1, -1
        if desc.jump_kind in ("Unconditional", "Conditional"):
            ap = 0
            if ln.inserted:
                if ln.jump_target is None:
                    raise ValueError(f"line {k}: inserted jump has no target (press Enter on the Addr operand)")
                jt = int(ln.jump_target)
            else:
                orig_addr = ln.orig[2][0][1]        # original displacement
                tgt_byte = ln.offset + int(orig_addr)
                if tgt_byte not in byte_to_idx:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"line {k}: the jump target ({tgt_byte:#x}) was "
                        f"deleted or is no longer aligned to an instruction")
                jt = byte_to_idx[tgt_byte]

        for s in ln.slots:
            if s.type in _REG_TYPES and s.value is not None:
                max_reg = max(max_reg, int(s.value))

        asm.append((ln.opcode, operands, jt, ap,
                    -1 if ln.offset is None else int(ln.offset)))

    frame_size = max(state.func.frameSize, max_reg + 1)
    if frame_size > 127 and not getattr(state.func, "overflowed", False):
        raise ValueError(f"frameSize {frame_size} > 127 (7-bit field) - "
                         f"the function would need to become overflowed (not supported)")
    if frame_size > state.func.frameSize and state.func.hasExceptionHandler:
        raise ValueError(
            "the inserted instruction would use a new register, but the function has "
            "an exception handler - use only registers < {} (frameSize bump is not "
            "safe with EH)".format(state.func.frameSize))

    # soft warning: the last instruction is not a terminator
    if nav:
        last = state.op_by_mn.get(nav[-1].mnemonic)
        if last is not None and last.jump_kind not in ("Return", "Throw"):
            warnings.append(
                f"the last instruction ({nav[-1].mnemonic}) is not Ret/Throw - "
                f"the function might execute past the end of the bytecode")

    return state.func.index, asm, frame_size, warnings, bool(getattr(state, "edit_all", False))


# Rendering

def _slot_text(slot: _Slot, strings: list) -> str:
    t, v = slot.type, slot.value
    if v is None:
        return f"⟨{_OP_KIND_NAME.get(t, '?')}⟩"   # ⟨Reg8⟩ - slot to fill in
    if slot.is_str_ref:
        if 0 <= v < len(strings):
            sv = strip_kind_suffix(str(strings[v]))
            sv = sv.replace("\n", "\\n").replace("\r", "\\r").replace("\t", "\\t")
            if len(sv) > 30:
                sv = sv[:27] + "..."
            return f'"{sv}"'
        return f"#{v}"
    if t in (_T.Reg8, _T.Reg32):
        return f"r{v}"
    if t == _T.Double:
        return fmt_num(v)
    if t in (_T.Addr8, _T.Addr32):
        return f"{'+' if v >= 0 else ''}{v}"
    return str(v)


def _tok_style(slot: _Slot | None, is_mn: bool) -> str:
    if is_mn:
        return MNEMONIC_STYLE
    return _OP_STYLE.get(slot.type, "") if slot else ""


def _line_fragments(state: "EditorState", line: _Line, is_cursor: bool):
    if not line.nav:
        return [(INFO_STYLE, line.note)]

    incomplete = not line.complete
    if incomplete:
        mark, mark_style = "!", INCOMPLETE_MARK_STYLE
    elif line.inserted:
        mark, mark_style = "+", DIRTY_MARK_STYLE
    elif line.dirty:
        mark, mark_style = "*", DIRTY_MARK_STYLE
    else:
        mark, mark_style = " ", GUTTER_STYLE
    off_txt = "??????" if line.offset is None else f"{line.offset:#06x}"
    frags = [(mark_style, mark), (GUTTER_STYLE, f"{off_txt}  ")]

    n_tokens = 1 + len(line.slots)
    for i in range(n_tokens):
        if i == 1:
            pad = max(1, state.mn_width - len(line.mnemonic)) + 1
            frags.append(("", " " * pad))
        elif i >= 2:
            frags.append(("", ", "))
        if i == 0:
            text, base = line.mnemonic, MNEMONIC_STYLE
        else:
            slot = line.slots[i - 1]
            text = _slot_text(slot, state.strings)
            base = EMPTY_STYLE if slot.value is None else _tok_style(slot, False)
        style = CURSOR_STYLE if (is_cursor and i == state.tok) else base
        frags.append((style, text))
    return frags


# edit func:new builds a NEW function in this same editor, from a stand-in
# FunctionInfo and two seed instructions. Its fixed metadata (paramCount 1,
# functionName 0, strict, callable and constructible) is set in C++
# (`Module::add_function`).

def new_function_stub():
    """`FunctionInfo`-like stand-in for `edit func:new`: the function isn't in
    `hbc.functions()` yet. `index=-1` is a sentinel, never used as an index
    (the REPL calls `apply_add_function`)."""
    return SimpleNamespace(
        index=-1, name="<new function>", frameSize=1,
        hasExceptionHandler=False, exceptionHandlers=[],
        shared=False, shareCount=1, overflowed=False,
    )


def new_function_seed_instrs(opcodes):
    """Seed body `LoadConstUndefined r0` / `Ret r0` (returns `undefined`),
    duck-typed as `hbc.Instruction`/`Operand` with the fields `_build_lines` reads."""
    op_by_mn = {d.mnemonic: d for d in opcodes}
    lcu = op_by_mn["LoadConstUndefined"]
    ret = op_by_mn["Ret"]
    reg0 = SimpleNamespace(type=_T.Reg8, u32=0, i32=0, f64=0.0)
    return [
        SimpleNamespace(offset=0, mnemonic="LoadConstUndefined", opcode=lcu.opcode, operands=[reg0]),
        SimpleNamespace(offset=2, mnemonic="Ret",                opcode=ret.opcode, operands=[reg0]),
    ]


def run_editor(func, instrs, *, strings=None, opcodes=None, version=None,
               _input=None, _output=None, _state=None) -> "EditorState":
    """Full-screen editor for a function; returns the state on exit.
    `strings` resolve and validate StringID operands, `opcodes` is
    `_libhbc.opcode_table(version)`, `version` is needed to encode at commit.
    `_input/_output/_state` are for headless tests."""
    state = _state if _state is not None else EditorState(
        func, instrs, strings=strings, opcodes=opcodes, version=version)

    def _title():
        d = state.dirty_count
        inc = sum(1 for i in state.nav_indices if not state.lines[i].complete)
        ins = sum(1 for i in state.nav_indices if state.lines[i].inserted)
        deleted = state._orig_nav_count - (len(state.nav_indices) - ins)
        dtxt = f"   {d} modified" if d else ""
        itxt = f"   {inc} incomplete" if inc else ""
        ntxt = f"   +{ins} inserted" if ins else ""
        xtxt = f"   -{deleted} deleted" if deleted > 0 else ""
        stxt = f"   ⚠ shared ×{state.share_count}" if state.shared else ""
        otxt = "   overflow" if getattr(func, "overflowed", False) else ""
        return [(
            "bold" if not inc else ERR_STYLE,
            f" hermit edit - func[{func.index}] {func.name}   "
            f"{len(state.nav_indices)} instr   {func.frameSize} regs{otxt}{stxt}   "
            f"EDIT{dtxt}{ntxt}{xtxt}{itxt} ",
        )]

    def _body():
        vh = view_height()
        state.ensure_visible(vh)
        out = []
        for off, line in enumerate(state.lines[state.top: state.top + vh]):
            real = state.top + off
            is_cursor = line.nav and real == state.cur_line_idx
            out.extend(_line_fragments(state, line, is_cursor))
            out.append(("", "\n"))
        if out and out[-1] == ("", "\n"):
            out.pop()
        return out

    def _status():
        ln = state.cur_line
        if ln is None:
            return [(CURSOR_STYLE, " (no instruction) ")]
        if state.tok == 0:
            kind, raw = "mnemonic", f"opcode {ln.opcode:#04x}"
        else:
            slot = ln.slots[state.tok - 1]
            kind = _OP_KIND_NAME.get(slot.type, "?")
            if ln.inserted and state.tok == 1 and state.is_jump_line(ln):
                if ln.jump_target is None:
                    raw = "⟨target not chosen - Enter, then ↑↓ and Enter on the destination⟩"
                else:
                    dst = state.lines[state.nav_indices[ln.jump_target]]
                    raw = f"-> line {ln.jump_target} ({dst.mnemonic})"
            elif slot.value is None:
                raw = "⟨empty - Enter to fill in⟩"
            elif slot.is_str_ref:
                sv = state.strings[slot.value] if 0 <= slot.value < len(state.strings) else "?"
                raw = f"#{slot.value}  {strip_kind_suffix(str(sv))!r}"
            elif slot.type in (_T.Addr8, _T.Addr32):
                tgt = "?" if ln.offset is None else f"{ln.offset + slot.value:#06x}"
                raw = f"{slot.value:+d}  -> {tgt}"
            else:
                raw = fmt_num(slot.value) if slot.type == _T.Double else str(slot.value)
        dtag = "  [inserted]" if ln.inserted else ("  [dirty]" if ln.dirty else "")
        off_txt = "??????" if ln.offset is None else f"{ln.offset:#06x}"
        return [(
            CURSOR_STYLE,
            f" line {state.ci + 1}/{len(state.nav_indices)}   off {off_txt}   "
            f"token {state.tok}: {kind} = {raw}{dtag} ",
        )]

    def _bar1():
        if state.mode == "insert_pick":
            return [(HINT_STYLE, f" insert {'above' if state._insert_above else 'below'} "),
                    ("", state.edit_buf), ("bold", "▁"),
                    (HINT_STYLE, "   Tab cycles · Enter · Esc")]
        if state.mode == "insert_target":
            return [(DIRTY_MARK_STYLE, " choose the jump destination "),
                    (HINT_STYLE, "  ↑↓ move · Enter confirms · Esc cancels")]
        if state.mode == "share_ask":
            return [(INCOMPLETE_MARK_STYLE,
                     f" ⚠ this code is shared by {state.share_count} functions - "
                     f"apply the change to ALL of them? "),
                    ("bold", " Y "), (HINT_STYLE, "yes   "),
                    ("bold", " N/Esc "), (HINT_STYLE, "cancel (private clone not supported) ")]
        if state.mode == "exit_ask":
            d = state.dirty_count
            ins = sum(1 for i in state.nav_indices if state.lines[i].inserted)
            deleted = state._orig_nav_count - (len(state.nav_indices) - ins)
            parts = []
            if d:       parts.append(f"{d} modified")
            if ins:     parts.append(f"{ins} inserted")
            if deleted > 0: parts.append(f"{deleted} deleted")
            summary = ", ".join(parts) or "changes"
            return [(DIRTY_MARK_STYLE, f" {summary} - apply to the in-memory file? "),
                    ("bold", " Y "), (HINT_STYLE, "apply and exit   "),
                    ("bold", " N "), (HINT_STYLE, "discard and exit   "),
                    ("bold", " Esc "), (HINT_STYLE, "cancel ")]
        if state.mode == "edit_mn":
            ln = state.cur_line
            sig = ",".join(_OP_KIND_NAME.get(s.type, "?") for s in ln.slots) or "-"
            return [(HINT_STYLE, " opcode "), ("", f"{state.edit_buf}"),
                    ("bold", "\u2581"), (HINT_STYLE, f"   [signature {sig}]")]
        if state.mode == "edit_op":
            slot = state.cur_slot
            kind = _OP_KIND_NAME.get(slot.type, "?") if slot else "?"
            old = _slot_text(slot, state.strings) if slot else ""
            return [(HINT_STYLE, f" edit {kind} (was {old}) "),
                    ("", state.edit_buf), ("bold", "\u2581")]
        return [(HINT_STYLE,
                 " <-> token   ↑↓ line   Enter edit   o/O insert   "
                 "^K delete   ^Z/^R undo   R restore   ^X save/exit ")]

    def _bar2():
        if state.edit_err:
            return [(ERR_STYLE, "  " + state.edit_err)]
        if state.mode == "insert_target":
            return [(HINT_STYLE, "  the assembler computes the displacement at commit time")]
        if state.mode == "exit_ask":
            return [(HINT_STYLE,
                     "  Y re-encodes the changes, applies them to the in-memory image "
                     "(with an integrity check) · the .hbc on disk is written by `patch`")]
        if state.mode in ("edit_mn", "insert_pick"):
            cands = state.filtered_candidates()
            if not cands:
                return [(HINT_STYLE, "  (no compatible opcode)")]
            frags = [(HINT_STYLE, "  ")]
            for i, m in enumerate(cands[:10]):
                if i:
                    frags.append((HINT_STYLE, "  "))
                frags.append((SEL_STYLE if i == state.cand_sel else "", m))
            if len(cands) > 10:
                frags.append((HINT_STYLE, f"   +{len(cands) - 10}"))
            frags.append((HINT_STYLE, "   Tab cycles · Enter confirms · Esc cancels"))
            return frags
        if state.mode == "edit_op":
            slot = state.cur_slot
            hint = ""
            if slot:
                if slot.is_str_ref:
                    hint = f"index 0–{max(0, len(state.strings) - 1)}"
                elif slot.type in _INT_RANGE:
                    lo, hi = _INT_RANGE[slot.type]
                    hint = f"{lo}–{hi}"
                elif slot.type == _T.Double:
                    hint = "number"
            return [(HINT_STYLE, f"  {hint}   Enter confirms · Esc cancels")]
        return [("", "")]

    # --- key bindings --------------------------------------------------

    kb = KeyBindings()
    in_nav = Condition(lambda: state.mode == "nav")
    in_type = Condition(lambda: state.mode in ("edit_op", "edit_mn", "insert_pick"))
    in_pick = Condition(lambda: state.mode in ("edit_mn", "insert_pick"))
    in_target = Condition(lambda: state.mode == "insert_target")
    in_editing = Condition(lambda: state.mode in
                           ("edit_op", "edit_mn", "insert_pick", "insert_target"))
    in_exit = Condition(lambda: state.mode == "exit_ask")
    in_share = Condition(lambda: state.mode == "share_ask")

    def _request_exit(event):
        # Clean buffer: exit at once. Otherwise ask Y/N. `structural_change`
        # covers deletions, which don't count in dirty_count.
        if state.dirty_count == 0 and not state.structural_change:
            event.app.exit()
            return
        incomplete = [i for i in state.nav_indices if not state.lines[i].complete]
        if incomplete:
            state.edit_err = (f"{len(incomplete)} incomplete lines (!) - fill them in "
                              f"or press R to restore them before exiting")
            event.app.invalidate()
            return
        state.edit_err = ""
        # Shared bytecode -> ask first whether to apply to all functions.
        if state.shared and not state.edit_all:
            state.mode = "share_ask"
        else:
            state.mode = "exit_ask"
        event.app.invalidate()

    @kb.add("q", filter=in_nav)
    @kb.add("c-x", filter=in_nav)
    def _q(event):
        _request_exit(event)

    @kb.add("y", filter=in_share)
    @kb.add("Y", filter=in_share)
    def _share_yes(event):
        state.edit_all = True
        state.mode = "exit_ask"
        event.app.invalidate()

    @kb.add("n", filter=in_share)
    @kb.add("N", filter=in_share)
    @kb.add("escape", filter=in_share)
    def _share_no(event):
        state.edit_all = False
        state.mode = "nav"
        state.edit_err = ("shared code: without «apply to all» the change "
                          "cannot be saved (private clone not supported)")
        event.app.invalidate()

    bind_exit_prompt(kb, state, in_exit, cancel_mode="nav")
    bind_abort(kb, state)

    @kb.add("left", filter=in_nav)
    def _left(event):
        state.move_token(-1); event.app.invalidate()

    @kb.add("right", filter=in_nav)
    def _right(event):
        state.move_token(+1); event.app.invalidate()

    @kb.add("up", filter=in_nav)
    def _up(event):
        state.move_line(-1); event.app.invalidate()

    @kb.add("down", filter=in_nav)
    def _down(event):
        state.move_line(+1); event.app.invalidate()

    @kb.add("pageup", filter=in_nav)
    def _pgup(event):
        state.move_line(-view_height()); event.app.invalidate()

    @kb.add("pagedown", filter=in_nav)
    def _pgdn(event):
        state.move_line(+view_height()); event.app.invalidate()

    @kb.add("home", filter=in_nav)
    @kb.add("g", filter=in_nav)
    def _home(event):
        state.move_line_to(0); state.top = 0; event.app.invalidate()

    @kb.add("end", filter=in_nav)
    @kb.add("G", filter=in_nav)
    def _end(event):
        state.move_line_to(len(state.nav_indices) - 1); event.app.invalidate()

    @kb.add("enter", filter=in_nav)
    def _open_edit(event):
        state.begin_edit(); event.app.invalidate()

    @kb.add("o", filter=in_nav)
    def _ins_below(event):
        state.begin_insert(above=False); event.app.invalidate()

    @kb.add("O", filter=in_nav)
    def _ins_above(event):
        state.begin_insert(above=True); event.app.invalidate()

    @kb.add("c-k", filter=in_nav)
    def _del_line(event):
        state.delete_line(); event.app.invalidate()

    @kb.add("R", filter=in_nav)
    def _revert(event):
        state.revert_line(); event.app.invalidate()

    @kb.add("c-z", filter=in_nav)
    def _undo(event):
        state.undo_action(); event.app.invalidate()

    @kb.add("c-r", filter=in_nav)
    def _redo(event):
        state.redo_action(); event.app.invalidate()

    # --- edit / insert modes ---
    @kb.add("escape", filter=in_editing)
    def _esc(event):
        state.cancel_edit(); event.app.invalidate()

    @kb.add("enter", filter=in_editing)
    def _commit(event):
        state.commit_edit(); event.app.invalidate()

    @kb.add("backspace", filter=in_type)
    def _bs(event):
        state.edit_backspace(); event.app.invalidate()

    @kb.add("tab", filter=in_pick)
    def _tab(event):
        state.edit_cycle(+1); event.app.invalidate()

    @kb.add("s-tab", filter=in_pick)
    def _stab(event):
        state.edit_cycle(-1); event.app.invalidate()

    @kb.add("<any>", filter=in_type)
    def _typed(event):
        if event.data and event.data.isprintable():
            state.edit_type_char(event.data)
            event.app.invalidate()

    # --- insert_target: free cursor to choose the jump destination ---
    @kb.add("up", filter=in_target)
    def _t_up(event):
        state.move_line(-1); event.app.invalidate()

    @kb.add("down", filter=in_target)
    def _t_down(event):
        state.move_line(+1); event.app.invalidate()

    run_screen(_title, _body, _status, _bar1, _bar2, kb, _input=_input, _output=_output)
    return state
```

`cli/editor/strings.py`:

```py
"""String editor (`edit string:<idx|value|new>`).

A line editor over one string. The new value is validated against the entry's
encoding (ASCII on 8-bit entries, BMP on UTF-16 ones). Its length is free: the
REPL picks the commit path, an in-place overwrite for an unshared same-length
value, otherwise a relocation (`Module.set_string_value`) that re-points the
entry. `edit string:new` and Ctrl+N switch to "new string" mode, committed with
`Module.add_string`. Identifiers are refused by the REPL (they need Hermes's
hash).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from prompt_toolkit.filters import Condition
from prompt_toolkit.formatted_text import ANSI
from prompt_toolkit.key_binding import KeyBindings

import _libhbc
from cli import display
from cli.editor.common import (
    CURSOR_STYLE, ERR_STYLE, HINT_STYLE, TextBufferMixin,
    apply_discard_cancel_bar, bind_abort, bind_exit_prompt, bind_text_input, input_bar,
    run_screen, view_height,
)


class _StrEditError(Exception):
    pass


def _encode_for_entry(value: str, entry, *, same_length: bool) -> bytes:
    """`value` encoded for `entry`: ASCII on an 8-bit entry, UTF-16LE (BMP
    only) on a UTF-16 one. With `same_length` the byte length must also match
    the entry's."""
    if value == "":
        raise _StrEditError(
            "empty value - the same-length edit does not delete the string "
            "(length change needs relocation)" if same_length
            else "empty value - the relocation path does not delete the string")

    if getattr(entry, "is_utf16", False):
        for ch in value:
            cp = ord(ch)
            if 0xD800 <= cp <= 0xDFFF:
                raise _StrEditError(
                    "isolated surrogate not allowed (BMP only on same-length edits)"
                    if same_length else "isolated surrogate not allowed (BMP only)")
            if cp > 0xFFFF:
                raise _StrEditError(
                    f"code point U+{cp:04X} outside the BMP (non-BMP / UTF-16 4B needs relocation)"
                    if same_length
                    else f"code point U+{cp:04X} outside the BMP (non-BMP not yet supported)")
        enc = value.encode("utf-16-le")
    else:
        try:
            enc = value.encode("ascii")
        except UnicodeEncodeError:
            raise _StrEditError(
                "non-ASCII character on an 8-bit entry - CESU-8 deferred to the relocation path"
                if same_length
                else "non-ASCII character on an 8-bit entry - CESU-8 not yet supported")

    if same_length and len(enc) != entry.byte_length:
        raise _StrEditError(
            f"{len(enc)} bytes ≠ {entry.byte_length} original bytes "
            f"(length change needs relocation)")
    return enc


def encode_string_value(value: str, entry) -> bytes:
    """Same-length edit: `value` encoded for `entry` (`_libhbc.StringEntry`, or
    anything with `.is_utf16` / `.byte_length`), with the original byte length."""
    return _encode_for_entry(value, entry, same_length=True)


def encode_string_new_value(value: str, entry) -> bytes:
    """Relocation path: same encoding as `encode_string_value`, any length."""
    return _encode_for_entry(value, entry, same_length=False)


def encode_string_commit(state: "StringEditState") -> dict:
    """`{absolute_storage_offset: bytes}` for the edited string, `{}` if
    unchanged. Re-validates Identifier, encoding and length."""
    if state.value == state.original:
        return {}
    if state.kind == _libhbc.StringKind.Identifier:
        raise _StrEditError(
            "Identifier string: editing not allowed (Identifier Hash Table)")
    return {state.entry.storage_offset: encode_string_value(state.value, state.entry)}


def encode_string_relocation_commit(state: "StringEditState") -> bytes | None:
    """Relocation path: the encoded bytes, or None if the value is unchanged.
    Choosing between patch and relocation is up to `cli/repl.py._edit_string`,
    which knows `is_shared`."""
    if state.value == state.original:
        return None
    if state.kind == _libhbc.StringKind.Identifier:
        raise _StrEditError(
            "Identifier string: editing not allowed (Identifier Hash Table)")
    return encode_string_new_value(state.value, state.entry)


def encode_new_string(value: str) -> bytes:
    """Encoder for `add_string`: kind String, ASCII only, non-empty, any length."""
    if value == "":
        raise _StrEditError("empty string - nothing to add")
    try:
        return value.encode("ascii")
    except UnicodeEncodeError:
        raise _StrEditError(
            "non-ASCII character - CESU-8 / UTF-16 encoder for new strings "
            "not yet supported")


class StringEditState(TextBufferMixin):
    """State of the string editor. Opens in edit mode.

    `is_add`: "new string" mode, with no entry and an empty buffer. Ctrl+N
    switches to it from an existing string (Esc comes back).
    `is_shared` / `shared_with`: the entry shares storage with other entries
    (their indices). It still opens, with a banner: editing detaches it from
    the group (the REPL commits through `apply_string_relocation`)."""

    def __init__(self, str_idx, strings, kinds, entries, xrefs, funcs,
                 *, context_bytes=b"", context_base=0, is_add=False,
                 is_shared=False, shared_with=()):
        self.str_idx = str_idx
        self.is_add = bool(is_add)
        self.is_shared = bool(is_shared)
        self.shared_with = list(shared_with)
        if self.is_add:
            self.original = ""
            self.entry = None
            self.kind = _libhbc.StringKind.String
            self.xrefs = []
            self.funcs = []
            self.context_bytes = b""
            self.context_base = 0
            self.highlight = None
        else:
            self.original = str(strings[str_idx]) if str_idx < len(strings) else ""
            self.entry = entries[str_idx]
            self.kind = kinds[str_idx] if str_idx < len(kinds) else None
            self.xrefs = list(xrefs)
            self.funcs = list(funcs)
            self.context_bytes = bytes(context_bytes)
            self.context_base = int(context_base)
            off = self.entry.storage_offset
            self.highlight = (off, off + self.entry.byte_length)

        self.value = self.original          # last confirmed value (commit_buf)
        self.buf = self.value               # text line being edited
        self.cur = len(self.buf)
        self.mode = "edit"                  # edit | exit_ask
        self.commit = False
        self.edit_err = ""

        self.top = 0
        self._max_top = 0

        self._prev = None                   # snapshot to return from add-mode (Ctrl+N -> Esc)

    def switch_to_add(self):
        """Switches to "new string": saves the current state for `Esc`."""
        if self.is_add:
            return
        self._prev = (self.original, self.value, self.buf, self.cur, self.entry,
                      self.kind, self.xrefs, self.funcs, self.context_bytes,
                      self.context_base, self.highlight, self.is_shared,
                      self.shared_with)
        self.is_add = True
        self.original = ""
        self.value = ""
        self.buf = ""
        self.cur = 0
        self.entry = None
        self.kind = _libhbc.StringKind.String
        self.xrefs = []
        self.funcs = []
        self.context_bytes = b""
        self.context_base = 0
        self.highlight = None
        self.is_shared = False
        self.shared_with = []
        self.edit_err = ""

    def _switch_back(self) -> bool:
        if not self._prev:
            return False
        (self.original, self.value, self.buf, self.cur, self.entry, self.kind,
         self.xrefs, self.funcs, self.context_bytes, self.context_base,
         self.highlight, self.is_shared, self.shared_with) = self._prev
        self._prev = None
        self.is_add = False
        self.edit_err = ""
        return True

    @property
    def modified(self) -> bool:
        return self.value != self.original

    @property
    def byte_length(self) -> int:
        if self.entry is None:
            return len(self.value.encode("ascii", errors="replace"))
        return self.entry.byte_length

    @property
    def char_length(self) -> int:
        if self.entry is None:
            return len(self.value)
        return self.entry.char_length

    @property
    def is_utf16(self) -> bool:
        return bool(self.entry.is_utf16) if self.entry is not None else False

    def commit_buf(self) -> bool:
        """Validates `buf` (`encode_new_string` in add mode, else
        `encode_string_new_value`). On success `value = buf`; on error sets `edit_err`."""
        try:
            if self.is_add:
                encode_new_string(self.buf)
            else:
                encode_string_new_value(self.buf, self.entry)
        except _StrEditError as ex:
            self.edit_err = str(ex)
            return False
        self.value = self.buf
        self.edit_err = ""
        return True

    def reset_buf(self):
        """Esc: leaves add mode if it was entered with Ctrl+N, else restores the original."""
        if self.is_add and self._switch_back():
            return
        self.buf = self.original
        self.cur = len(self.buf)
        self.value = self.original
        self.edit_err = ""

    def scroll(self, delta: int):
        self.top = max(0, min(self._max_top, self.top + delta))

    def buf_byte_len(self):
        try:
            if self.is_utf16:
                return len(self.buf.encode("utf-16-le"))
            return len(self.buf.encode("ascii"))
        except UnicodeEncodeError:
            return None

    def buf_ok(self) -> bool:
        try:
            if self.is_add:
                encode_new_string(self.buf)
            else:
                encode_string_new_value(self.buf, self.entry)
            return True
        except _StrEditError:
            return False

    def request_exit(self, event):
        # An unchanged buffer always exits, even if `original` can't be
        # re-encoded (e.g. real CESU-8): nothing to save.
        if self.buf == self.original:
            self.value = self.original
            self.commit = False
            event.app.exit()
            return
        if not self.commit_buf():
            event.app.invalidate()
            return
        if self.value == self.original:
            self.commit = False
            event.app.exit()
            return
        self.mode = "exit_ask"
        event.app.invalidate()



def run_string_editor(str_idx=0, strings=(), kinds=(), entries=(), xrefs=(),
                      funcs=(), *, context_bytes=b"", context_base=0, add=False,
                      is_shared=False, shared_with=(),
                      _input=None, _output=None, _state=None) -> "StringEditState":
    """Full-screen string editor; returns the state on exit. `add=True` opens
    "new string" mode. `_input/_output/_state` are for headless tests."""
    state = _state if _state is not None else StringEditState(
        str_idx, strings, kinds, entries, xrefs, funcs,
        context_bytes=context_bytes, context_base=context_base, is_add=add,
        is_shared=is_shared, shared_with=shared_with)

    def _title():
        if state.is_add:
            return [("bold",
                     f" hermit - new string   {state.char_length} char / "
                     f"{state.byte_length} B   kind String   8-bit ASCII ")]
        o = display.ellipsize(display.escape_ws(state.original), 40)
        return [(
            "bold",
            f' hermit edit string - [{state.str_idx}] "{o}"   '
            f"{state.char_length} char / {state.byte_length} B   "
            f"UTF16={1 if state.is_utf16 else 0}"
            f"{'  overflow' if state.entry.is_overflow else ''}"
            f"{f'  ⚠ shared ×{len(state.shared_with) + 1}' if state.is_shared else ''}"
            f"{'  *' if state.modified else ''} ",
        )]

    def _body_rows():
        if state.is_add:
            return [
                "\x1b[2mNew string to add to the string table.\x1b[0m",
                "",
                "\x1b[2mKind:\x1b[0m      String  \x1b[2m(Identifier not yet supported)\x1b[0m",
                f"\x1b[2mLength:\x1b[0m    {state.char_length} chars · "
                f"{state.byte_length} bytes  \x1b[2m(free)\x1b[0m",
                "\x1b[2mEncoding:\x1b[0m  8-bit ASCII  \x1b[2m(non-ASCII not yet supported)\x1b[0m",
                "",
                "\x1b[2mAppended to the end of the string storage: no existing index\x1b[0m",
                "\x1b[2mchanges. Use it later in a LoadConstString with `edit func:`.\x1b[0m",
            ]
        e = state.entry
        kind_name = ("Identifier" if state.kind == _libhbc.StringKind.Identifier
                     else "String")
        rows = [
            f"\x1b[2mKind:\x1b[0m      {kind_name}",
            f"\x1b[2mLength:\x1b[0m    {state.char_length} chars · "
            f"{state.byte_length} bytes  \x1b[2m(length is free - a value of "
            f"different length re-points the entry instead of overwriting it)\x1b[0m",
            f"\x1b[2mEncoding:\x1b[0m  "
            f"{'UTF-16LE' if state.is_utf16 else '8-bit ASCII'}"
            f"{'  overflow' if e.is_overflow else ''}",
        ]
        if state.is_shared:
            others = ", ".join(f"string:{j}" for j in state.shared_with)
            rows.append(
                f"\x1b[33m⚠ storage shared with {others}\x1b[0m - "
                f"this edit \x1b[1mDETACHES\x1b[0m it from the group (detach): "
                f"the others remain intact on the old bytes.")
        rows.append("")
        rows.append(f"\x1b[2mByte view (storage @ {e.storage_offset:#x}):\x1b[0m")
        rows += display.hex_view_rows(state.context_bytes, state.context_base,
                                      state.highlight)
        rows.append("")
        n = sum(len(x.sites) for x in state.xrefs)
        rows.append(f"\x1b[2mReferences ({n} sit{'e' if n == 1 else 'es'}):\x1b[0m")
        xr = display.xrefs_detail_to_ansi_rows(state.xrefs, state.funcs)
        rows += xr if xr else ["  \x1b[2m(no references)\x1b[0m"]
        return rows

    def _body():
        vh = view_height()
        rows = _body_rows()
        state._max_top = max(0, len(rows) - vh)
        state.top = max(0, min(state.top, state._max_top))
        return ANSI("\n".join(rows[state.top:state.top + vh]))

    def _status():
        if state.is_add:
            return [(CURSOR_STYLE,
                     f" new string (kind String)   {state.byte_length} B   "
                     f"{'ready' if state.buf_ok() else 'incomplete'} ")]
        return [(
            CURSOR_STYLE,
            f" off {state.entry.storage_offset:#x}   {state.byte_length} B original   "
            f"{'MODIFIED' if state.modified else 'unchanged'} ",
        )]

    def _bar1():
        if state.mode == "exit_ask":
            prompt = (" new string - add it to the string table? "
                      if state.is_add
                      else " string modified - apply to the in-memory image? ")
            return apply_discard_cancel_bar(prompt)
        n = state.buf_byte_len()
        ok = state.buf_ok()   # no length constraint, only the encoding
        if state.is_add:
            tag = f"   [{'?' if n is None else n} B {'OK' if ok else 'error'}]"
        else:
            tag = f"   [{'?' if n is None else n}/{state.byte_length} B {'OK' if ok else 'error'}]"
        return input_bar(" new value: ", state.buf, state.cur) + [
            (HINT_STYLE if ok else ERR_STYLE, tag)]

    def _bar2():
        if state.edit_err:
            return [(ERR_STYLE, "  " + state.edit_err)]
        if state.mode == "exit_ask":
            if state.is_add:
                return [(HINT_STYLE,
                         "  Y adds the string and rebuilds the file in memory · "
                         "the .hbc is written by `patch`")]
            return [(HINT_STYLE,
                     "  Y re-encodes and applies to the image (integrity check) · "
                     "the .hbc is written by `patch`")]
        if state.is_add:
            return [(HINT_STYLE,
                     "  <-> move · Home/End · BS/Del · Esc cancels · "
                     "^X add/exit   (ASCII only)")]
        hint = "BMP only (UTF-16LE)" if state.is_utf16 else "ASCII only (8-bit entry)"
        return [(HINT_STYLE,
                 f"  <-> move · Home/End · BS/Del · Esc restores · ^N new · "
                 f"PgUp/PgDn scrolls · ^X save/exit   ({hint})")]

    kb = KeyBindings()
    in_edit = Condition(lambda: state.mode == "edit")
    in_ask = Condition(lambda: state.mode == "exit_ask")
    not_add = Condition(lambda: state.mode == "edit" and not state.is_add)

    bind_abort(kb, state)

    @kb.add("c-n", filter=not_add)
    def _new(event):
        state.switch_to_add()
        event.app.invalidate()

    @kb.add("c-x", filter=in_edit)
    def _cx(event):
        state.request_exit(event)

    @kb.add("escape", filter=in_edit)
    def _esc(event):
        state.reset_buf(); event.app.invalidate()

    bind_text_input(kb, state, in_edit)

    @kb.add("pageup", filter=in_edit)
    def _pgup(event):
        state.scroll(-view_height()); event.app.invalidate()

    @kb.add("pagedown", filter=in_edit)
    def _pgdn(event):
        state.scroll(+view_height()); event.app.invalidate()

    bind_exit_prompt(kb, state, in_ask, cancel_mode="edit")

    run_screen(_title, _body, _status, _bar1, _bar2, kb, _input=_input, _output=_output)
    return state

```

`cli/literals.py`:

```py
"""Decoder/encoder for the SerializedLiteral (SLP) format of the array/object
literal buffers (`array buffer`, `object key buffer`, `object value buffer`),
read by NewArrayWithBuffer[Long] / NewObjectWithBuffer[Long].

Typed RLE runs (verified against hermes-dec and `hermes -dump-bytecode`):

    tag byte = [ext:1][tag:3][len:4]
    ext == 0  ->  len = tag_byte & 0x0F                      (run <= 15)
    ext == 1  ->  len = ((tag_byte & 0x0F) << 8) | next_byte  (run <= 4095, tag on 2 bytes)

    tag: 0 Null, 1 True, 2 False, 3 Number, 4 LongString,
         5 ShortString, 6 ByteString, 7 Integer
    Each element follows as little-endian value bytes:
        Null/True/False -> 0 bytes
        ByteString      -> 1 byte  (string index, uint8)
        ShortString     -> 2 bytes (string index, uint16)
        Integer         -> 4 bytes (int32, SIGNED)
        LongString      -> 4 bytes (string index, uint32)
        Number          -> 8 bytes (double)

Example: `var a=[10,20,30]` (`-g0`) gives the array buffer
`73 0a000000 14000000 1e000000` (tag Integer, run 3, three int32). A value that
doesn't fit int32 (e.g. 3000000000) is promoted by Hermes to the Number tag, a
different run with different bytes: that is why the same-size path rejects a
value that would change the tag (see `encode_slp_element`).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import struct
from collections import namedtuple
from enum import IntEnum


class SLPTag(IntEnum):
    NULL = 0
    TRUE = 1
    FALSE = 2
    NUMBER = 3
    LONG_STRING = 4
    SHORT_STRING = 5
    BYTE_STRING = 6
    INTEGER = 7


_STRING_TAGS = (SLPTag.LONG_STRING, SLPTag.SHORT_STRING, SLPTag.BYTE_STRING)
_ZERO_WIDTH_TAGS = (SLPTag.NULL, SLPTag.TRUE, SLPTag.FALSE)

_VALUE_WIDTH = {
    SLPTag.NULL: 0, SLPTag.TRUE: 0, SLPTag.FALSE: 0,
    SLPTag.NUMBER: 8, SLPTag.LONG_STRING: 4, SLPTag.SHORT_STRING: 2,
    SLPTag.BYTE_STRING: 1, SLPTag.INTEGER: 4,
}

# A decoded element. `byte_off`/`byte_len` are ABSOLUTE within the buffer
# passed to `decode_slp`.
SLPValue = namedtuple("SLPValue", "tag value byte_off byte_len")


class SLPError(Exception):
    pass


def decode_slp(data: bytes, start: int, count: int) -> list[SLPValue]:
    """Decode `count` elements of `data` (a whole buffer) starting at `start`.
    Raises `SLPError` if the buffer ends first (truncated, or a wrong offset)."""
    out: list[SLPValue] = []
    pos = start
    n = len(data)
    while len(out) < count:
        if pos >= n:
            raise SLPError(
                f"SLP buffer truncated at offset {pos:#x} "
                f"(expected {count} elements, read {len(out)})")
        tag_byte = data[pos]
        ext = tag_byte >> 7
        tag = SLPTag((tag_byte >> 4) & 0x7)
        if ext:
            if pos + 1 >= n:
                raise SLPError(f"extended SLP tag truncated at offset {pos:#x}")
            run_len = ((tag_byte & 0x0F) << 8) | data[pos + 1]
            pos += 2
        else:
            run_len = tag_byte & 0x0F
            pos += 1

        width = _VALUE_WIDTH[tag]
        for _ in range(run_len):
            if len(out) >= count:
                break
            byte_off = pos
            if pos + width > n:
                raise SLPError(f"SLP value truncated at offset {pos:#x}")
            raw = data[pos:pos + width]
            if tag == SLPTag.NUMBER:
                value = struct.unpack("<d", raw)[0]
            elif width:
                value = int.from_bytes(raw, "little")
                if tag == SLPTag.INTEGER:
                    value = struct.unpack("<i", raw)[0]   # signed
            else:
                value = None
            out.append(SLPValue(tag, value, byte_off, width))
            pos += width
    return out


def _encode_text(tag: SLPTag, s: str, string_count: int, *, same_size: bool) -> bytes:
    """Value bytes for `tag` from the (stripped, non-empty) text `s`.
    `same_size` only changes the Integer error text: it explains why a decimal
    point or a large value would change the tag."""
    if tag == SLPTag.INTEGER:
        try:
            n = int(s, 0)
        except ValueError:
            raise SLPError(
                "not an integer (decimal or 0x…) - a value with a decimal "
                "point would change the tag to Number" if same_size
                else "not an integer (decimal or 0x…)")
        if not (-(2**31) <= n <= 2**31 - 1):
            raise SLPError(
                "Integer out of range (int32: -2147483648..2147483647) - a "
                "larger value would promote the tag to Number" if same_size
                else "Integer out of range (int32: -2147483648..2147483647)")
        return struct.pack("<i", n)

    if tag == SLPTag.NUMBER:
        try:
            return struct.pack("<d", float(s))
        except ValueError:
            raise SLPError("not a number")

    if tag in _STRING_TAGS:
        try:
            idx = int(s, 0)
        except ValueError:
            raise SLPError("string index is not an integer (decimal or 0x…)")
        if not (0 <= idx < string_count):
            raise SLPError(f"string index out of range (0–{string_count - 1})")
        width = _VALUE_WIDTH[tag]
        if idx >= (1 << (width * 8)):
            raise SLPError(
                f"index {idx} doesn't fit in {tag.name} ({width * 8} bits)")
        return idx.to_bytes(width, "little")

    raise SLPError(f"unknown SLP tag: {tag!r}")


def encode_slp_element(tag: SLPTag, raw: str, *, string_count: int = 0) -> bytes:
    """Encode ONE element keeping the same `tag`, the only same-size case.
    `raw` is the text typed by the user (decimal or `0x…`); `string_count` is
    `len(strings())`, for the range check on string tags.

    Raises `SLPError` for: Null/True/False (toggling changes the tag byte, a
    relocation), a value not valid for the tag (a decimal point on Integer
    would change the tag to Number), Integer out of int32 range, string index
    out of range or too wide for the tag.
    """
    s = raw.strip()
    if not s:
        raise SLPError("empty value")

    if tag in _ZERO_WIDTH_TAGS:
        raise SLPError(
            f"element {tag.name} - Null/True/False toggle needs a relocation "
            f"(would change the tag byte, not just the value)")

    return _encode_text(tag, s, string_count, same_size=True)


def encode_slp_value(tag: SLPTag, raw: str, *, string_count: int = 0) -> bytes:
    """Like `encode_slp_element`, but for a tag the caller chose explicitly
    (e.g. from the editor's picker), so it may differ from the original:
    Null/True/False give `b""` (the tag itself is the value, `raw` is ignored).

    Raises `SLPError` for a value not valid for the tag, Integer out of int32
    range, string index out of range or too wide for the tag.
    """
    if tag in _ZERO_WIDTH_TAGS:
        return b""

    s = raw.strip()
    if not s:
        raise SLPError("empty value")

    return _encode_text(tag, s, string_count, same_size=False)


def reencode_value_bytes(tag: SLPTag, value) -> bytes:
    """Value bytes (no tag byte) of an already decoded element, to re-append an
    element the edit didn't touch. Exact: doubles round-trip through IEEE 754."""
    if tag in _ZERO_WIDTH_TAGS:
        return b""
    if tag == SLPTag.NUMBER:
        return struct.pack("<d", value)
    if tag == SLPTag.INTEGER:
        return struct.pack("<i", value)
    width = _VALUE_WIDTH[tag]
    return int(value).to_bytes(width, "little")


def encode_slp_sequence(items: "list[tuple[SLPTag, bytes]]") -> bytes:
    """Greedy RLE of a whole element sequence, the inverse of `decode_slp`
    (runs up to 4095 with the ext bit, else 15). It needn't match Hermes's
    original bytes: the regenerated site goes to a new region of the buffer."""
    out = bytearray()
    i = 0
    n = len(items)
    while i < n:
        tag = items[i][0]
        j = i
        while j < n and items[j][0] == tag and (j - i) < 4095:
            j += 1
        run_len = j - i
        if run_len <= 15:
            out.append((tag.value << 4) | run_len)
        else:
            out.append(0x80 | (tag.value << 4) | (run_len >> 8))
            out.append(run_len & 0xFF)
        for k in range(i, j):
            out.extend(items[k][1])
        i = j
    return bytes(out)


def rebuild_site_bytes(elements: "list[SLPValue]", edit_index: int,
                       new_tag: SLPTag, new_value_bytes: bytes) -> bytes:
    """COMPLETE payload of a site: `elements` re-encoded, with only
    `elements[edit_index]` replaced by `(new_tag, new_value_bytes)`."""
    items: list[tuple[SLPTag, bytes]] = []
    for i, item in enumerate(elements):
        if i == edit_index:
            items.append((new_tag, new_value_bytes))
        else:
            items.append((item.tag, reencode_value_bytes(item.tag, item.value)))
    return encode_slp_sequence(items)


def decode_value_bytes(tag: SLPTag, raw: bytes):
    """Decode one element's value bytes (no tag byte)."""
    if tag in _ZERO_WIDTH_TAGS:
        return None
    if tag == SLPTag.NUMBER:
        return struct.unpack("<d", raw)[0]
    if tag == SLPTag.INTEGER:
        return struct.unpack("<i", raw)[0]
    return int.from_bytes(raw, "little")


_TYPE_NAMES = {
    SLPTag.NULL: "Null", SLPTag.TRUE: "True", SLPTag.FALSE: "False",
    SLPTag.NUMBER: "Number", SLPTag.LONG_STRING: "LongString",
    SLPTag.SHORT_STRING: "ShortString", SLPTag.BYTE_STRING: "ByteString",
    SLPTag.INTEGER: "Integer",
}


def slp_type_name(tag: SLPTag) -> str:
    return _TYPE_NAMES.get(tag, f"tag{int(tag)}")


def slp_render(item: SLPValue, strings: list) -> str:
    """Human-readable form of an element, for the UI."""
    if item.tag == SLPTag.NULL:
        return "null"
    if item.tag == SLPTag.TRUE:
        return "true"
    if item.tag == SLPTag.FALSE:
        return "false"
    if item.tag == SLPTag.NUMBER:
        return repr(item.value)
    if item.tag == SLPTag.INTEGER:
        return str(item.value)
    if item.tag in _STRING_TAGS:
        if 0 <= item.value < len(strings):
            s = str(strings[item.value])
            if len(s) > 24:
                s = s[:21] + "..."
            return repr(s)
        return f"#{item.value}"
```
