`core/include/hbc/format.h`:

```h
// On-disk HBC structures. Layout is identical across v94, v95 and v96, so a
// single set of structs covers all supported versions; per-version differences
// live only in the opcode tables (see format/opcodes_vNN.cpp).
#pragma once

#include <array>
#include <cstdint>

namespace hbc {

// Little-endian bytes on disk: C6 1F BC 03 C1 03 19 1F.
constexpr uint64_t HBC_MAGIC = 0x1F1903C103BC1FC6ULL;

constexpr std::array<uint32_t, 3> SUPPORTED_VERSIONS = {94, 95, 96};

// Header byte at offset 0x6C. Usage: BytecodeOptions{h.options}.bits.hasAsync
// (bit order assumes GCC/Clang on little-endian).
union BytecodeOptions {
    struct Bits {
        uint8_t staticBuiltins               : 1;
        uint8_t cjsModulesStaticallyResolved : 1;
        uint8_t hasAsync                     : 1;
        uint8_t _reserved                    : 5;
    } bits;
    uint8_t raw;
    explicit BytecodeOptions(uint8_t r) : raw(r) {}
};
static_assert(sizeof(BytecodeOptions) == 1);

#pragma pack(push, 1)
struct HBCFileHeader {            // First 128 bytes of every HBC file.
    uint64_t magic;               // 0x00  HBC_MAGIC
    uint32_t version;             // 0x08  94, 95 or 96
    uint8_t  sourceHash[20];      // 0x0C  SHA-1 of the JS source (not verified by the runtime)
    uint32_t fileLength;          // 0x20  total size, footer included
    uint32_t globalCodeIndex;     // 0x24  function-table index of the top-level function
    uint32_t functionCount;       // 0x28
    uint32_t stringKindCount;     // 0x2C  RLE entries in the string kind table
    uint32_t identifierCount;     // 0x30  strings used as property keys
    uint32_t stringCount;         // 0x34
    uint32_t overflowStringCount; // 0x38  strings too long for SmallStringTableEntry
    uint32_t stringStorageSize;   // 0x3C  bytes of the raw string blob
    uint32_t bigIntCount;         // 0x40
    uint32_t bigIntStorageSize;   // 0x44
    uint32_t regExpCount;         // 0x48
    uint32_t regExpStorageSize;   // 0x4C
    uint32_t arrayBufferSize;     // 0x50  array literals buffer
    uint32_t objKeyBufferSize;    // 0x54  object literal keys
    uint32_t objValueBufferSize;  // 0x58  object literal values
    uint32_t segmentID;           // 0x5C  0 for monolithic bundles
    uint32_t cjsModuleCount;      // 0x60
    uint32_t functionSourceCount; // 0x64  preserved function sources
    uint32_t debugInfoOffset;     // 0x68  absolute offset of the debug info section
    uint8_t  options;             // 0x6C  see BytecodeOptions
    uint8_t  padding[19];         // 0x6D
};
static_assert(sizeof(HBCFileHeader) == 128);

// 4 bytes per string (bitfields assigned LSB-first on little-endian).
// length == 255 is the sentinel for "real offset/length in OverflowStringTableEntry";
// in that case `offset` is the index of that entry in the overflow table (a string
// goes there when length >= 255 or when its offset doesn't fit in 23 bits).
struct SmallStringTableEntry {
    uint32_t isUTF16 : 1;
    uint32_t offset  : 23;  // into string storage
    uint32_t length  : 8;   // in characters
};
static_assert(sizeof(SmallStringTableEntry) == 4);

// Holds the real offset/length of strings with SmallStringTableEntry.length == 255;
// indexed by the `offset` field of that small entry.
struct OverflowStringTableEntry {
    uint32_t offset;
    uint32_t length;
};
static_assert(sizeof(OverflowStringTableEntry) == 8);

// Values of FunctionFlags::prohibitInvoke. The VM checks
// `prohibitInvoke == isConstructCall`, so 3 behaves like None.
constexpr uint8_t kProhibitInvokeCall      = 0;  // call prohibited: usable only with `new` (ES6 class constructor)
constexpr uint8_t kProhibitInvokeConstruct = 1;  // `new` prohibited (arrow, async, generator)
constexpr uint8_t kProhibitInvokeNone      = 2;  // both allowed (plain function)

// Flags byte shared by SmallFuncHeader and FunctionHeader.
struct FunctionFlags {
    uint8_t prohibitInvoke     : 2;  // kProhibitInvoke*, a 2-bit enum (not two flags)
    uint8_t strictMode         : 1;
    uint8_t hasExceptionHandler: 1;
    uint8_t hasDebugInfo       : 1;
    uint8_t overflowed         : 1;  // SmallFuncHeader only, always 0 in FunctionHeader:
                                     // the real fields are in a FunctionHeader at largeOff, where
                                     // largeOff = (offset & 0xFFFF) | ((infoOffset & 0xFFFF) << 16)
    uint8_t _reserved          : 2;
};
static_assert(sizeof(FunctionFlags) == 1);

// 16 bytes per function in the function table: three bitfield words plus
// four byte fields.
struct SmallFuncHeader {
    // Word 1
    uint32_t offset     : 25;  // absolute offset of the bytecode
    uint32_t paramCount :  7;  // includes the implicit `this`
    // Word 2
    uint32_t bytecodeSizeInBytes : 15;
    uint32_t functionName        : 17;  // string table index
    // Word 3
    uint32_t infoOffset : 25;  // absolute offset of the function-info section (EH table + debug info)
    uint32_t frameSize  :  7;  // registers

    uint8_t       environmentSize;
    uint8_t       highestReadCacheIndex;
    uint8_t       highestWriteCacheIndex;
    FunctionFlags flags;
};
static_assert(sizeof(SmallFuncHeader) == 16);

// Full-width version of SmallFuncHeader, for functions whose fields don't fit
// the reduced widths (e.g. environmentSize > 255).
// Hermes sets infoOffset = largeOff (self-reference): the real function-info
// section sits right after this struct, at largeOff + sizeof(FunctionHeader).
struct FunctionHeader {
    uint32_t offset;
    uint32_t paramCount;
    uint32_t bytecodeSizeInBytes;
    uint32_t functionName;
    uint32_t infoOffset;  // sentinel, see above
    uint32_t frameSize;
    uint32_t environmentSize;
    uint8_t  highestReadCacheIndex;
    uint8_t  highestWriteCacheIndex;
    FunctionFlags flags;  // overflowed = 0
    uint8_t  padding;
};
static_assert(sizeof(FunctionHeader) == 32);

// Exception handler table: this header followed by `count` entries, located at
// the function's infoOffset (largeOff + 32 if overflowed), not right after the
// bytecode.
struct ExceptionHandlerTableHeader { uint32_t count; };

// Offsets are relative to the start of the function's bytecode.
struct HBCExceptionHandlerInfo {
    uint32_t start;   // inclusive
    uint32_t end;     // exclusive
    uint32_t target;  // catch handler entry
};
static_assert(sizeof(HBCExceptionHandlerInfo) == 12);

// `offset` is relative to the start of BigInt storage.
struct BigIntTableEntry { uint32_t offset; uint32_t length; };
static_assert(sizeof(BigIntTableEntry) == 8);

// `offset` is relative to the start of RegExp storage.
struct RegExpTableEntry { uint32_t offset; uint32_t length; };
static_assert(sizeof(RegExpTableEntry) == 8);

#pragma pack(pop)

}
```

`core/include/hbc/hbc.h`:

```h
// Public API of libhbc: the only header clients (Python bindings,
// tests) need.
#pragma once

#include "hbc/format.h"

#include <cstddef>
#include <memory>
#include <stdexcept>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

namespace hbc {

// =============================================================================
// Strings
// =============================================================================

//  Kind from the String Kind Table. Identifiers are property keys
// (GetByVal/PutByVal), Strings are literal values.
enum class StringKind : uint8_t {
    String     = 0,
    Identifier = 1,
};

// Raw location of a string in the file, for same-length in-place edits.
// HBCFile::string_entries() is parallel to strings() and stringKinds().
struct StringEntry {
    uint32_t   storageOffset;  // ABSOLUTE file offset of the first byte
    uint32_t   byteLength;     // charLength, or charLength * 2 if UTF-16
    uint32_t   charLength;     // resolved (overflow table included)
    bool       isUTF16;
    bool       isOverflow;     // SmallStringTableEntry.length == 255
    StringKind kind;
};

// =============================================================================
// Functions
// =============================================================================

// Offsets are relative to the start of the function's bytecode.
struct ExceptionHandlerInfo {
    uint32_t start;   // try-range start (inclusive)
    uint32_t end;     // try-range end (exclusive)
    uint32_t target;  // catch handler entry
};

struct FunctionInfo {
    uint32_t    index;                // position in the function table
    std::string name;                 // "anonymous_func_N" if anonymous
    uint32_t    offset;               // absolute offset of the bytecode
    uint32_t    bytecodeSizeInBytes;
    uint32_t    paramCount;           // includes the implicit `this`
    uint32_t    frameSize;            // registers
    uint32_t    infoOffset;           // absolute offset of the function-info section (EH + debug)
    bool        isStrictMode;
    bool        isAsync;
    bool        isGenerator;
    bool        hasExceptionHandler = false;
    bool        hasDebugInfo        = false;
    bool        prohibitCall        = false;  // usable only with `new` (class constructor)
    bool        prohibitConstruct   = false;  // `new` prohibited (arrow, async, generator)
    bool        overflowed          = false;  // real fields live in a FunctionHeader at largeOff
    bool        shared              = false;  // (offset, size) shared with at least one other function
    uint32_t    shareCount          = 1;      // functions (this one included) pointing to the same body
    uint32_t    debugOffset             = 0;  // into the source location data (relative to its start)
    uint32_t    scopeDescOffset         = 0;  // into the scope descriptor section (relative to its start)
    uint32_t    textifiedCalleesOffset  = 0;  // into the textified callees section (relative to its start)
    // Function Source Table: per-function `"show source"` / `"hide source"` /
    // `"sensitive"` directives (Hermes, same mechanism as `"use strict"`).
    bool        hasPreservedSource = false;  // function has any entry in the table
    bool        sourceIsHidden     = false;  // entry resolves to "" (hide/sensitive marker)
    std::string preservedSource;             // non-empty only for "show source"
    std::vector<ExceptionHandlerInfo> exceptionHandlers;
};

// =============================================================================
// Instructions and opcodes
// =============================================================================

struct Operand {
    enum class Type { Reg8, Reg32, UInt8, UInt16, UInt32, Imm32, Double, Addr8, Addr32, StringID };
    Type type;
    union {  // the member matching `type` is valid
        uint8_t  u8;
        uint16_t u16;
        uint32_t u32;
        int32_t  i32;
        double   f64;
    };
    std::string resolvedString;  // StringID only: the resolved string value
};

struct Instruction {
    uint32_t             offset;    // from the start of the function's bytecode
    uint8_t              opcode;
    std::string          mnemonic;  // e.g. "LoadParam", "Ret"
    std::vector<Operand> operands;
    // SwitchImm only: jump table, one target per case, ordered by case value
    // (index i = case operands[3].u32 + i). Targets are offsets from the start
    // of the function's bytecode. Empty for other opcodes, or if the
    // disassembler had no file buffer (see disassemble()).
    std::vector<uint32_t> switchTargets;
};

// Static description of an opcode, exposed to the Python bytecode editor to
// validate edits and suggest compatible opcodes.
struct OpcodeDesc {
    uint8_t                    opcode;
    std::string                mnemonic;       // e.g. "LoadConstTrue"
    std::vector<Operand::Type> operands;       // PHYSICAL types (never StringID)
    uint8_t                    stringRefMask;  // bit N set: operand N is a string table index
    std::string                jumpKind;       // "None"|"Unconditional"|"Conditional"|"Switch"|"Return"|"Throw"
};

// Defined opcodes for an HBC version; empty if the version isn't supported.
std::vector<OpcodeDesc> opcode_table(uint32_t version);

// Size in bytes of a physical operand type.
uint32_t operand_size(Operand::Type t);

// Encodes one instruction (opcode byte + little-endian operands). Inverse of
// the disassembler's operand decoding. `operands` are numeric values in
// signature order, all passed as double (exact up to 2^53, enough for UInt32/Imm32).
// Throws std::invalid_argument on unknown opcode or wrong operand count,
// std::range_error if a value doesn't fit its operand's physical width.
std::vector<uint8_t> encode_instruction(uint32_t version, uint8_t opcode,
                                        const std::vector<double>& operands);

// =============================================================================
// CFG
// =============================================================================

enum class EdgeKind : uint8_t {
    FallThrough,
    Jump,              // unconditional (Jmp / JmpLong)
    CondTaken,
    CondFallThru,
    SwitchDefault,
    SwitchCase,
    BackEdge,          // loop edge, detected via DFS
    ExceptionHandler,  // edge to the catch block
};

struct CFGEdge {
    uint32_t targetId;  // id of the destination BasicBlock
    EdgeKind kind;
};

// Maximal instruction sequence with no branches in or out except at the ends.
struct BasicBlock {
    uint32_t id;
    uint32_t startOffset;  // in the function's bytecode
    uint32_t endOffset;    // exclusive
    std::vector<Instruction> instructions;
    std::vector<CFGEdge>     successors;
    std::vector<uint32_t>    predecessors;  // block ids
    bool isLoopHeader = false;              // target of a back-edge
};

struct CFGData {
    std::vector<BasicBlock> blocks;
    uint32_t entryId  = 0;
    bool     hasLoops = false;
};

// =============================================================================
// XREFs and call graph
// =============================================================================

struct XRefSite {
    uint32_t    functionIndex;
    uint32_t    instructionOffset;  // in the function's bytecode
    std::string mnemonic;           // e.g. "LoadConstString", "GetByIdShort"
};

// Reference sites of one string. string_xrefs() only returns strings with at least one site.
struct StringXRef {
    uint32_t              stringIndex;  // in strings() and stringKinds()
    std::string           stringValue;  // raw CESU-8 bytes
    std::vector<XRefSite> sites;        // never empty
};

// Edge in the call graph. calleeIndex == 0xFFFFFFFF means not statically
// resolvable (indirect call).
struct CallSite {
    uint32_t    callerIndex;
    uint32_t    calleeIndex;
    uint32_t    offset;       // in the caller's bytecode
    bool        isDirect;     // true: CallDirect*; false: CreateClosure* or Call*/Construct*
    std::string mnemonic;     // distinguishes the cases, e.g. "CallDirect", "CreateClosure", "Call2"
};

// =============================================================================
// Literal buffers
// =============================================================================

// A NewArrayWithBuffer[Long] / NewObjectWithBuffer[Long] instruction. The
// serialized literal (SLP format, decoded in `cli/literals.py`) lives in the
// array / object key / object value buffers.
struct LiteralSite {
    uint32_t    functionIndex;
    uint32_t    instructionOffset;  // in the function's bytecode
    std::string mnemonic;
    bool        isObject;
    uint32_t    count;              // numElems (array) or numLiterals (object)
    uint32_t    bufferIdx;          // array: the buffer; object: the value buffer
    uint32_t    keyBufferIdx;       // object only (0 for arrays)
};

// =============================================================================
// Modules, source locations, sections
// =============================================================================

// Metro module, from the __d(factory, moduleId, deps) pattern in the global function.
struct ModuleInfo {
    uint32_t functionIndex;  // factory function
    uint32_t moduleId;
};

// An entry of the CJS Module Table (header.cjsModuleCount), present only
// when the file was compiled with Hermes's own native CommonJS mode
// (`hermes -commonjs`), never in a Metro-bundled bundle (recover_modules()
// covers that case instead; the two mechanisms are mutually exclusive). See
// doc/hbc-format/v96-format.md §9 for the on-disk format. The table has two
// on-disk shapes, selected by header.options.cjsModulesStaticallyResolved;
// as of the public Hermes source this project targets, the "static" shape
// can never actually be emitted by the compiler (confirmed by reading
// ResolveStaticRequire's dead `getUseCJSModules()` guard and by compiling
// samples), so `modulePath` is populated and `isStaticallyResolved` is
// false in every file observed so far.
struct CJSModuleInfo {
    uint32_t    functionIndex;        // the module's wrapper function (exports, require, module)
    bool        isStaticallyResolved; // header.options bit 1, see above
    uint32_t    moduleId;             // raw "first" field of the entry: a String Table
                                       // index when !isStaticallyResolved, otherwise a
                                       // compiler-assigned integer (never observed)
    std::string modulePath;           // !isStaticallyResolved only: strings()[moduleId],
                                       // the module's source file path. Empty otherwise.
};

// Maps a bytecode address to a source position (from the debug info section).
struct SourceLocation {
    uint32_t address;  // from the start of the function's bytecode
    uint32_t line;     // 1-indexed, relative to FileRegion.line
    uint32_t column;   // 0-indexed
};

struct Section {
    std::string name;
    uint32_t    offset;  // absolute
    uint32_t    size;
    uint32_t    align;
};

// =============================================================================
// Debug info
// =============================================================================
// 7-field header at header.debugInfoOffset. The last four fields are
// CUMULATIVE offsets into the data blob (which starts after the filename
// table, filename storage and file regions): each marks the end of its
// sub-section, i.e. the start of the next.
//   [0, sourceLocDataEnd)               source location data
//   [sourceLocDataEnd, scopeDescDataEnd)   scope descriptor data
//   [scopeDescDataEnd, textifiedCalleesEnd) textified callees data
//   [textifiedCalleesEnd, stringTableEnd)   debug string table
// Hermes calls them scopeDescDataOffset, textifiedCalleeOffset,
// stringTableOffset and debugDataSize (same values, read as the start of the
// following sub-section).
struct DebugInfoHeader {
    uint32_t filenameCount;
    uint32_t filenameStorageSize;
    uint32_t fileRegionCount;
    uint32_t sourceLocDataEnd;
    uint32_t scopeDescDataEnd;
    uint32_t textifiedCalleesEnd;
    uint32_t stringTableEnd;  // = total blob size
};

// A variable captured in a function's scope, in declaration order. NOT indexed
// by register: the register-to-name binding must be derived separately (e.g.
// from StoreToEnvironment/LoadFromEnvironment).
struct ScopeVariable {
    std::string name;
};

// Call site with the callee's textual name, for readable stack traces.
struct TextifiedCallee {
    uint32_t    bytecodeOffset;  // of the call instruction
    std::string name;            // from the debug string table
};

// =============================================================================
// HBCFile
// =============================================================================
// An open HBC file (Pimpl: fd/mmap live in parser.cpp). Copies share the
// underlying Impl; the last one destroyed unmaps and closes.
class HBCFile {
public:
    // Opens and validates a file. Throws FileTooSmallError, InvalidMagicError
    // or UnsupportedVersionError.
    static HBCFile open(const std::string& path);

    // Like open() but from an in-memory image (copied). Used by the patcher to
    // re-parse an edited image. Same exceptions as open().
    static HBCFile from_bytes(const std::string& bytes);

    uint32_t version() const;  // 94, 95 or 96

    // Header, referencing the mapped file.
    const HBCFileHeader& header() const;

    const std::vector<std::string>&  strings()                      const;
    const std::vector<FunctionInfo>& functions()                    const;
    const std::vector<StringKind>&   stringKinds()                  const;
    const std::vector<StringEntry>&  string_entries()               const;
    const std::vector<LiteralSite>&  literal_sites()                const;
    const std::string&               array_buffer()                 const;
    const std::string&               obj_key_buffer()               const;
    const std::string&               obj_value_buffer()             const;
    // ABSOLUTE file offsets of the three buffers (from section_map()); 0 if the
    // section is absent.
    uint32_t                         array_buffer_offset()          const;
    uint32_t                         obj_key_buffer_offset()        const;
    uint32_t                         obj_value_buffer_offset()      const;
    std::vector<Instruction>         disasm(uint32_t functionIndex) const;
    CFGData                          cfg(uint32_t functionIndex)    const;
    std::vector<StringXRef>          string_xrefs()                 const;
    std::vector<CallSite>            call_graph()                   const;
    std::vector<ModuleInfo>          recover_modules()              const;
    std::vector<CJSModuleInfo>       cjs_modules()                  const;
    std::vector<std::string>         source_files()                 const;
    std::vector<SourceLocation>      source_locations(uint32_t functionIndex) const;
    std::string                      decompile(uint32_t functionIndex) const;
    DebugInfoHeader                  debug_info_header()            const;
    std::vector<ScopeVariable>       scope_variables(uint32_t functionIndex)   const;
    std::vector<TextifiedCallee>     textified_callees(uint32_t functionIndex) const;
    std::vector<std::string>         debug_strings()                const;

    // The file's raw bytes (read-only mapped memory) and size (= header
    // fileLength, footer included).
    const uint8_t* raw_data() const;
    size_t         raw_size() const;

    // All sections with absolute offset, size and alignment. Offsets are
    // computed from the header counts: the format only stores debugInfoOffset.
    std::vector<Section> section_map() const;

    // Byte copy of the mapped file (an unchanged file is identical to the source).
    std::vector<uint8_t> serialize() const;

private:
    struct Impl;
    std::shared_ptr<Impl> impl_;
    explicit HBCFile(std::shared_ptr<Impl> impl);
};

// =============================================================================
// Exceptions
// =============================================================================

// First 8 bytes don't match HBC_MAGIC.
struct InvalidMagicError : std::runtime_error {
    InvalidMagicError() : std::runtime_error("Not a valid HBC file (bad magic)") {}
};

// Version not in SUPPORTED_VERSIONS.
struct UnsupportedVersionError : std::runtime_error {
    explicit UnsupportedVersionError(uint32_t v)
        : std::runtime_error("Unsupported HBC version: " + std::to_string(v)) {}
};

// Smaller than the 128-byte header.
struct FileTooSmallError : std::runtime_error {
    FileTooSmallError() : std::runtime_error("File too small to be a valid HBC file") {}
};

} // namespace hbc

```

`core/include/hbc/module.h`:

```h
// Structural serializer. A Module is a snapshot of an HBCFile that accepts
// edits which change sizes (a longer function body, a new string, a resized
// literal, a new function) and re-serializes the whole file: function table,
// section offsets, the exception handler tables of touched functions,
// header.fileLength / debugInfoOffset and the SHA-1 footer. The result is a
// valid .hbc that Hermes loads.
//
// Only ONE kind of edit can be queued per Module (two edits mean two commits,
// i.e. two Modules): serialize() throws if they are combined.
#pragma once

#include "hbc/hbc.h"

#include <cstdint>
#include <optional>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

namespace hbc {

// Abstract instruction for the assembler. For jumps, `jumpTargetIdx` is the
// INDEX of the target in the instruction list (not a byte offset) and
// `addrOperandPos` the position of the Addr operand to fill in.
struct AsmInstr {
    uint8_t             opcode         = 0;
    std::vector<double> operands;              // the Addr slot is a placeholder
    int32_t             jumpTargetIdx  = -1;   // -1 = not a jump
    int8_t              addrOperandPos = -1;   // -1 = no Addr operand
    // Byte offset the instruction had in the ORIGINAL body (function-relative),
    // -1 if it is new. Used to relocate the exception handler table.
    int32_t             origByteOffset = -1;
};

struct AssembledFunction {
    std::vector<uint8_t>  bytecode;
    std::vector<uint32_t> offsets;   // byte offset of every instruction
};

// Relocatable assembler: assigns offsets, promotes short jumps (Addr8) to
// their Long variant (Addr32) until every displacement fits, fills in the
// displacements and emits the bytes.
// Throws std::invalid_argument (version/opcode), std::out_of_range (target
// index), std::runtime_error (short jump with no Long variant, no convergence).
AssembledFunction assemble_function(uint32_t version, std::vector<AsmInstr> ir);

class Module {
public:
    // Snapshot of `file`. Handles overflowed functions and real bundles
    // (bodies out of index order, shared bytecode).
    static Module from(const HBCFile& file);

    uint32_t version() const { return version_; }
    uint32_t function_count() const { return static_cast<uint32_t>(funcs_.size()); }

    // Replaces the body of function `funcIdx`. `frameSize` is the new register
    // count (>= original, <= 127). With `editAll`, a function with shared
    // bytecode has the edit applied to every function of the group (their EH
    // tables are relocated at serialize time).
    // Throws std::runtime_error if: the original function contains SwitchImm or
    // SaveGenerator; `ir` contains a SwitchImm; `frameSize` doesn't fit 7 bits;
    // `frameSize` grows on a function with an exception handler (with editAll:
    // on any such member of the group); the bytecode is shared and
    // `editAll == false` (a private clone is not supported).
    void set_function_body(uint32_t funcIdx, std::vector<AsmInstr> ir,
                           uint32_t frameSize, bool editAll = false);

    // Appends a `String`-kind string. Returns its index in the serialized file.
    // It goes at the end of the string storage, so no existing entry moves.
    // Throws std::invalid_argument if `value` is empty or non-ASCII.
    uint32_t add_string(const std::string& value);

    // Replaces the content (and length) of string `idx`. `newBytes` is already
    // encoded by the caller (ASCII on 8-bit entries, UTF-16LE on isUTF16 ones).
    // The new bytes are appended to the string storage and only entry `idx` is
    // repointed, never an overwrite: a shared entry is detached automatically.
    // Throws std::out_of_range (bad idx); std::invalid_argument (odd size on a
    // UTF-16 entry); std::runtime_error if the entry isn't overflow and the new
    // length is >= 255 (promotion not supported), or if a string edit is already
    // queued. An entry that is already overflow stays overflow.
    void set_string_value(uint32_t idx, const std::string& newBytes);

    // Replaces the COMPLETE SLP payload of a NewArrayWithBuffer[Long] /
    // NewObjectWithBuffer[Long] site (`newBufferBytes` is the whole buffer
    // re-encoded by the Python side). It is appended to "array buffer" or
    // "object value buffer" (never "object key buffer": keys are read-only) and
    // only this instruction's bufferIdx operand is repointed, in place, same
    // width. count/sizeHint are unchanged.
    // Resolved IMMEDIATELY by re-disassembling the function, not in serialize().
    // Throws std::out_of_range (no instruction of the expected mnemonic at
    // funcIdx/instrOffset); std::runtime_error if the function has shared
    // bytecode, the new offset doesn't fit the operand (promotion to *Long not
    // supported), or another edit is already queued.
    void set_literal_value(uint32_t funcIdx, uint32_t instrOffset,
                           bool isObject, const std::string& newBufferBytes);

    // Adds (`isAdd`) or removes the LAST element (array) or key-value pair
    // (object) of a literal site. `newBufferBytes` is the COMPLETE value payload
    // with count +/- 1 elements, `newKeyBufferBytes` the complete key payload
    // (objects only). Both are appended to their sections; count, sizeHint (only
    // if it equalled count), bufferIdx and keyBufferIdx are rewritten. An
    // existing key is never touched.
    // Throws std::out_of_range (no such instruction, or `!isAdd` with count == 0);
    // std::runtime_error if the bytecode is shared, sizeHint != count in the
    // original (mixed literal + dynamic), the new count exceeds 65535 (no *Long
    // variant exists), an offset doesn't fit its operand, or another edit is queued.
    void resize_literal(uint32_t funcIdx, uint32_t instrOffset, bool isObject,
                        bool isAdd, const std::string& newBufferBytes,
                        const std::string& newKeyBufferBytes = std::string());

    // Appends a new function at the end of the function table and returns its
    // index (= current function_count()). `ir` is assembled in serialize();
    // `frameSize` must cover the registers used (<= 127, never an overflow
    // function). Metadata is fixed: paramCount = 1 (`this` only), functionName =
    // string 0 (cosmetic), strict mode, no exception handler, no debug info
    // (so its function-info section is empty).
    // Throws std::runtime_error if `ir` is empty, has an unknown opcode or a
    // SwitchImm, `frameSize` > 127, or another edit is already queued.
    uint32_t add_function(std::vector<AsmInstr> ir, uint32_t frameSize);

    // Rebuilds the complete file (header, tables, bytecode, info, debug, footer).
    std::vector<uint8_t> serialize();

    const std::vector<std::string>& warnings() const { return warnings_; }

private:
    struct FuncState {
        uint32_t                 origOffset      = 0;
        uint32_t                 origSize        = 0;
        uint32_t                 origInfoOffset  = 0;
        uint32_t                 origFrameSize   = 0;
        bool                     hasEH           = false;
        bool                     hasDebugInfo    = false;
        bool                     overflowed      = false;
        uint32_t                 origLargeOff    = 0;   // only if overflowed
        bool                     sharedBody      = false;
        std::vector<uint32_t>    shareGroup;            // indices sharing origOffset (self included)
        bool                     dirty           = false;
        bool                     editAll         = false;
        std::vector<AsmInstr>    newIr;
        uint32_t                 newFrameSize    = 0;
    };

    // A section between string storage and bytecode (array/object buffers,
    // bigint, regexp, cjs module table, function source table), re-laid-out
    // with its own `align`. `name` is the section_map() name.
    struct MidSection {
        std::string          name;
        uint32_t             align = 1;
        std::vector<uint8_t> bytes;
    };

    // The string sections as they will be serialized, after add_string /
    // set_string_value.
    struct StringSections {
        std::vector<uint8_t> kindTable, stringTable, overflowTable, storage;
        uint32_t stringCount = 0, kindCount = 0, overflowCount = 0;
    };
    StringSections buildStringSections() const;

    // A NewArray/ObjectWithBuffer instruction located in its function, with the
    // absolute byte position (in bytecodeBlob_) and width of each operand.
    struct LiteralTarget {
        Instruction           instr;
        std::vector<uint32_t> operandBytePos;
        std::vector<uint32_t> operandWidth;
    };
    // `who` prefixes error messages; `action` completes the shared-bytecode error;
    // `maxOperandIdx` is the highest operand the caller uses.
    LiteralTarget locateLiteralSite(const char* who, const char* action, uint32_t funcIdx,
                                    uint32_t instrOffset, bool isObject,
                                    uint32_t maxOperandIdx) const;

    // Offset a buffer appended to section `midName` will start at, checked
    // against the operand width.
    uint32_t newBufferOffset(const char* who, const char* midName, uint32_t operandWidth) const;

    uint32_t version_ = 0;

    std::vector<uint8_t>     header_;        // 128 bytes
    std::vector<uint8_t>     funcHeaders_;   // 16 * count (raw SmallFuncHeader)

    std::vector<uint8_t>     kindTable_;     // string kind table
    std::vector<uint8_t>     idHash_;        // identifier hash table, kept verbatim
    std::vector<uint8_t>     stringTable_;
    std::vector<uint8_t>     overflowTable_;
    std::vector<uint8_t>     stringStorage_;
    std::vector<MidSection>  midSections_;

    std::vector<uint8_t>     bytecodeBlob_;  // all function bodies, verbatim, from blobStart_
    std::vector<uint8_t>     infoBlob_;      // function-info sections (overflow FunctionHeader + EH + debug)
    std::vector<uint8_t>     debugBlob_;     // debug info section

    uint32_t funcTableEnd_       = 0;   // 128 + count*16 (start of the kind table)
    uint32_t blobStart_          = 0;   // lowest function offset (NOT funcs_[0].origOffset)
    uint32_t oldInfoStart_       = 0;
    uint32_t oldDebugInfoOffset_ = 0;
    uint32_t origStringCount_    = 0;

    // Queued edits. The setters resolve everything that depends on the original
    // file immediately (operand positions, overflow slot, ...), so serialize()
    // only does mechanical work.
    std::vector<std::string> pendingStrings_;  // add_string()

    struct PendingStringEdit {
        uint32_t    idx;
        std::string newBytes;    // already encoded
        bool        isUTF16;
        bool        wasOverflow;
        uint32_t    ovfSlot;     // valid only if wasOverflow
    };
    std::optional<PendingStringEdit> pendingStringEdit_;

    struct PendingLiteralEdit {
        uint32_t    operandBytePos;   // absolute in bytecodeBlob_
        uint32_t    operandWidth;     // 2 (UInt16) or 4 (UInt32)
        std::string midSectionName;   // "array buffer" | "object value buffer"
        std::string newBufferBytes;
        uint32_t    offRel;           // new value of the bufferIdx operand
    };
    std::optional<PendingLiteralEdit> pendingLiteralEdit_;

    struct PendingLiteralResize {
        uint32_t    countOperandBytePos;
        uint32_t    sizeHintOperandBytePos;
        uint32_t    newCount;                 // written into count and sizeHint

        uint32_t    valueOperandBytePos;
        uint32_t    valueOperandWidth;
        std::string valueMidSectionName;      // "array buffer" | "object value buffer"
        std::string newBufferBytes;
        uint32_t    valueOffRel;

        bool        isObject;
        uint32_t    keyOperandBytePos;        // objects only
        uint32_t    keyOperandWidth;
        std::string newKeyBufferBytes;
        uint32_t    keyOffRel;
    };
    std::optional<PendingLiteralResize> pendingLiteralResize_;

    struct PendingFunction {
        std::vector<AsmInstr> ir;
        uint32_t              frameSize      = 0;
        uint32_t              paramCount     = 1;
        uint32_t              functionNameId = 0;
        bool                  strictMode     = true;
    };
    std::optional<PendingFunction> pendingNewFunction_;

    std::vector<FuncState>    funcs_;
    std::vector<std::string>  warnings_;
};

}  // namespace hbc
```

`core/src/analysis/analysis.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "analysis/analysis.h"
#include "hbc/hbc.h"
#include <algorithm>
#include <limits>
#include <unordered_set>

namespace hbc {

namespace {

// Calls fn(function, instruction) for every instruction of every function.
template <typename Fn>
void forEachInstruction(const HBCFile& f, Fn&& fn) {
    for (const auto& func : f.functions())
        for (const auto& instr : f.disasm(func.index))
            fn(func, instr);
}

bool isCreateClosure(const std::string& mnemonic) {
    return mnemonic == "CreateClosure" || mnemonic == "CreateClosureLongIndex";
}

} // namespace

// Reference sites of every StringID operand, grouped by string. Only strings
// with at least one reference are returned, in index order.
std::vector<StringXRef> HBCFile::string_xrefs() const {
    const auto& strs = strings();
    std::vector<std::vector<XRefSite>> sitesByString(strs.size());

    forEachInstruction(*this, [&](const FunctionInfo& func, const Instruction& instr) {
        for (const auto& op : instr.operands)
            if (op.type == Operand::Type::StringID && op.u32 < strs.size())
                sitesByString[op.u32].push_back({func.index, instr.offset, instr.mnemonic});
    });

    std::vector<StringXRef> result;
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < static_cast<uint32_t>(strs.size()); ++i)
        if (!sitesByString[i].empty())
            result.push_back({i, strs[i], std::move(sitesByString[i])});
    return result;
}

// Call sites in three categories:
//   CallDirect*             callee known, isDirect = true
//   CreateClosure*          callee known, isDirect = false (static reference)
//   Call*, Construct*       callee 0xFFFFFFFF, isDirect = false (indirect)
std::vector<CallSite> computeCallGraph(const HBCFile& self) {
    static const std::unordered_set<std::string> DIRECT_CALL = {
        "CallDirect", "CallDirectLongIndex"
    };
    static const std::unordered_set<std::string> STATIC_REF = {
        "CreateClosure",              "CreateClosureLongIndex",
        "CreateGeneratorClosure",     "CreateGeneratorClosureLongIndex",
        "CreateAsyncClosure",         "CreateAsyncClosureLongIndex",
        "CreateGenerator",            "CreateGeneratorLongIndex"
    };
    static const std::unordered_set<std::string> INDIRECT = {
        "Call", "Call1", "Call2", "Call3", "Call4", "CallLong",
        "CallBuiltin", "CallBuiltinLong",
        "Construct", "ConstructLong"
    };

    const size_t functionCount = self.functions().size();
    const uint32_t UNRESOLVED = std::numeric_limits<uint32_t>::max();
    std::vector<CallSite> result;

    forEachInstruction(self, [&](const FunctionInfo& func, const Instruction& instr) {
        const bool isDirect = DIRECT_CALL.count(instr.mnemonic) > 0;
        if ((isDirect || STATIC_REF.count(instr.mnemonic)) && instr.operands.size() >= 3) {
            const uint32_t calleeIdx = instr.operands[2].u32;
            if (calleeIdx < functionCount)
                result.push_back({func.index, calleeIdx, instr.offset, isDirect, instr.mnemonic});
        } else if (INDIRECT.count(instr.mnemonic)) {
            result.push_back({func.index, UNRESOLVED, instr.offset, false, instr.mnemonic});
        }
    });
    return result;
}

// Finds Metro modules in the global function, from the pattern
// __d(factory, moduleId, deps):
//   TryGetById "__d"
//   CreateClosure K              factory = func[K]
//   LoadConstZero/UInt8/Int N    moduleId = N, within 5 instructions
//   NewArrayWithBuffer ...
//   Call4 ...                    within 5 instructions after the moduleId
// The Call4 check avoids false modules from LoadConst* used as ordinary
// arguments (e.g. debug_func(2, ...)).
std::vector<ModuleInfo> computeModules(const HBCFile& self) {
    const auto& funcs = self.functions();
    const auto instrs = self.disasm(self.header().globalCodeIndex);

    std::vector<ModuleInfo> result;
    const size_t N = instrs.size();
    const uint32_t NONE = std::numeric_limits<uint32_t>::max();

    for (size_t i = 0; i < N; ++i) {
        const auto& instr = instrs[i];
        if (!isCreateClosure(instr.mnemonic) || instr.operands.size() < 3) continue;

        const uint32_t factoryIdx = instr.operands[2].u32;
        if (factoryIdx >= funcs.size()) continue;

        uint32_t moduleId    = NONE;
        size_t   moduleIdPos = N;
        for (size_t j = i + 1; j < std::min(N, i + 6); ++j) {
            const auto& next = instrs[j];
            if (next.mnemonic == "LoadConstZero") {
                moduleId    = 0;
                moduleIdPos = j;
                break;
            }
            if ((next.mnemonic == "LoadConstUInt8" || next.mnemonic == "LoadConstInt")
                && next.operands.size() >= 2)
            {
                moduleId    = next.operands[1].u32;
                moduleIdPos = j;
                break;
            }
        }
        if (moduleId == NONE) continue;

        bool hasCall = false;
        for (size_t k = moduleIdPos + 1; k < std::min(N, moduleIdPos + 6); ++k) {
            const std::string& mn = instrs[k].mnemonic;
            if (mn == "Call4" || mn == "CallLong") {
                hasCall = true;
                break;
            }
            if (isCreateClosure(mn)) break;  // the next module starts here
        }

        if (hasCall)
            result.push_back({factoryIdx, moduleId});
    }
    return result;
}

// New{Array,Object}WithBuffer[Long] sites. Operands (v94-96): dst, sizeHint,
// count, then one buffer index (array) or two (object: key buffer, value
// buffer). An object's bufferIdx is the value buffer, the editable one.
std::vector<LiteralSite> computeLiteralSites(const HBCFile& self) {
    std::vector<LiteralSite> result;

    forEachInstruction(self, [&](const FunctionInfo& func, const Instruction& instr) {
        const bool isArr = instr.mnemonic == "NewArrayWithBuffer" ||
                           instr.mnemonic == "NewArrayWithBufferLong";
        const bool isObj = instr.mnemonic == "NewObjectWithBuffer" ||
                           instr.mnemonic == "NewObjectWithBufferLong";
        if (!isArr && !isObj) return;

        LiteralSite site{};
        site.functionIndex     = func.index;
        site.instructionOffset = instr.offset;
        site.mnemonic          = instr.mnemonic;
        site.isObject          = isObj;

        if (isArr) {
            if (instr.operands.size() < 4) return;  // truncated
            site.count        = instr.operands[2].u32;
            site.bufferIdx    = instr.operands[3].u32;
            site.keyBufferIdx = 0;
        } else {
            if (instr.operands.size() < 5) return;
            site.count        = instr.operands[2].u32;
            site.keyBufferIdx = instr.operands[3].u32;
            site.bufferIdx    = instr.operands[4].u32;
        }
        result.push_back(std::move(site));
    });
    return result;
}

} // namespace hbc
```

`core/src/cfg/cfg.cpp`:

```cpp
// Algorithm:
//   1. Leaders: the first instruction, every jump target, and the instruction
//      after every jump or terminator.
//   2. Blocks: the ranges [leader_i, leader_{i+1}).
//   3. Successors, from the jumpKind of each block's last instruction.
//   4. Exception handler edges: every block overlapping a try range gets an
//      edge to its catch block.
//   5. DFS (White/Gray/Black): an edge to a Gray node is a back-edge (loop).

#include "cfg/cfg.h"
#include "format/opcodes.h"

#include <algorithm>
#include <functional>
#include <unordered_map>
#include <unordered_set>
#include <vector>

namespace hbc {

// Jump offsets are relative to the start of the jump instruction itself
// (ip + offset), NOT to the next instruction.
static uint32_t relativeTarget(const Instruction& instr, int32_t relOffset) {
    return static_cast<uint32_t>(static_cast<int32_t>(instr.offset) + relOffset);
}

// Taken target of Jmp/Jcc: operand 0 (Addr8 or Addr32).
static uint32_t jumpTarget(const Instruction& instr) {
    return relativeTarget(instr, instr.operands[0].i32);
}

// SwitchImm default target: operand 2 (Addr32). Case targets are in
// instr.switchTargets, already resolved by the disassembler.
static uint32_t switchDefaultTarget(const Instruction& instr) {
    return relativeTarget(instr, instr.operands[2].i32);
}

static bool isFullSwitch(const Instruction& instr) {
    return instr.operands.size() >= 5;
}

CFGData buildCFG(
    const std::vector<Instruction>&          instrs,
    uint32_t                                 funcBytecodeSize,
    uint32_t                                 version,
    const std::vector<ExceptionHandlerInfo>& handlers)
{
    CFGData cfg;
    if (instrs.empty()) return cfg;

    const OpcodeInfo* table = getOpcodeTable(version);

    // ---- 1. Leaders ---------------------------------------------------------
    std::unordered_set<uint32_t> leaders;
    leaders.insert(instrs[0].offset);

    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < instrs.size() && table; i++) {
        const Instruction& instr = instrs[i];
        const OpcodeInfo& info = table[instr.opcode];
        if (!info.mnemonic || info.jumpKind == JumpKind::None) continue;

        if (i + 1 < instrs.size())
            leaders.insert(instrs[i + 1].offset);

        switch (info.jumpKind) {
            case JumpKind::Unconditional:
            case JumpKind::Conditional:
                leaders.insert(jumpTarget(instr));
                break;

            case JumpKind::Switch:
                if (isFullSwitch(instr)) {
                    leaders.insert(switchDefaultTarget(instr));
                    leaders.insert(instr.switchTargets.begin(), instr.switchTargets.end());
                }
                break;

            case JumpKind::Return:
            case JumpKind::Throw:
            case JumpKind::None:
                break;
        }
    }

    // ---- 2. Blocks ----------------------------------------------------------
    std::vector<uint32_t> leaderVec(leaders.begin(), leaders.end());
    std::sort(leaderVec.begin(), leaderVec.end());

    std::unordered_map<uint32_t, uint32_t> offsetToBlockId;
    offsetToBlockId.reserve(leaderVec.size());
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < leaderVec.size(); i++)
        offsetToBlockId[leaderVec[i]] = i;

    cfg.blocks.resize(leaderVec.size());
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < leaderVec.size(); i++) {
        cfg.blocks[i].id          = i;
        cfg.blocks[i].startOffset = leaderVec[i];
        cfg.blocks[i].endOffset   = (i + 1 < leaderVec.size()) ? leaderVec[i + 1] : funcBytecodeSize;
    }

    uint32_t bIdx = 0;
    for (const auto& instr : instrs) {
        while (bIdx + 1 < cfg.blocks.size() && instr.offset >= cfg.blocks[bIdx + 1].startOffset)
            bIdx++;
        cfg.blocks[bIdx].instructions.push_back(instr);
    }

    // ---- 3. Successors ------------------------------------------------------
    // Edges to offsets that aren't a block start are dropped.
    auto addEdge = [&](uint32_t fromId, uint32_t targetOff, EdgeKind kind) {
        auto it = offsetToBlockId.find(targetOff);
        if (it == offsetToBlockId.end()) return;
        const uint32_t toId = it->second;
        cfg.blocks[fromId].successors.push_back({toId, kind});
        cfg.blocks[toId].predecessors.push_back(fromId);
    };

    for (uint32_t b = 0; b < cfg.blocks.size() && table; b++) {
        const BasicBlock& bb = cfg.blocks[b];
        if (bb.instructions.empty()) continue;

        const Instruction& last = bb.instructions.back();
        const OpcodeInfo& info = table[last.opcode];
        if (!info.mnemonic) continue;

        const bool hasNext = b + 1 < cfg.blocks.size();

        switch (info.jumpKind) {
            case JumpKind::Return:
            case JumpKind::Throw:
                break;  // exit node

            case JumpKind::None:
                if (hasNext)
                    addEdge(b, cfg.blocks[b + 1].startOffset, EdgeKind::FallThrough);
                break;

            case JumpKind::Unconditional:
                addEdge(b, jumpTarget(last), EdgeKind::Jump);
                break;

            case JumpKind::Conditional:
                addEdge(b, jumpTarget(last), EdgeKind::CondTaken);
                if (hasNext)
                    addEdge(b, cfg.blocks[b + 1].startOffset, EdgeKind::CondFallThru);
                break;

            case JumpKind::Switch:
                if (isFullSwitch(last)) {
                    addEdge(b, switchDefaultTarget(last), EdgeKind::SwitchDefault);
                    for (uint32_t caseTarget : last.switchTargets)
                        addEdge(b, caseTarget, EdgeKind::SwitchCase);
                }
                break;
        }
    }

    // ---- 4. Exception handler edges ----------------------------------------
    // Models the implicit transfer on throw; without it catch blocks would be
    // unreachable from the entry.
    for (const auto& eh : handlers) {
        auto catchIt = offsetToBlockId.find(eh.target);
        if (catchIt == offsetToBlockId.end()) continue;
        const uint32_t catchId = catchIt->second;

        for (uint32_t b = 0; b < cfg.blocks.size(); b++) {
            const BasicBlock& bb = cfg.blocks[b];
            if (bb.startOffset >= eh.end || bb.endOffset <= eh.start) continue;  // outside [start, end)
            if (b == catchId) continue;

            const bool already = std::any_of(bb.successors.begin(), bb.successors.end(),
                [&](const CFGEdge& e) {
                    return e.targetId == catchId && e.kind == EdgeKind::ExceptionHandler;
                });
            if (!already)
                addEdge(b, eh.target, EdgeKind::ExceptionHandler);
        }
    }

    // ---- 5. Back-edges ------------------------------------------------------
    enum class Color : uint8_t { White, Gray, Black };
    std::vector<Color> color(cfg.blocks.size(), Color::White);

    std::function<void(uint32_t)> dfs = [&](uint32_t bid) {
        color[bid] = Color::Gray;
        for (auto& edge : cfg.blocks[bid].successors) {
            if (color[edge.targetId] == Color::Gray) {
                edge.kind = EdgeKind::BackEdge;
                cfg.blocks[edge.targetId].isLoopHeader = true;
                cfg.hasLoops = true;
            } else if (color[edge.targetId] == Color::White) {
                dfs(edge.targetId);
            }
        }
        color[bid] = Color::Black;
    };

    dfs(cfg.entryId);

    return cfg;
}

} // namespace hbc

```

```h
// Private header (the CFG types are public, in hbc/hbc.h).
#pragma once

#include "hbc/hbc.h"

namespace hbc {

// Builds a function's CFG from its disassembled instructions (HBCFile::disasm).
//
//   instrs            must come from disassemble() with the file buffer, so that
//                     SwitchImm instructions carry their switchTargets; otherwise
//                     a SwitchImm only gets its SwitchDefault edge
//   funcBytecodeSize  end of the last block
//   version           selects the opcode table (jumpKind)
//   handlers          the function's exception handler table, may be empty
CFGData buildCFG(
    const std::vector<Instruction>&          instrs,
    uint32_t                                 funcBytecodeSize,
    uint32_t                                 version,
    const std::vector<ExceptionHandlerInfo>& handlers = {});
```
