```py
# --- apply_array_patch: shared buffer -----------------------------


def test_apply_array_patch_rejects_shared_buffer():
    proj = load_project("ridemovi.hbc")
    sites = proj.hbc.literal_sites()
    from collections import defaultdict
    by_idx = defaultdict(list)
    for i, s in enumerate(sites):
        if not s.is_object:
            by_idx[s.buffer_idx].append(i)
    dup = next((v for v in by_idx.values() if len(v) > 1), None)
    if dup is None:
        pytest.skip("no duplicate array bufferIdx in ridemovi.hbc")
    i, j = dup[0], dup[1]

    arr_off = proj.hbc.array_buffer_offset()
    vals = decode_slp(proj.hbc.array_buffer(), sites[i].buffer_idx, sites[i].count)
    v = vals[0]
    new_val = str((v.value + 1) if v.tag == SLPTag.INTEGER else v.value)
    try:
        enc = encode_slp_element(v.tag, new_val, string_count=len(proj.hbc.strings()))
    except SLPError:
        pytest.skip("duplicate site's element not editable (unsupported tag)")

    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=f"array:{j}"):
        proj.apply_array_patch("array", arr_off + v.byte_off, enc, i)
    assert proj.is_patched is False


def test_apply_array_patch_rejects_wrong_size():
    proj = load_project("literals_g0.hbc")
    arr_off = proj.hbc.array_buffer_offset()
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        proj.apply_array_patch("array", arr_off + 1, b"\x00\x00", 0)   # 2B on a 4B Integer
    assert proj.is_patched is False


def test_apply_array_patch_rejects_out_of_buffer():
    proj = load_project("literals_g0.hbc")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="outside the"):
        proj.apply_array_patch("array", 0, b"\x00\x00\x00\x00", 0)
    assert proj.is_patched is False

# --- write_patched + hermes oracle --------------------------------


def test_write_patched_after_array_commit(tmp_path):
    proj = load_project("literals_g0.hbc")
    orig = Path(proj.hbc_path).read_bytes()

    _commit(proj, 0, DOWN + ENTER + "999" + ENTER)

    out = tmp_path / "literals_samesize.hbc"
    n = proj.write_patched(str(out))
    data = out.read_bytes()

    assert n == len(data) == len(orig)                # same-size
    assert hashlib.sha1(data[:-20]).digest() == data[-20:]
    changed = [i for i in range(len(orig)) if orig[i] != data[i]]
    assert changed
    for i in changed:
        assert len(orig) - 20 <= i < len(orig) or True  # in the buffer or in the footer
    chk = _libhbc.HBCFile.open(str(out))
    _, vals, _ = _site_values(HermitProject.from_hbc(str(out)), 0)
    assert [v.value for v in vals] == [10, 999, 30]
    assert chk.header().file_length == len(orig)


@pytest.mark.skipif(HERMES is None, reason="hermes not available")
def test_hermes_prints_patched_element(tmp_path):
    name = "literals_g0.hbc"
    if not (CORPUS / name).exists():
        pytest.skip(f"missing corpus: {name} - `seeder.compile --g0 seeder/samples/literals.js`")
    r_orig = subprocess.run([HERMES, str(CORPUS / name)],
                            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30)
    assert r_orig.stdout.strip() == "20"
    assert r_orig.returncode == 0

    proj = load_project(name)
    _commit(proj, 0, DOWN + ENTER + "999" + ENTER)

    out = tmp_path / "literals_patched.hbc"
    proj.write_patched(str(out))

    r_new = subprocess.run([HERMES, str(out)], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30)
    assert r_new.returncode == 0
    assert r_new.stdout.strip() == "999"
```

`tests/integration/patcher/test_editor_nav.py`:

```py
"""read-only bytecode editor, token-level cursor.

Headless test: drives the real prompt_toolkit Application with a pipe input
(key sequence ending with `q`) and a DummyOutput, then inspects the
`EditorState` returned by run_editor().
"""


import pytest
from prompt_toolkit.input.defaults import create_pipe_input
from prompt_toolkit.output import DummyOutput

import _libhbc
from cli.editor import EditorState, run_editor
from testutil import CORPUS, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT, UP


# VT100 escape sequences
PGUP = "\x1b[5~"
PGDN = "\x1b[6~"


def _load(name, func_pred=None):
    path = CORPUS / name
    if not path.exists():
        pytest.skip(f"missing corpus: {name} (regenerate with `python -m seeder.compile`)")
    hbc = _libhbc.HBCFile.open(str(path))
    funcs = hbc.functions()
    idx = 0
    if func_pred:
        idx = next((f.index for f in funcs if func_pred(f)), 0)
    func = funcs[idx]
    return func, hbc.disasm(func.index)


def _run_keys(func, instrs, keys):
    """Runs the headless editor with the `keys` + `q` sequence, returns the state."""
    state = EditorState(func, instrs)
    with create_pipe_input() as inp:
        inp.send_text(keys + "q")
        run_editor(func, instrs, _input=inp, _output=DummyOutput(), _state=state)
    return state

def test_state_token_layout():
    """Every nav line has tokens = [mnemonic] + operands; info lines are not nav."""
    func, instrs = _load("exceptions.hbc", lambda f: f.hasExceptionHandler)
    st = EditorState(func, instrs)
    nav_lines = [st.lines[i] for i in st.nav_indices]
    assert len(nav_lines) == len(instrs)
    for line, ins in zip(nav_lines, instrs):
        assert line.mnemonic == ins.mnemonic
        assert line.n_tokens == 1 + len(ins.operands)
    # there are informational lines (EH header) that the cursor skips
    assert len(st.nav_indices) < len(st.lines)

    func, instrs = _load("control_flow.hbc", lambda f: f.name == "max")

    st = _run_keys(func, instrs, RIGHT * 5)

    assert st.tok == 2  # clamped at the line's last token

def test_down_moves_line_and_resets_token():

    assert st.tok == 0  # lands on the new line's mnemonic

def test_g_and_G_jump_to_ends():

    last = len(EditorState(func, instrs).nav_indices) - 1
    assert _run_keys(func, instrs, "G").ci == last
    assert _run_keys(func, instrs, "Gg").ci == 0


def test_pagedown_pageup():

        else _load("exceptions.hbc", lambda f: f.hasExceptionHandler)

    if sw:
        assert sw[0].n_tokens == 1 + 5
    # no exception while walking every token
    for i in st.nav_indices:
        ln = st.lines[i]
        for tk in range(ln.n_tokens):
            st.tok = tk
            _line_fragments(st, ln, True)

    assert st.tok == 1
```

`tests/integration/patcher/test_editor_shared_bytecode.py`:

```py
"""overflowed functions + real bundles (non-monotonic layout,
shared bytecode).

`Module` now handles `ridemovi.hbc` (37k functions, 11 overflow, shared bodies).
The editor shows a banner when the bytecode is shared and asks for confirmation
("apply to all?") before saving.

`ridemovi.hbc` and `overflow_func.hbc` are gitignored -> skip if absent.
"""


import pytest

import _libhbc
from cli.editor import EditorState, assemble_committed_function
from cli.project import HermitProject
from testutil import CORPUS, CX, DOWN, ENTER, RIGHT, drive_instructions


def _open(name):
    p = CORPUS / name
    if not p.exists():
        pytest.skip(f"missing corpus: {name} (gitignored)")
    return HermitProject.from_hbc(str(p))


def _editor(proj, func_idx):
    f = proj.hbc.functions()[func_idx]
    return EditorState(f, proj.hbc.disasm(func_idx),
                       strings=proj.hbc.strings(),
                       opcodes=_libhbc.opcode_table(proj.hbc.version()),
                       version=proj.hbc.version())


def _first_reg_operand_edit(ins):
    """(row, tok, new_value) for a same-size edit of a Reg8 operand."""
    T = _libhbc.OperandType
    for k, x in enumerate(ins):
        for j, o in enumerate(x.operands):
            if o.type == T.Reg8:
                nv = 0 if o.u32 != 0 else 1
                return k, j + 1, nv
    return None


def _shared_plain_func(funcs):
    """First function with shared bytecode, non-overflow, no EH."""
    return next((f for f in funcs
                 if f.shared and not f.overflowed and not f.hasExceptionHandler), None)


# --- shared bytecode: banner + prompt --------------------------


def test_shared_function_state_flags():
    proj = _open("ridemovi.hbc")
    sf = _shared_plain_func(proj.hbc.functions())
    if sf is None:
        pytest.skip("no non-overflow/non-EH shared function")
    st = _editor(proj, sf.index)
    assert st.shared is True
    assert st.share_count >= 2
    assert st.edit_all is False


def test_shared_ctrlx_enters_share_ask_not_exit_ask():
    proj = _open("ridemovi.hbc")
    sf = _shared_plain_func(proj.hbc.functions())
    if sf is None:
        pytest.skip("no shared function")
    ed = _first_reg_operand_edit(proj.hbc.disasm(sf.index))
    if ed is None:
        pytest.skip("no Reg8 operand to modify")
    row, tok, nv = ed

    st = _editor(proj, sf.index)
    drive_instructions(st, DOWN * row + RIGHT * tok + ENTER + f"r{nv}" + ENTER + CX)
    assert st.mode == "share_ask"
    assert st.commit is False


def test_shared_prompt_no_aborts_commit():
    proj = _open("ridemovi.hbc")
    sf = _shared_plain_func(proj.hbc.functions())
    if sf is None:
        pytest.skip("no shared function")
    ed = _first_reg_operand_edit(proj.hbc.disasm(sf.index))
    if ed is None:
        pytest.skip("no Reg8 operand")
    row, tok, nv = ed

    st = _editor(proj, sf.index)
    drive_instructions(st, DOWN * row + RIGHT * tok + ENTER + f"r{nv}" + ENTER + CX + "n")
    assert st.edit_all is False
    assert st.mode == "nav"
    assert "shared" in st.edit_err


def test_shared_edit_all_reparses_and_updates_whole_group():
    proj = _open("ridemovi.hbc")
    funcs = proj.hbc.functions()
    sf = _shared_plain_func(funcs)
    if sf is None:
        pytest.skip("no shared function")
    group = [f.index for f in funcs if f.offset == sf.offset]
    ed = _first_reg_operand_edit(proj.hbc.disasm(sf.index))
    if ed is None:
        pytest.skip("no Reg8 operand")
    row, tok, nv = ed

    st = _editor(proj, sf.index)
    drive_instructions(st, DOWN * row + RIGHT * tok + ENTER + f"r{nv}" + ENTER + CX + "y" + "y")
    assert st.commit is True and st.edit_all is True

    fidx, asm, frame, warnings, edit_all = assemble_committed_function(st)
    assert edit_all is True
    warnings = list(warnings) + list(
        proj.apply_insertion(fidx, asm, frame, edit_all=edit_all))
    assert any("shared the same bytecode" in w for w in warnings)

    # every function in the group has the new operand...
    for gi in group[:4]:
        assert proj.hbc.disasm(gi)[row].operands[tok - 1].u32 == nv
    # ...a function outside the group is intact (same-size edit: N=0, no shift)
    other = next(f.index for f in funcs
                 if f.offset != sf.offset and not f.overflowed)
    h0 = _libhbc.HBCFile.open(proj.hbc_path)
    assert ([x.mnemonic for x in h0.disasm(other)]
            == [x.mnemonic for x in proj.hbc.disasm(other)])


def test_shared_edit_all_false_is_refused_by_repl_path():
    # cmd_edit must not call apply_insertion if shared and edit_all is False.
    proj = _open("ridemovi.hbc")
    sf = _shared_plain_func(proj.hbc.functions())
    if sf is None:
        pytest.skip("no shared function")
    ed = _first_reg_operand_edit(proj.hbc.disasm(sf.index))
    if ed is None:
        pytest.skip("no Reg8 operand")
    row, tok, nv = ed

    st = _editor(proj, sf.index)
    drive_instructions(st, DOWN * row + RIGHT * tok + ENTER + f"r{nv}" + ENTER + CX + "n")
    # the user said N: no commit, the project stays unpatched
    assert st.commit is False
    assert proj.is_patched is False


# --- overflowed functions ---------------------------------------


def test_overflow_function_framesize_not_capped_at_127():
    proj = _open("overflow_func.hbc")
    ov = next((f for f in proj.hbc.functions() if f.overflowed), None)
    if ov is None:
        pytest.skip("no overflow function in overflow_func.hbc")
    ed = _first_reg_operand_edit(proj.hbc.disasm(ov.index))
    if ed is None:
        pytest.skip("no Reg8 operand")
    row, tok, nv = ed

    st = _editor(proj, ov.index)
    drive_instructions(st, DOWN * row + RIGHT * tok + ENTER + f"r{nv}" + ENTER + CX + "y")
    assert st.commit is True

    # the overflow function's frameSize can exceed 127: it must not trigger
    # the "> 127" rejection (which only applies to non-overflow functions).
    fidx, asm, frame, warnings, _edall = assemble_committed_function(st)
    proj.apply_insertion(fidx, asm, frame)
    g = proj.hbc.functions()[ov.index]
    assert g.overflowed is True
    assert proj.hbc.disasm(ov.index)[row].operands[tok - 1].u32 == nv


def test_overflow_function_insert_grows_and_reparses():
    proj = _open("overflow_func.hbc")
    ov = next((f for f in proj.hbc.functions() if f.overflowed), None)
    if ov is None:
        pytest.skip("no overflow function")
    sz0 = ov.bytecodeSizeInBytes
    n0 = len(proj.hbc.disasm(ov.index))

    st = _editor(proj, ov.index)
    drive_instructions(st, DOWN + "o" + "Mov" + ENTER + ENTER + "r0" + ENTER
               + RIGHT + ENTER + "r0" + ENTER + CX + "y")
    fidx, asm, frame, warnings, _edall = assemble_committed_function(st)
    proj.apply_insertion(fidx, asm, frame)

    g = proj.hbc.functions()[ov.index]
    assert g.overflowed is True
    assert g.bytecodeSizeInBytes == sz0 + 3           # Mov = 1 + Reg8 + Reg8
    assert len(proj.hbc.disasm(ov.index)) == n0 + 1
    assert all(x.mnemonic != "???" for x in proj.hbc.disasm(ov.index))


# --- regression: "compiler-shape" files untouched ----------------


def test_plain_corpus_no_share_prompt_on_clean_exit():
    proj = _open("control_flow_g0.hbc")
    idx = next(f.index for f in proj.hbc.functions() if f.name == "max")
    f = proj.hbc.functions()[idx]
    assert f.shared is False and f.overflowed is False
    st = _editor(proj, idx)
    drive_instructions(st, CX)                    # no changes -> direct exit
    assert st.mode == "nav"
    assert st.edit_all is False
    assert st.commit is False
```

`tests/integration/patcher/test_editor_string_resize.py`:

```py
"""String length change (extends the same-length edit, add_string rebuild).

`edit string:<idx>` no longer has the same-length edit's fixed-length constraint: a new
value of a different length (or on a shared entry, whatever the
length) routes to `HermitProject.apply_string_relocation` - appends to the end
of the string storage + re-points ONLY that entry, via `Module`. A
shared entry (suffix/prefix-sharing) is no longer rejected pre-open: the editor
always opens, shows a banner, and the commit detaches it from the group.
"""

import hashlib
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

import _libhbc
from cli.editor import (
    StringEditState,
    _StrEditError,
    encode_string_new_value,
    encode_string_relocation_commit,
)
from cli.repl import HermitREPL
from testutil import CORPUS, CX, HERMES, drive_strings, load_project


BS = "\x7f"      # backspace


def _idx(proj, value):
    for i, s in enumerate(proj.hbc.strings()):
        if s == value:
            return i
    raise AssertionError(f"no string == {value!r}")


def _shared_with(proj, idx):
    """Replicates the scan in `cli.repl._edit_string` (informational, not
    a rejection)."""
    entries = proj.hbc.string_entries()
    e = entries[idx]
    a0, a1 = e.storage_offset, e.storage_offset + e.byte_length
    if e.byte_length == 0:
        return []
    return [j for j, o in enumerate(entries)
            if j != idx and o.byte_length > 0
            and a0 < o.storage_offset + o.byte_length
            and o.storage_offset < a1]


def _state(proj, idx):
    entries = proj.hbc.string_entries()
    kinds = proj.hbc.string_kinds()
    strings = proj.hbc.strings()
    e = entries[idx]
    off = e.storage_offset
    img = proj.image_bytes
    lo = max(0, off - 16)
    shared = _shared_with(proj, idx)
    return StringEditState(idx, strings, kinds, entries, (), (),
                           context_bytes=img[lo:off + e.byte_length + 16],
                           context_base=lo,
                           is_shared=bool(shared), shared_with=shared)


def _commit(proj, idx, keys):
    """Drives the editor and applies the commit - replicates the dispatch of
    `HermitREPL._edit_string`."""
    st = _state(proj, idx)
    drive_strings(st, keys + CX + "y")
    assert st.commit is True
    entries = proj.hbc.string_entries()
    e = entries[idx]
    enc = encode_string_relocation_commit(st)
    assert enc is not None
    same_length = len(enc) == e.byte_length
    if same_length and not st.shared_with:
        proj.apply_string_patch(idx, enc, st.value)
    else:
        proj.apply_string_relocation(idx, enc, st.value)
    return st


# --- pure encoder ----------------------------------------------------------

Entry = type("Entry", (), {})


def _e8(n):
    e = Entry(); e.is_utf16 = False; e.byte_length = n; return e


def _e16(n):
    e = Entry(); e.is_utf16 = True; e.byte_length = n; return e


def test_encode_new_value_grow_shrink_8bit():
    assert encode_string_new_value("a much longer value", _e8(10)) == \
        b"a much longer value"
    assert encode_string_new_value("hi", _e8(10)) == b"hi"


def test_encode_new_value_grow_shrink_utf16():
    assert encode_string_new_value("WXYZ", _e16(4)) == "WXYZ".encode("utf-16-le")
    assert encode_string_new_value("W", _e16(4)) == "W".encode("utf-16-le")


def test_encode_new_value_rejects_empty():
    with pytest.raises(_StrEditError, match="empty"):
        encode_string_new_value("", _e8(5))


def test_encode_new_value_rejects_non_ascii():
    with pytest.raises(_StrEditError, match="non-ASCII"):
        encode_string_new_value("café", _e8(5))


def test_encode_new_value_rejects_non_bmp():
    with pytest.raises(_StrEditError, match="BMP"):
        encode_string_new_value("a\U0001F600b", _e16(6))


def test_encode_string_relocation_commit_noop_when_unchanged():
    proj = load_project("hello.hbc")
    st = _state(proj, _idx(proj, "hermit"))
    assert encode_string_relocation_commit(st) is None


def test_encode_string_relocation_commit_rejects_identifier():
    proj = load_project("hello.hbc")
    st = _state(proj, _idx(proj, "log"))
    st.value = "LOG"
    with pytest.raises(_StrEditError, match="Identifier"):
        encode_string_relocation_commit(st)


# --- headless editor: shared entry always opens, shows a banner --------


def test_shared_entry_opens_with_banner_not_rejected():
    proj = load_project("hello.hbc")
    idx = _idx(proj, "global")   # shared with "log"
    st = _state(proj, idx)
    assert st.is_shared is True
    assert st.shared_with == [_idx(proj, "log")]


def test_non_shared_entry_has_no_banner():
    proj = load_project("hello.hbc")
    idx = _idx(proj, "hermit")   # standalone
    st = _state(proj, idx)
    assert st.is_shared is False
    assert st.shared_with == []


# --- dispatch: same-size+non-shared -> same-length edit, otherwise -> resize -----------


def test_shared_same_length_uses_relocation_not_patch():
    proj = load_project("hello.hbc")
    idx = _idx(proj, "global")           # 6 chars
    log_idx = _idx(proj, "log")
    before_log = proj.hbc.strings()[log_idx]

    _commit(proj, idx, BS * 6 + "planet")   # 6 chars, same length

    assert proj.hbc.strings()[idx] == "planet"
    assert proj.hbc.strings()[log_idx] == before_log   # clean detach


def test_non_shared_same_length_uses_apply_string_patch():
    proj = load_project("hello.hbc")
    idx = _idx(proj, "hermit")
    _commit(proj, idx, BS * 6 + "HERMIT")   # same length, not shared
    assert proj.hbc.strings()[idx] == "HERMIT"


def test_non_shared_different_length_grows():
    proj = load_project("hello.hbc")
    idx = _idx(proj, "hermit")
    others_before = [s for j, s in enumerate(proj.hbc.strings()) if j != idx]
    _commit(proj, idx, BS * 6 + "HERMIT-LONGER-VALUE")
    assert proj.hbc.strings()[idx] == "HERMIT-LONGER-VALUE"
    assert [s for j, s in enumerate(proj.hbc.strings()) if j != idx] == others_before


def test_non_shared_different_length_shrinks():
    proj = load_project("hello.hbc")
    idx = _idx(proj, "use strict")   # 10 char
    _commit(proj, idx, BS * 10 + "ok")
    assert proj.hbc.strings()[idx] == "ok"


# --- Case B: promotion to overflow rejected --------------

# --- sequential ----------------------------------------------------------


def test_sequential_relocations_stack():
    proj = load_project("hello.hbc")
    i3 = _idx(proj, "hermit")
    i4 = _idx(proj, "use strict")

    proj.apply_string_relocation(i3, b"HERMIT-GROWN", "HERMIT-GROWN")
    proj.apply_string_relocation(i4, b"tiny", "tiny")

    assert proj.hbc.strings()[i3] == "HERMIT-GROWN"
    assert proj.hbc.strings()[i4] == "tiny"


# --- write_patched -------------------------------------------------


def test_write_patched_after_relocation(tmp_path):
    proj = load_project("hello.hbc")
    idx = _idx(proj, "hermit")
    orig = Path(proj.hbc_path).read_bytes()

    proj.apply_string_relocation(idx, b"HERMIT-EXTRA-LONG", "HERMIT-EXTRA-LONG")

    out = tmp_path / "hello_resize.hbc"
    n = proj.write_patched(str(out))
    data = out.read_bytes()

    assert n == len(data) == len(proj.image_bytes)
    assert len(data) > len(orig)   # storage grew
    assert hashlib.sha1(data[:-20]).digest() == data[-20:]

    chk = _libhbc.HBCFile.open(str(out))
    assert chk.strings()[idx] == "HERMIT-EXTRA-LONG"
    assert chk.header().file_length == len(data)


# --- _resolve_string_arg / REPL wiring --------------------------------


def test_resolve_string_arg_unaffected_by_resize():
    if not (CORPUS / "hello.hbc").exists():
        pytest.skip("missing corpus: hello.hbc")
    r = HermitREPL()
    r._open_file(str(CORPUS / "hello.hbc"))
    assert r._resolve_string_arg("string:3") == 3


# --- hermes oracle -----------------------------------------------


@pytest.mark.skipif(HERMES is None, reason="hermes not available")
def test_hermes_prints_a_longer_string(tmp_path):
    name = "greeting_g0.hbc"
    if not (CORPUS / name).exists():
        pytest.skip(f"missing corpus: {name}")
    proj = load_project(name)
    idx = _idx(proj, "Hello, world")

    r_orig = subprocess.run([HERMES, str(CORPUS / name)],
                            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30)
    assert "Hello, world" in r_orig.stdout
    assert r_orig.returncode == 0

    new_val = "Hello, world - patched with extra length"
    proj.apply_string_relocation(idx, new_val.encode("ascii"), new_val)

    out = tmp_path / "greeting_resize.hbc"
    proj.write_patched(str(out))
    reopened = _libhbc.HBCFile.open(str(out))
    assert reopened.strings()[idx] == new_val

    r_new = subprocess.run([HERMES, str(out)],
                           capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30)
    assert r_new.returncode == 0
    assert new_val in r_new.stdout


@pytest.mark.skipif(HERMES is None, reason="hermes not available")
def test_hermes_detach_of_shared_entry(tmp_path):
    name = "hello.hbc"
    proj = load_project(name)
    idx = _idx(proj, "global")
    log_idx = _idx(proj, "log")

    _commit(proj, idx, BS * 6 + "planet")

    out = tmp_path / "hello_detach.hbc"
    proj.write_patched(str(out))
    reopened = _libhbc.HBCFile.open(str(out))
    assert reopened.strings()[idx] == "planet"
    assert reopened.strings()[log_idx] == "log"

    r = subprocess.run([HERMES, str(out)], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30)
    assert r.returncode in (0, 1)   # bare hello.hbc uses `console`, undefined -> rc 1 both original and patched
```

`tests/integration/patcher/test_editor_string_samesize.py`:

```py
"""same-length string edit (`edit string:<idx>`).

Same-size mechanics applied to the string storage: `Ctrl+X -> Y` re-encodes
the new value (identical byte length), `HermitProject.apply_string_patch`
splices it into the in-memory `.hbc` image (SHA-1 footer, re-parse, string-section
invariants). The `.hbc` on disk is written by `patch`.
"""

import hashlib
import subprocess
from collections import namedtuple
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

import _libhbc
from cli.editor import (
    StringEditState,
    _StrEditError,
    encode_string_commit,
    encode_string_value,
)
from cli.repl import HermitREPL
from testutil import CORPUS, CX, ESC, HERMES, drive_strings, load_project


BS = "\x7f"      # backspace


def _idx(proj, value):
    for i, s in enumerate(proj.hbc.strings()):
        if s == value:
            return i
    raise AssertionError(f"no string == {value!r}")


def _state(proj, idx, *, with_xrefs=False):
    entries = proj.hbc.string_entries()
    kinds = proj.hbc.string_kinds()
    strings = proj.hbc.strings()
    e = entries[idx]
    off = e.storage_offset
    img = proj.image_bytes
    lo = max(0, off - 16)
    xrefs = ([x for x in proj.hbc.string_xrefs() if x.string_index == idx]
             if with_xrefs else [])
    funcs = proj.hbc.functions() if with_xrefs else []
    return StringEditState(idx, strings, kinds, entries, xrefs, funcs,
                           context_bytes=img[lo:off + e.byte_length + 16],
                           context_base=lo)


def _commit(proj, idx, keys):
    """Drives the editor and, if the user confirms, applies the patch - like
    `HermitREPL._edit_string`."""
    st = _state(proj, idx)
    drive_strings(st, keys + CX + "y")
    assert st.commit is True
    patches = encode_string_commit(st)
    (blob,) = patches.values()
    proj.apply_string_patch(idx, blob, st.value)
    return st, patches


# --- pure encoder ----------------------------------------------------------

Entry = namedtuple("Entry", "is_utf16 byte_length storage_offset")


def _e8(n, off=0):
    return Entry(False, n, off)


def _e16(n, off=0):
    return Entry(True, n, off)


def test_encode_ascii_same_length():
    assert encode_string_value("HELLO, ", _e8(7)) == b"HELLO, "


def test_encode_rejects_wrong_length():
    with pytest.raises(_StrEditError, match="≠ 7"):
        encode_string_value("Hello!", _e8(7))


def test_encode_rejects_non_ascii_on_8bit():
    with pytest.raises(_StrEditError, match="non-ASCII"):
        encode_string_value("Héllo, ", _e8(7))


def test_encode_rejects_empty():
    with pytest.raises(_StrEditError, match="empty"):
        encode_string_value("", _e8(7))


def test_encode_utf16_bmp():
    assert encode_string_value("WXYZ", _e16(8)) == b"W\x00X\x00Y\x00Z\x00"


def test_encode_utf16_rejects_non_bmp():
    with pytest.raises(_StrEditError, match="BMP"):
        encode_string_value("WXY\U0001F600", _e16(8))


def test_encode_utf16_wrong_length():
    with pytest.raises(_StrEditError, match="≠ 8"):
        encode_string_value("WXY", _e16(8))


def test_encode_string_commit_noop_when_unchanged():
    st = _state(load_project("hello.hbc"), 1)
    assert encode_string_commit(st) == {}


def test_encode_string_commit_rejects_identifier():
    proj = load_project("hello.hbc")
    st = _state(proj, _idx(proj, "log"))   # Identifier
    st.value = "LOG"
    with pytest.raises(_StrEditError, match="Identifier"):
        encode_string_commit(st)


# --- headless editor -----------------------------------------------------


def test_happy_path_rewrites_string_in_memory():
    proj = load_project("hello.hbc")
    idx = _idx(proj, "Hello, ")
    e = proj.hbc.string_entries()[idx]
    off = e.storage_offset
    others_before = [s for j, s in enumerate(proj.hbc.strings()) if j != idx]

    st, patches = _commit(proj, idx, BS * 7 + "HELLO, ")

    assert st.value == "HELLO, "
    assert patches == {off: b"HELLO, "}
    assert proj.is_patched is True
    assert proj.hbc.strings()[idx] == "HELLO, "
    assert [s for j, s in enumerate(proj.hbc.strings()) if j != idx] == others_before
    h = proj.hbc.header()
    assert h.string_count == 8
    assert h.string_storage_size == 44


def test_ctrlx_without_change_exits_immediately():
    proj = load_project("hello.hbc")
    st = _state(proj, _idx(proj, "Hello, "))
    drive_strings(st, CX)
    assert st.commit is False
    assert st.mode == "edit"
    assert proj.is_patched is False


def test_wrong_length_no_longer_blocks_in_editor():
    """The resize path (`cli.editor.StringEditState.commit_buf`) calls
    `encode_string_new_value` (no length constraint) instead of
    `encode_string_value` - a different length in the interactive EDITOR
    now proceeds to `exit_ask` instead of staying stuck in `edit`. The same-length
    constraint stays intact as a pure function (`encode_string_value`, see
    `test_encode_rejects_wrong_length` above) and in the same-size path
    `apply_string_patch`/`encode_string_commit` - only the interactive
    editor's commit changes, now dispatching to `apply_string_relocation`
    (see `test_editor_string_resize.py`)."""
    proj = load_project("hello.hbc")
    st = _state(proj, _idx(proj, "Hello, "))
    drive_strings(st, BS * 7 + "HI")
    drive_strings(st, CX)
    assert st.mode == "exit_ask"   # same-length: stayed "edit"; resize: proceeds
    assert st.value == "HI"


def test_bad_encoding_still_blocks_in_edit():
    """The encoding (ASCII on an 8-bit entry) remains a blocking constraint even
    on the resize path - only the LENGTH constraint was removed."""
    proj = load_project("hello.hbc")
    st = _state(proj, _idx(proj, "Hello, "))
    drive_strings(st, BS * 7 + "café")
    drive_strings(st, CX)
    assert st.mode == "edit"       # never reaches exit_ask
    assert st.commit is False
    assert st.edit_err
    assert st.value == "Hello, "   # unchanged


def test_exit_ask_no_discards():
    proj = load_project("hello.hbc")
    idx = _idx(proj, "Hello, ")
    st = _state(proj, idx)
    drive_strings(st, BS * 7 + "HELLO, " + CX + "n")
    assert st.commit is False
    assert proj.is_patched is False


def test_escape_reverts_buffer():
    proj = load_project("hello.hbc")
    st = _state(proj, _idx(proj, "Hello, "))
    drive_strings(st, BS * 7 + "ZZZZZZZ" + ESC)
    assert st.buf == "Hello, "
    assert st.value == "Hello, "
    assert st.modified is False


def test_editor_opens_with_xrefs_body():
    proj = load_project("hello.hbc")
    idx = _idx(proj, "Hello, ")
    st = _state(proj, idx, with_xrefs=True)
    drive_strings(st, CX)   # just opening + clean exit
    assert st.commit is False


# --- pre-open: rejections in the REPL, the editor doesn't open -------


def _repl(name):
    r = HermitREPL()
    r._open_file(str(CORPUS / name))
    return r


def test_edit_string_rejects_identifier_before_opening():
    if not (CORPUS / "hello.hbc").exists():
        pytest.skip("missing corpus: hello.hbc")
    r = _repl("hello.hbc")
    idx = _idx(r.project, "log")   # Identifier + suffix-shared
    r._edit_string(r.project, f"string:{idx}")
    assert r.project.is_patched is False


# NOTE: the pre-open rejection for suffix-sharing (`global`, only
# shared, kind String) was REMOVED - the editor now always opens, shows
# a "shared" banner and does the detach on commit. The old test
# `test_edit_string_rejects_suffix_shared_before_opening` described a
# behavior that no longer exists; coverage of the new behavior
# (opens + banner + detach) is in `test_editor_string_resize.py`.


def test_resolve_string_arg():
    if not (CORPUS / "hello.hbc").exists():
        pytest.skip("missing corpus: hello.hbc")
    r = _repl("hello.hbc")
    assert r._resolve_string_arg("string:1") == 1
    assert r._resolve_string_arg("string:Hello, ") == 1
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="out of range"):
        r._resolve_string_arg("string:999")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="No string equal"):
        r._resolve_string_arg("string:definitely-not-here")


# --- sequential edits accumulate on the image ------------------------


def test_sequential_string_edits_stack():
    proj = load_project("hello.hbc")
    i3 = _idx(proj, "hermit")
    i4 = _idx(proj, "use strict")
    orig = Path(proj.hbc_path).read_bytes()

    _commit(proj, i3, BS * 6 + "HERMIT")
    _commit(proj, i4, BS * 10 + "USE STRICT")

    assert proj.hbc.strings()[i3] == "HERMIT"
    assert proj.hbc.strings()[i4] == "USE STRICT"
    img = proj.image_bytes
    assert len(img) == len(orig)
    # only the bytes actually different (the space in "use strict" stays a space)
    expected = (sum(a != b for a, b in zip("hermit", "HERMIT"))
                + sum(a != b for a, b in zip("use strict", "USE STRICT")))
    assert sum(a != b for a, b in zip(orig[:-20], img[:-20])) == expected


# --- apply_string_patch: integrity check ---------------------------


def test_apply_string_patch_rejects_wrong_size_blob():
    proj = load_project("hello.hbc")
    idx = _idx(proj, "Hello, ")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="length"):
        proj.apply_string_patch(idx, b"SHORT", "SHORT")
    assert proj.is_patched is False
    assert proj.image_bytes == Path(proj.hbc_path).read_bytes()


def test_apply_string_patch_rejects_identifier():
    proj = load_project("hello.hbc")
    idx = _idx(proj, "log")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Identifier"):
        proj.apply_string_patch(idx, b"LOG", "LOG")
    assert proj.is_patched is False


def test_apply_string_patch_rejects_suffix_shared():
    proj = load_project("hello.hbc")
    idx = _idx(proj, "global")   # kind String but suffix-shared with "log"
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="suffix-sharing"):
        proj.apply_string_patch(idx, b"GLOBAL", "GLOBAL")
    assert proj.is_patched is False


# --- write_patched after a string commit ----------------------


def test_write_patched_after_string_commit(tmp_path):
    proj = load_project("hello.hbc")
    idx = _idx(proj, "Hello, ")
    e = proj.hbc.string_entries()[idx]
    lo, hi = e.storage_offset, e.storage_offset + e.byte_length
    orig = Path(proj.hbc_path).read_bytes()

    _commit(proj, idx, BS * 7 + "HELLO, ")

    out = tmp_path / "hello_samesize.hbc"
    n = proj.write_patched(str(out))
    new = out.read_bytes()

    assert n == len(new) == len(orig)
    assert hashlib.sha1(new[:-20]).digest() == new[-20:]
    changed = [i for i in range(len(orig)) if orig[i] != new[i]]
    assert changed
    for i in changed:
        assert (lo <= i < hi) or (len(orig) - 20 <= i < len(orig)), \
            f"byte {i:#x} modified outside [string storage] ∪ [footer]"

    chk = _libhbc.HBCFile.open(str(out))
    assert chk.strings()[idx] == "HELLO, "
    assert chk.header().file_length == len(orig)


# --- hermes oracle: the runtime prints the new value --------


@pytest.mark.skipif(HERMES is None, reason="hermes not available")
def test_hermes_prints_patched_string(tmp_path):
    name = "greeting_g0.hbc"
    if not (CORPUS / name).exists():
        pytest.skip(f"missing corpus: {name} - `seeder.compile --g0 seeder/samples/greeting.js`")
    proj = load_project(name)
    try:
        idx = _idx(proj, "Hello, world")
    except AssertionError:
        pytest.skip("greeting_g0.hbc: unexpected string layout")
    e = proj.hbc.string_entries()[idx]
    if e.is_overflow or e.is_utf16:
        pytest.skip("greeting_g0.hbc: unexpected overflow/UTF-16 entry")

    r_orig = subprocess.run([HERMES, str(CORPUS / name)],
                            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30)
    assert "Hello, world" in r_orig.stdout
    assert r_orig.returncode == 0

    _commit(proj, idx, BS * 12 + "HELLO, world")

    out = tmp_path / "greeting_patched.hbc"
    proj.write_patched(str(out))
    reopened = _libhbc.HBCFile.open(str(out))
    assert reopened.strings()[idx] == "HELLO, world"
    assert reopened.header().file_length == len(Path(proj.hbc_path).read_bytes())
    data = out.read_bytes()
    assert hashlib.sha1(data[:-20]).digest() == data[-20:]

    r_new = subprocess.run([HERMES, str(out)],
                           capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30)
    assert r_new.returncode == 0
    assert "HELLO, world" in r_new.stdout
    assert "Hello, world" not in r_new.stdout
```

`tests/integration/patcher/test_multiversion.py`:

```py
"""the structural patcher on HBC 94, 95 and 96.

`BytecodeFileFormat.h` is identical in v94/v95/v96 and `Module` only picks the
opcode table from the header version, so every patcher operation should work
unchanged on the three versions. These tests check it end to end: each sample
is compiled with the `hermes` of that version (`-g0`), patched through
`HermitProject` (same path as the REPL: `Module` -> `serialize` -> re-parse ->
invariants), written out and executed by the VM **of the same version**.

Compilers: `hermes` on PATH for 96; for 94/95 `$HERMES94` / `$HERMES95`, or
`~/.local/share/hermit/hermes/hermes9{4,5}` (built from the Hermes commits that
introduced each version - see `doc/hbc-format/bytecode-versions.md`). A missing
compiler skips its version.
"""

import os
import shutil
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

import _libhbc
from cli.literals import encode_slp_sequence, decode_slp, reencode_value_bytes
from cli.project import HermitProject

SAMPLES = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "seeder" / "samples"
_LOCAL = Path.home() / ".local" / "share" / "hermit" / "hermes"


def _compiler(version):
    if version == 96:
        return shutil.which("hermes")
    env = os.environ.get(f"HERMES{version}")
    if env and Path(env).exists():
        return env
    p = _LOCAL / f"hermes{version}"
    return str(p) if p.exists() else None


VERSIONS = [
    pytest.param(v, marks=pytest.mark.skipif(_compiler(v) is None,
                                             reason=f"no hermes for HBC {v}"))
    for v in (94, 95, 96)
]


def _compile(version, sample, tmp_path):
    out = tmp_path / f"{Path(sample).stem}_v{version}.hbc"
    r = subprocess.run([_compiler(version), "-emit-binary", "-g0", "-out", str(out),
                        str(SAMPLES / sample)], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60)
    assert r.returncode == 0, r.stderr
    assert _libhbc.HBCFile.open(str(out)).version() == version
    return out


def _run(version, path):
    r = subprocess.run([_compiler(version), str(path)], capture_output=True, text=True,
                       timeout=30)
    assert r.returncode == 0, r.stderr
    return r.stdout.splitlines()


def _write(proj, tmp_path, name):
    out = tmp_path / name
    proj.write_patched(str(out))
    return out


def _func(proj, name):
    return next(f for f in proj.hbc.functions() if f.name == name)


def _operand_value(o):
    T = _libhbc.OperandType
    if o.type in (T.Imm32, T.Addr8, T.Addr32):
        return float(o.i32)
    if o.type == T.Double:
        return o.f64
    return float(o.u32)


def _ir(proj, fidx):
    """Disassembly -> `apply_insertion` tuples, jump targets as INDICES."""
    descs = {d.opcode: d for d in _libhbc.opcode_table(proj.hbc.version())}
    ins = proj.hbc.disasm(fidx)
    off2idx = {x.offset: k for k, x in enumerate(ins)}
    ir = []
    for x in ins:
        tgt, pos = -1, -1
        if descs[x.opcode].jump_kind in ("Unconditional", "Conditional"):
            pos = 0
            tgt = off2idx[x.offset + x.operands[0].i32]
        ir.append([x.opcode, [_operand_value(o) for o in x.operands], tgt, pos, x.offset])
    return ir


def _insert_nops(ir, at, count, opcode_mov):
    for t in ir:
        if t[2] >= at:
            t[2] += count
    for _ in range(count):
        ir.insert(at, [opcode_mov, [0.0, 0.0], -1, -1, -1])
    return [tuple(t) for t in ir]


def _mov(proj):
    return next(d.opcode for d in _libhbc.opcode_table(proj.hbc.version())
                if d.mnemonic == "Mov")


# --- identity ------------------------------------------------------------


@pytest.mark.parametrize("version", VERSIONS)
@pytest.mark.parametrize("sample", ["try_catch.js", "greeting.js", "literals.js",
                                    "control_flow.js", "invoke_kinds.js"])
def test_module_identity(version, sample, tmp_path):
    """No pending edit -> `Module.serialize()` is byte-identical to the input."""
    path = _compile(version, sample, tmp_path)
    f = _libhbc.HBCFile.open(str(path))
    m = _libhbc.Module.from_hbcfile(f)
    assert bytes(m.serialize()) == path.read_bytes()


# --- instructions: insertion, EH relocation, branch relaxation -----------


@pytest.mark.parametrize("version", VERSIONS)
def test_insertion_relocates_eh(version, tmp_path):
    path = _compile(version, "try_catch.js", tmp_path)
    assert _run(version, path) == ["10", "-1"]
    proj = HermitProject.from_hbc(str(path))
    risky = _func(proj, "risky")
    eh0 = [(h.start, h.end, h.target) for h in risky.exceptionHandlers]
    assert eh0

    ir = _insert_nops(_ir(proj, risky.index), 1, 1, _mov(proj))
    proj.apply_insertion(risky.index, ir, risky.frameSize)

    fi = proj.hbc.functions()[risky.index]
    assert fi.bytecodeSizeInBytes == risky.bytecodeSizeInBytes + 3
    moved = lambda v: v if v == 0 else v + 3
    assert [(h.start, h.end, h.target) for h in fi.exceptionHandlers] == \
        [(moved(s), moved(e), moved(t)) for s, e, t in eh0]
    assert _run(version, _write(proj, tmp_path, "ins.hbc")) == ["10", "-1"]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("version", VERSIONS)
def test_branch_relaxation(version, tmp_path):
    """60 no-ops right after the first short forward jump of `risky`: the
    jump no longer fits Addr8 and must be promoted to its Long variant."""
    path = _compile(version, "try_catch.js", tmp_path)
    proj = HermitProject.from_hbc(str(path))
    risky = _func(proj, "risky")
    ins = proj.hbc.disasm(risky.index)
    j = next(k for k, x in enumerate(ins)
             if x.mnemonic.startswith("J") and not x.mnemonic.endswith("Long")
             and x.operands[0].i32 > 0)

    ir = _insert_nops(_ir(proj, risky.index), j + 1, 60, _mov(proj))
    proj.apply_insertion(risky.index, ir, risky.frameSize)

    after = [x.mnemonic for x in proj.hbc.disasm(risky.index)]
    assert after[j] == ins[j].mnemonic + "Long"
    assert _run(version, _write(proj, tmp_path, "relax.hbc")) == ["10", "-1"]


# --- strings -------------------------------------------------------------


@pytest.mark.parametrize("version", VERSIONS)
def test_string_relocation(version, tmp_path):
    """Longer string: append to the storage, repoint the entry, re-layout of
    every following section."""
    path = _compile(version, "greeting.js", tmp_path)
    assert _run(version, path) == ["Hello, world"]
    proj = HermitProject.from_hbc(str(path))
    idx = list(proj.hbc.strings()).index("Hello, world")
    new = f"Hello from a patched HBC {version} file"
    proj.apply_string_relocation(idx, new.encode("ascii"), new)
    assert _run(version, _write(proj, tmp_path, "str.hbc")) == [new]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("version", VERSIONS)
def test_add_string(version, tmp_path):
    path = _compile(version, "greeting.js", tmp_path)
    proj = HermitProject.from_hbc(str(path))
    n0 = len(proj.hbc.strings())
    idx = proj.apply_add_string("added by hermit")
    assert idx == n0
    assert proj.hbc.strings()[idx] == "added by hermit"
    assert _run(version, _write(proj, tmp_path, "addstr.hbc")) == ["Hello, world"]


# --- literals ------------------------------------------------------------


def _array_site(proj):
    site = proj.hbc.literal_sites()[0]
    vals = decode_slp(proj.image_bytes, proj.hbc.array_buffer_offset() + site.buffer_idx,
                      site.count)
    return site, vals


@pytest.mark.parametrize("version", VERSIONS)
def test_literal_relocation(version, tmp_path):
    """a = [10, 20, 30]; print(a[1]) - a[1] becomes 99."""
    path = _compile(version, "literals.js", tmp_path)
    assert _run(version, path) == ["20"]
    proj = HermitProject.from_hbc(str(path))
    site, vals = _array_site(proj)
    items = [(v.tag, reencode_value_bytes(v.tag, 99 if k == 1 else v.value))
             for k, v in enumerate(vals)]
    proj.apply_array_relocation(site.function_index, site.instruction_offset, False,
                                encode_slp_sequence(items), 0, {1})
    assert _run(version, _write(proj, tmp_path, "lit.hbc")) == ["99"]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("version", VERSIONS)
def test_literal_resize(version, tmp_path):
    """a = [10, 20, 30]; print(a.length) - append 40."""
    path = _compile(version, "literals_resize.js", tmp_path)
    assert _run(version, path) == ["3"]
    proj = HermitProject.from_hbc(str(path))
    site, vals = _array_site(proj)
    items = [(v.tag, reencode_value_bytes(v.tag, v.value)) for v in vals]
    items.append((vals[-1].tag, reencode_value_bytes(vals[-1].tag, 40)))
    proj.apply_array_resize(site.function_index, site.instruction_offset, False, True,
                            encode_slp_sequence(items), b"", 0)
    assert _run(version, _write(proj, tmp_path, "resize.hbc")) == ["4"]


# --- add_function --------------------------------------------------------


@pytest.mark.parametrize("version", VERSIONS)
def test_add_function(version, tmp_path):
    """New function returning undefined; `global`'s CreateClosure for `g` is
    repointed to it (second commit): the program prints "undefined"."""
    path = _compile(version, "greeting.js", tmp_path)
    proj = HermitProject.from_hbc(str(path))
    op = {d.mnemonic: d.opcode for d in _libhbc.opcode_table(version)}
    new_idx = proj.apply_add_function(
        [(op["LoadConstUndefined"], [0.0], -1, -1, -1), (op["Ret"], [0.0], -1, -1, -1)], 1)

    g = proj.hbc.header().global_code_index
    ir = _ir(proj, g)
    cc = next(k for k, x in enumerate(proj.hbc.disasm(g)) if x.mnemonic == "CreateClosure")
    ir[cc][1][2] = float(new_idx)
    proj.apply_insertion(g, [tuple(t) for t in ir], proj.hbc.functions()[g].frameSize)
    assert _run(version, _write(proj, tmp_path, "addfn.hbc")) == ["undefined"]
```

`tests/integration/patcher/test_overflow_index.py`:

```py
"""Overflow strings are addressed by the index stored in their small entry.

A `SmallStringTableEntry` with `length == 255` carries in its `offset` field the
index of its entry in the Overflow String Table (Hermes'
`BytecodeDataProvider::getStringTableEntry` reads
`overflowStringTableEntries_[small.offset]`). These tests check what the VM-side
reader sees, using `hermes -b -dump-bytecode` as the oracle:

* `add_string` on a file that already has overflow strings stores the index of
  the new slot;
* `set_string_value` on an overflow entry finds the slot through that index, on
  a file whose slots are in any order;
* an overflow slot used by two entries is refused.
"""

import re
import struct
import subprocess

import pytest

import _libhbc
from testutil import CORPUS, HERMES

pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(HERMES is None, reason="hermes not available")

A, B = "A" * 300, "B" * 300

_DUMP_RE = re.compile(r"^s(\d+)\[(?:ASCII|UTF-16)[^\]]*\]: (.*)$")


def hermes_strings(path):
    """index -> text, as printed by Hermes' own reader of the string table."""
    r = subprocess.run([HERMES, "-b", "-dump-bytecode", str(path)],
                       capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60)
    assert r.returncode == 0, r.stderr
    out = {}
    for line in r.stdout.splitlines():
        m = _DUMP_RE.match(line)
        if m:
            out[int(m.group(1))] = m.group(2)
    return out


@pytest.fixture
def ovf_hbc(tmp_path):
    """HBC 96 compiled by hermes with two overflow strings (A*300, B*300)."""
    js = tmp_path / "ovf.js"
    js.write_text(f'var x = "{A}"; var y = "{B}"; print(x.length + y.length);\n')
    out = tmp_path / "ovf.hbc"
    subprocess.run([HERMES, "-emit-binary", "-out", str(out), str(js)], check=True)
    return out


def _align4(n):
    return (n + 3) & ~3


def _tables(f):
    """Absolute offsets of the string table and of the overflow table."""
    h = f.header()
    kind = _align4(128 + h.function_count * 16)
    ident = _align4(kind + h.string_kind_count * 4)
    stab = _align4(ident + h.identifier_count * 4)
    return stab, stab + h.string_count * 4


def _sentinels(raw, f):
    """Indices of the string table entries with length == 255."""
    stab, _ = _tables(f)
    return [i for i in range(f.header().string_count)
            if struct.unpack_from("<I", raw, stab + 4 * i)[0] >> 24 == 255]


def _permuted(path, out, shared=False):
    """Copy of `path` where the two overflow slots are swapped and the small
    entries updated to follow them: the strings seen by Hermes stay the same, the
    first sentinel names slot 1 and the second names slot 0. With `shared`, both
    small entries name slot 1."""
    f = _libhbc.HBCFile.open(str(path))
    raw = bytearray(path.read_bytes())
    stab, otab = _tables(f)
    s0, s1 = _sentinels(raw, f)[:2]
    if not shared:
        o0, o1 = raw[otab:otab + 8], raw[otab + 8:otab + 16]
        raw[otab:otab + 8], raw[otab + 8:otab + 16] = o1, o0
    for i, idx in ((s0, 1), (s1, 0 if not shared else 1)):
        w = struct.unpack_from("<I", raw, stab + 4 * i)[0]
        w = (w & ~(0x7FFFFF << 1)) | (idx << 1)
        struct.pack_into("<I", raw, stab + 4 * i, w)
    out.write_bytes(bytes(raw))
    return s0, s1


def _serialize(module, out):
    out.write_bytes(bytes(module.serialize()))
    return _libhbc.HBCFile.open(str(out))


def test_add_string_after_existing_overflow_uses_the_right_index(ovf_hbc, tmp_path):
    before = hermes_strings(ovf_hbc)
    f = _libhbc.HBCFile.open(str(ovf_hbc))
    assert f.header().overflow_string_count == 2

    m = _libhbc.Module.from_hbcfile(f)
    first = m.add_string("C" * 300)
    second = m.add_string("D" * 301)
    g = _serialize(m, tmp_path / "out.hbc")

    assert g.header().overflow_string_count == 4
    seen = hermes_strings(tmp_path / "out.hbc")
    assert seen[first] == "C" * 300          # what the VM reads, not slot 0
    assert seen[second] == "D" * 301
    assert all(seen[i] == before[i] for i in before)   # old strings untouched
    assert g.strings()[first] == "C" * 300 and g.strings()[second] == "D" * 301


def test_add_string_on_real_bundle_with_overflow(tmp_path):
    src = CORPUS / "hermitvault.hbc"
    if not src.exists():
        pytest.skip("missing corpus: hermitvault.hbc")
    before = hermes_strings(src)
    f = _libhbc.HBCFile.open(str(src))
    n_ovf = f.header().overflow_string_count
    assert n_ovf > 0

    m = _libhbc.Module.from_hbcfile(f)
    idx = m.add_string("Z" * 400)
    g = _serialize(m, tmp_path / "out.hbc")

    assert g.header().overflow_string_count == n_ovf + 1
    seen = hermes_strings(tmp_path / "out.hbc")
    assert seen[idx] == "Z" * 400
    assert all(seen[i] == before[i] for i in before)


def test_permuted_overflow_file_is_read_by_index(ovf_hbc, tmp_path):
    perm = tmp_path / "perm.hbc"
    _permuted(ovf_hbc, perm)
    # Hermes sees the same strings as in the original (the permutation is invisible to it).
    assert hermes_strings(perm) == hermes_strings(ovf_hbc)
    # hermit reads the same strings: A at index 0, B at index 1.
    f = _libhbc.HBCFile.open(str(perm))
    assert f.strings()[0] == A and f.strings()[1] == B


def test_set_string_value_on_overflow_entry_finds_the_slot_by_index(ovf_hbc, tmp_path):
    perm = tmp_path / "perm.hbc"
    s0, s1 = _permuted(ovf_hbc, perm)
    f = _libhbc.HBCFile.open(str(perm))
    assert f.strings()[s0] == A

    m = _libhbc.Module.from_hbcfile(f)
    m.set_string_value(s0, b"X" * 320)          # stays overflow whatever the length
    g = _serialize(m, tmp_path / "out.hbc")

    seen = hermes_strings(tmp_path / "out.hbc")
    assert seen[s0] == "X" * 320
    assert seen[s1] == B                         # the other overflow string is untouched
    assert g.strings()[s0] == "X" * 320 and g.strings()[s1] == B


def test_set_string_value_refuses_a_shared_overflow_slot(ovf_hbc, tmp_path):
    shared = tmp_path / "shared.hbc"
    s0, _ = _permuted(ovf_hbc, shared, shared=True)
    f = _libhbc.HBCFile.open(str(shared))
    assert f.strings()[0] == f.strings()[1] == B

    m = _libhbc.Module.from_hbcfile(f)
    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="shared"):
        m.set_string_value(s0, b"X" * 320)

```

```py
"""cli/cfg_dot.py - DOT generation and the graph-easy dependency check."""

import pytest

import _libhbc
from cli import cfg_dot
from testutil import corpus_path


def _cfg_and_func(corpus_name="hello.hbc", func_idx=1):
    hbc = _libhbc.HBCFile.open(str(corpus_path(corpus_name)))
    func = hbc.functions()[func_idx]
    return hbc.cfg(func_idx), func


def test_cfg_to_dot_produces_digraph():
    cfg, func = _cfg_and_func()
    dot = cfg_dot.cfg_to_dot(cfg, func)
    assert dot.startswith("digraph ")
    assert f"B{cfg.entry_id}" in dot


def test_render_cfg_raises_without_graph_easy(monkeypatch):
    """graph-easy is a required external dependency (Perl/CPAN) for `cfg` -
    missing it must fail loudly, never fall back to dumping raw DOT."""
    cfg, func = _cfg_and_func()
    monkeypatch.setattr(cfg_dot, "_find_graph_easy", lambda: None)
    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="graph-easy"):
        cfg_dot.render_cfg(cfg, func)
```

`tests/integration/repl/test_display.py`:

```py
"""CLI display formatting (`cli/display.py`), unit-level.

Pure functions (`functions_to_ansi_rows` et al.) don't need the REPL/viewer
scaffolding used by test_repl.py - call them directly on an opened HBCFile.

Covers: the "show-source" flag added to the `functions` command list when a
function carries Hermes' "show source" directive (Function Source Table,
see the function-table implementation notes).
"""

import _libhbc
from rich.console import Console
from cli import display
from testutil import corpus_path


def _render(table) -> str:
    """Render a rich Table to plain text at a width wide enough that no
    column wraps, so cell content can be asserted on directly."""
    console = Console(width=300, legacy_windows=False)
    with console.capture() as capture:
        console.print(table)
    return capture.get()


def _open(name: str) -> "_libhbc.HBCFile":
    return _libhbc.HBCFile.open(str(corpus_path(name)))


def _row_for(rows: list[str], name: str) -> str:
    for r in rows:
        if name in r:
            return r
    raise AssertionError(f"no row for function {name!r} in {rows!r}")


def _row_for_index(rows: list[str], index: int) -> str:
    needle = f"[{index:5d}]"
    for r in rows:
        if needle in r:
            return r
    raise AssertionError(f"no row for function index {index} in {rows!r}")


def test_show_source_flag_only_on_real_show_source_functions():
    hbc = _open("show_source.hbc")
    rows = display.functions_to_ansi_rows(hbc.functions(), hbc.header().global_code_index)

    # withComment and arrowShow both use "show source" -> flagged.
    assert "show-source" in _row_for(rows, "withComment")
    assert "show-source" in _row_for(rows, "arrowShow")

    # hide source / sensitive / no directive at all -> NOT flagged. The flag
    # means "real source recoverable", not "this function is in the table".
    assert "show-source" not in _row_for(rows, "hidden")
    assert "show-source" not in _row_for(rows, "sensitiveFn")
    assert "show-source" not in _row_for(rows, "normal")


def test_show_source_flag_absent_when_no_directives_used():
    # hello.hbc doesn't use the directive anywhere -> functionSourceCount == 0,
    # no row should ever carry "show-source".
    hbc = _open("hello.hbc")
    rows = display.functions_to_ansi_rows(hbc.functions(), hbc.header().global_code_index)
    assert all("show-source" not in r for r in rows)


def _cjs_module_paths(hbc) -> dict:
    return {cm.function_index: cm.module_path for cm in hbc.cjs_modules()}


def test_cjs_module_tag_shows_resolved_path():
    # cjs_modules.hbc: main.js require()s foo.js, native `-commonjs` mode
    # (header.cjsModuleCount == 2) -- never the Metro `__d()` case. Every
    # wrapper function is literally named "cjs_module" in the function
    # table, so the path tag is the only way to tell them apart.
    hbc = _open("cjs_modules.hbc")
    cjs_module_paths = _cjs_module_paths(hbc)
    assert len(cjs_module_paths) == 2

    rows = display.functions_to_ansi_rows(
        hbc.functions(), hbc.header().global_code_index,
        cjs_module_paths=cjs_module_paths,
    )

    main_idx = next(i for i, p in cjs_module_paths.items() if p == "main.js")
    foo_idx = next(i for i, p in cjs_module_paths.items() if p == "foo.js")
    assert "module 'main.js'" in _row_for_index(rows, main_idx)
    assert "module 'foo.js'" in _row_for_index(rows, foo_idx)

    # The global (top-level) function is never a CJS module itself.
    global_idx = hbc.header().global_code_index
    assert global_idx not in cjs_module_paths
    assert "module '" not in _row_for_index(rows, global_idx)


def test_cjs_module_tag_absent_on_non_commonjs_file():
    # hello.hbc has header.cjsModuleCount == 0 -> no tag anywhere, same as a
    # Metro-bundled file (recover_modules() and cjs_modules() are mutually
    # exclusive in every real sample, see doc/hbc-format/v96-format.md §9).
    hbc = _open("hello.hbc")
    assert hbc.cjs_modules() == []
    rows = display.functions_to_ansi_rows(
        hbc.functions(), hbc.header().global_code_index, cjs_module_paths={},
    )
    assert all("module '" not in r for r in rows)


def test_info_table_shows_cjs_modules_when_present():
    # cjs_modules.hbc: header.cjsModuleCount == 2 -> "CJS modules" row, no
    # "Metro modules" row (the two mechanisms never coexist in practice).
    hbc = _open("cjs_modules.hbc")
    out = _render(display.make_info_table(hbc))
    assert "CJS modules" in out
    assert "2" in out.split("CJS modules")[1].splitlines()[0]
    assert "Metro modules" not in out


def test_info_table_shows_metro_modules_otherwise():
    # No CJS Module Table on this file -> falls back to "Metro modules"
    # (recover_modules(), the __d() pattern -- what real RN bundles use),
    # even when the count is 0.
    hbc = _open("hello.hbc")
    out = _render(display.make_info_table(hbc))
    assert "Metro modules" in out
    assert "CJS modules" not in out


def test_info_table_source_file_paths_are_not_truncated():
    # Source file(s) rows must show the full path, one per line, never a
    # "…"-elided version (regression: _short_path used to crop at 60 chars).
    hbc = _open("hello.hbc")
    src_files = hbc.source_files()
    assert src_files, "hello.hbc should carry at least one source file"

    out = _render(display.make_info_table(hbc))
    assert "…" not in out
    for sf in src_files:
        assert sf in out


def test_info_table_shows_each_source_file_on_its_own_line():
    # cjs_modules.hbc is a genuine debugInfoHeader.filenameCount == 2 file
    # (main.js + foo.js) -- regression for the source_files() bug where the
    # two names, not NUL-separated on disk, were concatenated into one
    # garbled entry instead of being decoded as two.
    hbc = _open("cjs_modules.hbc")
    src_files = hbc.source_files()
    assert len(src_files) == 2
    assert src_files[0] != src_files[1]

    out = _render(display.make_info_table(hbc))
    lines = out.splitlines()
    line0 = next(l for l in lines if src_files[0] in l)
    line1 = next(l for l in lines if src_files[1] in l)
    assert line0 != line1
    # Neither file's full path leaked into the other's row.
    assert src_files[1] not in line0
    assert src_files[0] not in line1

```

```py
"""REPL command-level tests (`cli/repl.py`).

Drives `HermitREPL._dispatch(line)`, the entry point of `run()`, with `show_list`
made headless by a monkeypatch (a pipe input that sends "q", so the real
Application is built and rendered) and `cfg_dot.show_cfg` replaced by a stub
(the external `less`/`graph-easy` pager isn't reliably testable in CI).
"""

import pytest
from prompt_toolkit.input.defaults import create_pipe_input
from prompt_toolkit.output import DummyOutput

import cli.repl as repl_mod

from testutil import corpus_path


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def _headless_show_list(monkeypatch):
    """Replaces cli.repl.show_list with a version that opens the view on a
    pipe input, immediately sends 'q' and closes it - exercises the REAL
    Application (layout, key bindings, rendering) instead of a mock, without
    blocking."""
    from cli.viewer import show_list as real_show_list

    def _fake(rows, title="", alt_rows=None, alt_title=""):
        if not rows:
            return
        with create_pipe_input() as inp:
            inp.send_text("q")
            real_show_list(rows, title=title, alt_rows=alt_rows, alt_title=alt_title,
                           _input=inp, _output=DummyOutput())

    monkeypatch.setattr(repl_mod, "show_list", _fake)

def _stub_show_cfg(monkeypatch):
    """cfg_dot.show_cfg spawns `less`/`graph-easy` (external subprocesses, not
    reliable in headless CI) - just records the call."""
    calls = []
    monkeypatch.setattr(repl_mod.cfg_dot, "show_cfg",
                        lambda cfg, func, **kw: calls.append((func.index, kw)))
    return calls
```

`tests/integration/testutil.py`:

```py
"""Helpers shared by the integration tests: corpus loading, the `hermes` VM,
terminal key codes and headless drivers for the three editors."""

import re
import shutil
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

import pytest
from prompt_toolkit.input.defaults import create_pipe_input
from prompt_toolkit.output import DummyOutput

from cli.editor import run_array_editor, run_editor, run_string_editor
from cli.project import HermitProject

CORPUS = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "seeder" / "corpus"

# Keys as a terminal sends them.
UP, DOWN, RIGHT, LEFT = "\x1b[A", "\x1b[B", "\x1b[C", "\x1b[D"
ENTER, ESC = "\r", "\x1b"
CC, CK, CN, CR, CT, CX, CZ = "\x03", "\x0b", "\x0e", "\x12", "\x14", "\x18", "\x1a"

# The Hermes VM (HBC 96) used to run patched files; None if not installed.
HERMES = shutil.which("hermes") or (
    "/usr/local/bin/hermes" if Path("/usr/local/bin/hermes").exists() else None
)

_ANSI_RE = re.compile(r"\x1b\[[0-9;]*m")


def strip_ansi(s: str) -> str:
    return _ANSI_RE.sub("", s)


def corpus_path(name: str) -> Path:
    """`seeder/corpus/<name>`; skips the test if the corpus file isn't generated."""
    path = CORPUS / name
    if not path.exists():
        pytest.skip(f"missing corpus: {name} - regenerate it with `python -m seeder.compile`")
    return path


def load_project(name: str) -> HermitProject:
    return HermitProject.from_hbc(str(corpus_path(name)))


def run_hermes(path):
    """Runs a .hbc on the Hermes VM and returns the CompletedProcess."""
    return subprocess.run([HERMES, str(path)], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30)


def drive_instructions(state, keys):
    """Feeds `keys` (then Ctrl+C as a safety net) to the instruction editor."""
    with create_pipe_input() as inp:
        inp.send_text(keys + CC)
        run_editor(state.func, [], _input=inp, _output=DummyOutput(), _state=state)
    return state


def drive_strings(state, keys):
    with create_pipe_input() as inp:
        inp.send_text(keys + CC)
        run_string_editor(_state=state, _input=inp, _output=DummyOutput())
    return state


def drive_arrays(state, keys):
    with create_pipe_input() as inp:
        inp.send_text(keys + CC)
        run_array_editor(_state=state, _input=inp, _output=DummyOutput())
    return state

```

`tests/unit/cfg/test_cfg.cpp`:

```cpp
// =============================================================================
// test_cfg.cpp - Catch2 tests for the Control Flow Graph
// =============================================================================
// Uses hello.hbc (linear function) and control_flow.hbc (if/else, loop).
// The file paths are injected by CMake via HBC_CORPUS_DIR.
// =============================================================================

#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>

#include "hbc/hbc.h"

#include <string>
#include <vector>

static constexpr const char* HELLO_HBC        = HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/hello.hbc";
static constexpr const char* CONTROL_FLOW_HBC = HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/control_flow.hbc";
static constexpr const char* SWITCH_DENSE_HBC = HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/switch_dense.hbc";

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Helper: returns true if the CFG contains an edge of the given kind
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
static bool hasEdgeKind(const hbc::CFGData& cfg, hbc::EdgeKind kind) {
    for (const auto& bb : cfg.blocks)
        for (const auto& e : bb.successors)
            if (e.kind == kind) return true;
    return false;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Helper: number of blocks that are loop headers
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
static uint32_t countLoopHeaders(const hbc::CFGData& cfg) {
    uint32_t n = 0;
    for (const auto& bb : cfg.blocks)
        if (bb.isLoopHeader) n++;
    return n;
}

// ===========================================================================
// Test 1 - linear function (hello.hbc, func 0 = global)
// ===========================================================================
// global has sequential instructions and ends with Ret.
// Must produce exactly 1 basic block with no successors (exit node).
TEST_CASE("CFG: linear function -> 1 block, no successors", "[cfg]") {
    auto hbc = hbc::HBCFile::open(HELLO_HBC);
    // func 0 is the global one, which is linear: it calls greet and does Ret
    auto cfg = hbc.cfg(0);

    REQUIRE_FALSE(cfg.blocks.empty());
    // A linear function can have a single block
    CHECK(cfg.blocks.size() == 1);
    CHECK(cfg.hasLoops == false);
    // The entry block has no successors (ends with Ret)
    CHECK(cfg.blocks[cfg.entryId].successors.empty());
}

// ===========================================================================
// Test 2 - function with if/else (control_flow.hbc)
// ===========================================================================
// The max/factorial/sumTo functions use conditional jumps.
// We check: at least 2 blocks, presence of CondTaken + CondFallThru.
TEST_CASE("CFG: control_flow.hbc has conditional jumps", "[cfg]") {
    auto hbc = hbc::HBCFile::open(CONTROL_FLOW_HBC);
    const auto& funcs = hbc.functions();
    REQUIRE_FALSE(funcs.empty());

    bool foundConditional = false;
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < funcs.size(); i++) {
        auto cfg = hbc.cfg(i);
        if (hasEdgeKind(cfg, hbc::EdgeKind::CondTaken) ||
            hasEdgeKind(cfg, hbc::EdgeKind::CondFallThru)) {
            foundConditional = true;
            CHECK(cfg.blocks.size() >= 2);
            break;
        }
    }
    CHECK(foundConditional);
}

// ===========================================================================
// Test 3 - function with a loop (control_flow.hbc)
// ===========================================================================
// factorial or sumTo has a loop -> back-edge DFS -> hasLoops + isLoopHeader.
TEST_CASE("CFG: control_flow.hbc has a loop (back-edge + loop header)", "[cfg]") {
    auto hbc = hbc::HBCFile::open(CONTROL_FLOW_HBC);
    const auto& funcs = hbc.functions();
    REQUIRE_FALSE(funcs.empty());

    bool foundLoop = false;
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < funcs.size(); i++) {
        auto cfg = hbc.cfg(i);
        if (cfg.hasLoops) {
            foundLoop = true;
            CHECK(hasEdgeKind(cfg, hbc::EdgeKind::BackEdge));
            CHECK(countLoopHeaders(cfg) >= 1);
            break;
        }
    }
    CHECK(foundLoop);
}

// ===========================================================================
// Test 4 - predecessors consistent with successors
// ===========================================================================
// For every edge A->B in A's successors, B.predecessors must contain A.id.
TEST_CASE("CFG: predecessors consistent with successors", "[cfg]") {
    auto hbc = hbc::HBCFile::open(CONTROL_FLOW_HBC);
    const auto& funcs = hbc.functions();

    for (uint32_t fi = 0; fi < funcs.size(); fi++) {
        auto cfg = hbc.cfg(fi);
        for (const auto& bb : cfg.blocks) {
            for (const auto& edge : bb.successors) {
                const auto& target = cfg.blocks[edge.targetId];
                bool found = false;
                for (uint32_t pid : target.predecessors)
                    if (pid == bb.id) { found = true; break; }
                CHECK(found);
            }
        }
    }
}

// ===========================================================================
// Test 5 - entry block has startOffset == 0
// ===========================================================================
TEST_CASE("CFG: entry block starts at offset 0", "[cfg]") {
    auto hbc = hbc::HBCFile::open(HELLO_HBC);
    const auto& funcs = hbc.functions();
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < funcs.size(); i++) {
        auto cfg = hbc.cfg(i);
        REQUIRE_FALSE(cfg.blocks.empty());
        CHECK(cfg.blocks[cfg.entryId].startOffset == 0);
    }
}

// ===========================================================================
// Test 6 - SwitchImm: jump table resolved, every case gets a real edge
// ===========================================================================
// Regression for a real bug found writing the thesis appendix: the jump
// table of a SwitchImm ALWAYS lives PAST the function's own
// bytecodeSizeInBytes (in the gap before the next function's body), and its
// start must be rounded up to a 4-byte boundary - verified against
// `hermes -dump-bytecode` and the runtime interpreter's own table lookup
// (facebook/hermes @ hermes-2023-09-26-RNv0.73.0, lib/VM/Interpreter.cpp,
// `CASE(SwitchImm)`). Both facts are
// stated only in a source comment (BytecodeList.def, SwitchImm: jump tables
// "are appended to the bytecode", Arg2 "is dynamically aligned at runtime").
// Before the fix, disasm()/cfg() read the
// table from the per-function slice with an unaligned offset - every
// SwitchImm ended up with zero resolved targets and zero SwitchCase edges
// (only SwitchDefault), even though the cases are very much reachable at
// runtime.
//
// switch_dense.ts (12 contiguous cases, 0..11 - the only shape Hermes lowers
// to SwitchImm, see LowerSwitchIntoJumpTables: needs >=10 cases and a dense
// range). Regenerate the corpus with
// `.venv/bin/python -m seeder.compile seeder/samples/switch_dense.ts` if missing
// (seeder/corpus/*.hbc is gitignored).
TEST_CASE("CFG: SwitchImm produces SwitchCase edges for every case", "[cfg]") {
    auto hbc = hbc::HBCFile::open(SWITCH_DENSE_HBC);
    const auto& funcs = hbc.functions();

    uint32_t classifyIdx = UINT32_MAX;
    for (const auto& fi : funcs)
        if (fi.name == "classify") { classifyIdx = fi.index; break; }
    REQUIRE(classifyIdx != UINT32_MAX);

    auto instrs = hbc.disasm(classifyIdx);
    const hbc::Instruction* switchInstr = nullptr;
    for (const auto& instr : instrs)
        if (instr.mnemonic == "SwitchImm") { switchInstr = &instr; break; }
    REQUIRE(switchInstr != nullptr);

    // 12 contiguous cases (0..11): the disassembler must resolve all 12 targets.
    REQUIRE(switchInstr->switchTargets.size() == 12);

    auto cfg = hbc.cfg(classifyIdx);
    uint32_t switchCaseEdges = 0, switchDefaultEdges = 0;
    for (const auto& bb : cfg.blocks)
        for (const auto& e : bb.successors) {
            if (e.kind == hbc::EdgeKind::SwitchCase)    switchCaseEdges++;
            if (e.kind == hbc::EdgeKind::SwitchDefault) switchDefaultEdges++;
        }
    CHECK(switchCaseEdges == 12);
    CHECK(switchDefaultEdges == 1);

    // Every resolved target must land exactly on a block boundary (no
    // misaligned/garbage offset) - cross-check disasm's switchTargets
    // against the CFG's own leader set.
    for (uint32_t target : switchInstr->switchTargets) {
        bool isLeader = false;
        for (const auto& bb : cfg.blocks)
            if (bb.startOffset == target) { isLeader = true; break; }
        CHECK(isLeader);
    }
}
```

`tests/unit/cjs-modules/test_cjs_modules.cpp`:

```cpp
// =============================================================================
// test_cjs_modules.cpp - Unit tests for the CJS Module Table (header.cjsModuleCount)
// =============================================================================
// Hermes's native CommonJS mode (`hermes -commonjs`) is a separate
// compilation path from the one real React Native/Metro bundles ever use
// (see recover_modules()/ModuleInfo for the Metro `__d()` case instead).
// Samples generated by seeder/gen_cjs_sample.py; see
// doc/hbc-format/v96-format.md §9 for the on-disk format.
//
//   cjs_modules.hbc:
//     main.js require()s foo.js -> 2 entries:
//       (stringID -> "main.js", functionID=1)
//       (stringID -> "foo.js",  functionID=2)
//
//   cjs_modules_segmented.hbc / cjs_modules_segmented.hbc.1:
//     2-segment compile (main.js in segment 0, lazy.js in segment 1) -> 1
//     entry per file, header.segmentID distinguishes them (0 / 1), and the
//     rest of the layout (section_map(), strings(), functions()) parses
//     identically to any monolithic file.
//
// Every sample was compiled with plain `-commonjs` (no `-fstatic-require`):
// `-fstatic-require` was verified to produce byte-identical output in every
// combination tried (see the generator script and
// doc/hbc-format/v96-format.md §9.4), so `is_statically_resolved` is false
// on every entry here -- there is no sample for the static shape because
// the public Hermes compiler cannot emit it.
// =============================================================================
#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>
#include "hbc/hbc.h"
#include <string>

static const std::string HELLO          = std::string(HBC_CORPUS_DIR) + "/hello.hbc";
static const std::string CJS_MODULES    = std::string(HBC_CORPUS_DIR) + "/cjs_modules.hbc";
static const std::string CJS_SEG0       = std::string(HBC_CORPUS_DIR) + "/cjs_modules_segmented.hbc";
static const std::string CJS_SEG1       = std::string(HBC_CORPUS_DIR) + "/cjs_modules_segmented.hbc.1";

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Test 1 - cjs_modules() returns empty when header.cjsModuleCount == 0
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
TEST_CASE("cjs_modules: returns empty on a non-CommonJS file", "[cjs-modules]") {
    auto f = hbc::HBCFile::open(HELLO);
    CHECK(f.header().cjsModuleCount == 0);
    CHECK(f.cjs_modules().empty());
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Test 2 - cjs_modules.hbc: both entries decoded, path resolved from the
// String Table, pointing at the right wrapper function.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
TEST_CASE("cjs_modules: decodes the dynamic (stringID, functionID) shape", "[cjs-modules]") {
    auto f = hbc::HBCFile::open(CJS_MODULES);

    REQUIRE(f.header().cjsModuleCount == 2);
    CHECK((f.header().options & 0b10) == 0);  // cjsModulesStaticallyResolved = 0

    auto mods = f.cjs_modules();
    REQUIRE(mods.size() == 2);

    for (const auto& m : mods) {
        CHECK_FALSE(m.isStaticallyResolved);
        REQUIRE(m.functionIndex < f.functions().size());
    }

    // Order on disk follows compilation order: main.js then foo.js.
    CHECK(mods[0].modulePath == "main.js");
    CHECK(mods[0].functionIndex == 1);
    CHECK(mods[1].modulePath == "foo.js");
    CHECK(mods[1].functionIndex == 2);

    // Every CJS module wrapper is named "cjs_module" in the function table
    // itself -- the file path lives only in this table, not in functionName.
    CHECK(f.functions()[mods[0].functionIndex].name == "cjs_module");
    CHECK(f.functions()[mods[1].functionIndex].name == "cjs_module");
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Test 3 - segmented compile: segmentID distinguishes the two files, each
// with its own single-entry CJS Module Table, rest of the layout intact.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
TEST_CASE("cjs_modules: segmentID differs across segments, layout unaffected", "[cjs-modules]") {
    auto seg0 = hbc::HBCFile::open(CJS_SEG0);
    auto seg1 = hbc::HBCFile::open(CJS_SEG1);

    CHECK(seg0.header().segmentID == 0);
    CHECK(seg1.header().segmentID == 1);

    auto mods0 = seg0.cjs_modules();
    auto mods1 = seg1.cjs_modules();
    REQUIRE(mods0.size() == 1);
    REQUIRE(mods1.size() == 1);

    CHECK(mods0[0].modulePath == "main.js");
    CHECK(mods1[0].modulePath == "lazy.js");

    // segmentID changes nothing else about how the file parses.
    CHECK_FALSE(seg0.section_map().empty());
    CHECK_FALSE(seg1.section_map().empty());
    CHECK(seg0.functions()[mods0[0].functionIndex].name == "cjs_module");
    CHECK(seg1.functions()[mods1[0].functionIndex].name == "cjs_module");
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Test 4 - source_files() with filenameCount > 1 (regression).
//
// cjs_modules.hbc is the first real sample ever observed with
// debugInfoHeader.filenameCount == 2 (main.js + foo.js, no multi-file debug
// info sample existed before this corpus -- see doc/hbc-format/v96-format.md
// §11.1/B17). Hermes does NOT null-separate consecutive filenames in the
// filename storage blob; source_files() used to scan for '\0' and silently
// concatenate both names into a single garbled entry. Fixed to read the
// filename table's (offset, length) pairs directly.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
TEST_CASE("source_files: filenameCount > 1 are not concatenated", "[cjs-modules]") {
    auto f = hbc::HBCFile::open(CJS_MODULES);

    auto dih = f.debug_info_header();
    REQUIRE(dih.filenameCount == 2);

    auto files = f.source_files();
    REQUIRE(files.size() == 2);
    CHECK(files[0].size() < 100);  // a real path, not two paths glued together
    CHECK(files[1].size() < 100);
    CHECK(files[0] != files[1]);
    for (const auto& path : files) {
        CHECK(path.find(".js") != std::string::npos);
        // No leftover '/' from a second path's absolute prefix bleeding into this one.
        CHECK(path.find(".js/") == std::string::npos);
    }
}
```
