`tests/unit/decompiler/test_decompiler.cpp`:

```cpp
// =============================================================================
// test_decompiler.cpp - Catch2 tests for the Decompiler
// =============================================================================
// Tests via the public API (HBCFile::decompile/debug_info_header/scope_variables/
// textified_callees/debug_strings), same pattern as test_cfg.cpp - no
// direct access to emitExpression()/structureCFG() (private, decompiler.h is
// not in the test target's include path).
//
// control_flow_g.hbc / closure_scope_g.hbc / exceptions.hbc are generated by
// the seeder (seeder/samples/*.ts compiled with `hermes -emit-binary -g`, see
// implementation-notes.md) - the absolute source paths embedded in the
// filename storage vary from machine to machine, so the tests check
// structural invariants (function/variable names, monotonic ordering
// of offsets) and never exact raw byte values.
// =============================================================================

#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>

#include "hbc/hbc.h"

#include <string>
#include <vector>

static constexpr const char* CONTROL_FLOW_HBC   = HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/control_flow.hbc";
static constexpr const char* CONTROL_FLOW_G_HBC = HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/control_flow_g.hbc";
static constexpr const char* CLOSURE_SCOPE_HBC  = HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/closure_scope_g.hbc";
static constexpr const char* EXCEPTIONS_HBC     = HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/exceptions.hbc";
static constexpr const char* FUNCTIONS_HBC      = HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/functions.hbc";
static constexpr const char* SWITCH_HBC         = HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/switch.hbc";
static constexpr const char* ARRAY_OBJECT_LITERALS_HBC = HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/array_object_literals.hbc";
static constexpr const char* ARRAY_OBJECT_LITERALS_LONG_HBC =
    HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/array_object_literals_long.hbc";
static constexpr const char* SHOW_SOURCE_HBC = HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/show_source.hbc";

static const hbc::FunctionInfo& findFunc(const hbc::HBCFile& hbc, const std::string& name) {
    for (const auto& f : hbc.functions())
        if (f.name == name) return f;
    FAIL("function not found: " << name);
    throw std::runtime_error("unreachable");
}

static bool contains(const std::string& haystack, const std::string& needle) {
    return haystack.find(needle) != std::string::npos;
}

// ===========================================================================
// Expression emitter + CFG structurer (via decompile())
// ===========================================================================

TEST_CASE("decompile: linear function produces non-empty output with return", "[decompiler]") {
    auto hbc = hbc::HBCFile::open(CONTROL_FLOW_HBC);
    const auto& fn = findFunc(hbc, "max");
    std::string code = hbc.decompile(fn.index);
    CHECK_FALSE(code.empty());
    CHECK(contains(code, "return"));
    CHECK(contains(code, "function"));
}

TEST_CASE("decompile: rebuilds if/else (max)", "[decompiler]") {
    auto hbc = hbc::HBCFile::open(CONTROL_FLOW_HBC);
    const auto& fn = findFunc(hbc, "max");
    std::string code = hbc.decompile(fn.index);
    CHECK(contains(code, "if ("));
    CHECK(contains(code, "else"));
    // paramCount includes `this` - 2 JS parameters, not 3
    CHECK(contains(code, "param_0"));
    CHECK(contains(code, "param_1"));
}

TEST_CASE("decompile: rebuilds a loop (sumTo)", "[decompiler]") {
    auto hbc = hbc::HBCFile::open(CONTROL_FLOW_HBC);
    const auto& fn = findFunc(hbc, "sumTo");
    std::string code = hbc.decompile(fn.index);
    bool hasLoop = contains(code, "while (") || contains(code, "while(");
    CHECK(hasLoop);
}

TEST_CASE("decompile: rebuilds try/catch (safeDivide)", "[decompiler]") {
    auto hbc = hbc::HBCFile::open(EXCEPTIONS_HBC);
    const auto& fn = findFunc(hbc, "safeDivide");
    std::string code = hbc.decompile(fn.index);
    CHECK(contains(code, "try {"));
    CHECK(contains(code, "catch ("));
    // The throw branch and the normal branch (a / b) must both appear
    // inside the try - not as "unstructured" blocks out of place.
    CHECK(contains(code, "throw"));
}

TEST_CASE("decompile: closure signature for functions with an inferred name", "[decompiler]") {
    auto hbc = hbc::HBCFile::open(FUNCTIONS_HBC);
    const auto& fn = findFunc(hbc, "double");
    std::string code = hbc.decompile(fn.index);
    // "double" doesn't start with anonymous_func_ -> the real name must appear,
    // as a closure (const double = function...), not a function declaration.
    CHECK(contains(code, "const double = function"));
}

// ===========================================================================
// Regression: never `this = ...` (SyntaxError - found on ridemovi.hbc)
// ===========================================================================

TEST_CASE("decompile: never an assignment to `this` (SyntaxError)", "[decompiler]") {
    for (const char* path : {CONTROL_FLOW_HBC, EXCEPTIONS_HBC, FUNCTIONS_HBC, SWITCH_HBC,
                              ARRAY_OBJECT_LITERALS_HBC, ARRAY_OBJECT_LITERALS_LONG_HBC, SHOW_SOURCE_HBC}) {
        auto hbc = hbc::HBCFile::open(path);
        for (const auto& f : hbc.functions()) {
            std::string code = hbc.decompile(f.index);
            CHECK_FALSE(contains(code, "this = "));
        }
    }
}

// ===========================================================================
// Robustness: decompiling every function of every corpus file must never
// throw an exception (the raw fallback guarantees total coverage - Ex 10.5).
// ===========================================================================

TEST_CASE("decompile: no exception across all functions in the corpus", "[decompiler]") {
    for (const char* path : {CONTROL_FLOW_HBC, EXCEPTIONS_HBC, FUNCTIONS_HBC, SWITCH_HBC,
                              ARRAY_OBJECT_LITERALS_HBC, ARRAY_OBJECT_LITERALS_LONG_HBC, SHOW_SOURCE_HBC}) {
        auto hbc = hbc::HBCFile::open(path);
        for (const auto& f : hbc.functions()) {
            CHECK_NOTHROW(hbc.decompile(f.index));
        }
    }
}

// ===========================================================================
// Array/object literal buffer resolution
// ===========================================================================
// array_object_literals.js: `var arr = [1, 2.5, "three", true, false, null];
// var obj = { a: 1, b: "two", c: false };` - compiled by Hermes as
// NewArrayWithBuffer r1, 6, 6, 0 / NewObjectWithBuffer r1, 3, 3, 0, 0
// (verified with `hermes -dump-bytecode`), one run of every SLP tag
// reachable from array/object literal syntax: Integer, Number, the three
// string tags (collapsed to one JS string literal either way), True,
// False, Null.

TEST_CASE("decompile: resolves array literal buffer content", "[decompiler]") {
    auto hbc = hbc::HBCFile::open(ARRAY_OBJECT_LITERALS_HBC);
    const auto& fn = findFunc(hbc, "global");
    std::string code = hbc.decompile(fn.index);
    CHECK(contains(code, "[1, 2.5, \"three\", true, false, null]"));
    CHECK_FALSE(contains(code, "content not resolved"));
}

TEST_CASE("decompile: resolves object literal buffer content", "[decompiler]") {
    auto hbc = hbc::HBCFile::open(ARRAY_OBJECT_LITERALS_HBC);
    const auto& fn = findFunc(hbc, "global");
    std::string code = hbc.decompile(fn.index);
    CHECK(contains(code, "{\"a\": 1, \"b\": \"two\", \"c\": false}"));
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Long variant (NewArrayWithBufferLong / NewObjectWithBufferLong)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// array_object_literals_long.js (seeder/gen_long_literal_sample.py): a
// 16400-element `bigArr`/`bigObj` pushes the array buffer / object value
// buffer past the 65535-byte UInt16 range, so the following `arrLong`/
// `objLong` are compiled with the Long variant (bufferIdx/keyBufferIdx/
// valBufferIdx widen to UInt32) - verified with `hermes -dump-bytecode`.
// Both variants share the exact same decode path in emitExpression(): the
// disassembler normalizes every integer operand to `.u32` regardless of
// its encoded width (empirical finding), so there is no separate Long-variant
// branch to test - this only guards that assumption against silent
// regressions (e.g. a future change that reads op[].u16 directly).

TEST_CASE("decompile: resolves array literal buffer content (Long variant)", "[decompiler]") {
    auto hbc = hbc::HBCFile::open(ARRAY_OBJECT_LITERALS_LONG_HBC);
    const auto& fn = findFunc(hbc, "global");

    // Fixture sanity check: fail loudly if a different hermes build ever
    // stops emitting the Long opcode here, instead of silently degrading
    // into a duplicate of the short-variant test above.
    bool sawLong = false;
    for (const auto& instr : hbc.disasm(fn.index))
        if (instr.mnemonic == "NewArrayWithBufferLong") sawLong = true;
    REQUIRE(sawLong);

    std::string code = hbc.decompile(fn.index);
    CHECK(contains(code, "[7, 8, 9]"));
    CHECK_FALSE(contains(code, "content not resolved"));
}

TEST_CASE("decompile: resolves object literal buffer content (Long variant)", "[decompiler]") {
    auto hbc = hbc::HBCFile::open(ARRAY_OBJECT_LITERALS_LONG_HBC);
    const auto& fn = findFunc(hbc, "global");

    bool sawLong = false;
    for (const auto& instr : hbc.disasm(fn.index))
        if (instr.mnemonic == "NewObjectWithBufferLong") sawLong = true;
    REQUIRE(sawLong);

    std::string code = hbc.decompile(fn.index);
    CHECK(contains(code, "{\"x\": 1, \"y\": 2}"));
}

// ===========================================================================
// Debug info section
// ===========================================================================

TEST_CASE("debug_info_header: cumulative offsets are monotonically non-decreasing", "[decompiler]") {
    auto hbc = hbc::HBCFile::open(CONTROL_FLOW_G_HBC);
    auto h = hbc.debug_info_header();
    CHECK(h.filenameCount >= 1);
    CHECK(h.sourceLocDataEnd <= h.scopeDescDataEnd);
    CHECK(h.scopeDescDataEnd <= h.textifiedCalleesEnd);
    CHECK(h.textifiedCalleesEnd <= h.stringTableEnd);
}

TEST_CASE("scope_variables: resolves the real name of a captured variable", "[decompiler]") {
    auto hbc = hbc::HBCFile::open(CLOSURE_SCOPE_HBC);
    const auto& fn = findFunc(hbc, "makeCounter");
    auto vars = hbc.scope_variables(fn.index);
    REQUIRE(vars.size() == 1);
    CHECK(vars[0].name == "count");
}

TEST_CASE("scope_variables: empty list for a function with no captured variables", "[decompiler]") {
    auto hbc = hbc::HBCFile::open(CLOSURE_SCOPE_HBC);
    const auto& fn = findFunc(hbc, "increment");
    // increment doesn't create its own environment (it accesses
    // makeCounter's via GetEnvironment) - its own scope_variables() is empty.
    auto vars = hbc.scope_variables(fn.index);
    CHECK(vars.empty());
}

TEST_CASE("textified_callees: resolves the callee's name via the debug string table", "[decompiler]") {
    auto hbc = hbc::HBCFile::open(CONTROL_FLOW_G_HBC);
    const auto& fn = findFunc(hbc, "factorial");
    auto callees = hbc.textified_callees(fn.index);
    REQUIRE(callees.size() == 1);
    CHECK(callees[0].name == "factorial");
}

TEST_CASE("debug_strings: contains the names used by scope_variables/textified_callees", "[decompiler]") {
    auto hbc = hbc::HBCFile::open(CONTROL_FLOW_G_HBC);
    auto strs = hbc.debug_strings();
    bool found = false;
    for (const auto& s : strs) if (s == "factorial") found = true;
    CHECK(found);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Debug string references are BYTE OFFSETS into the debug string table
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// debug_names_g.hbc (seeder/samples/debug_names.js). Oracle, from
// `hermes -dump-bytecode -g`:
//   Debug string table:  0x00 a, 0x02 counter, 0x0a runAll, 0x11 makeState,
//                        0x1b step, 0x20 print, 0x26 console.log
//   makeState scope:     "a", "counter"            (references 0, 2)
//   runAll callees:      bc 9 makeState, 19 step, 23 print, 39 step,
//                        43 console.log            (references 17, 27, 32, 27, 38)
// Reading references as positional indices (the old bug) gave "runAll" for
// `counter` (index 2: a wrong name, silently) and <debug_str_N> placeholders
// for every callee. The control_flow_g/closure_scope_g tests above could not
// catch it: their only referenced string sits at offset 0 = index 0.
static constexpr const char* DEBUG_NAMES_HBC = HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/debug_names_g.hbc";

TEST_CASE("scope_variables: resolves names by byte offset, not by position", "[decompiler]") {
    auto hbc = hbc::HBCFile::open(DEBUG_NAMES_HBC);
    const auto& fn = findFunc(hbc, "makeState");
    auto vars = hbc.scope_variables(fn.index);
    REQUIRE(vars.size() == 2);
    CHECK(vars[0].name == "a");
    CHECK(vars[1].name == "counter");   // index-based reading returned "runAll"
}

TEST_CASE("textified_callees: resolves every callee name by byte offset", "[decompiler]") {
    auto hbc = hbc::HBCFile::open(DEBUG_NAMES_HBC);
    const auto& fn = findFunc(hbc, "runAll");
    auto callees = hbc.textified_callees(fn.index);
    REQUIRE(callees.size() == 5);
    const std::vector<std::pair<uint32_t, std::string>> expected = {
        {9, "makeState"}, {19, "step"}, {23, "print"}, {39, "step"}, {43, "console.log"},
    };
    for (size_t i = 0; i < expected.size(); i++) {
        CHECK(callees[i].bytecodeOffset == expected[i].first);
        CHECK(callees[i].name == expected[i].second);
    }
}

TEST_CASE("debug_strings: file order of the debug string table", "[decompiler]") {
    auto hbc = hbc::HBCFile::open(DEBUG_NAMES_HBC);
    const std::vector<std::string> expected = {
        "a", "counter", "runAll", "makeState", "step", "print", "console.log",
    };
    CHECK(hbc.debug_strings() == expected);
}

TEST_CASE("decompile: real variable names when available (scope_variables wired up)", "[decompiler]") {
    auto hbc = hbc::HBCFile::open(CLOSURE_SCOPE_HBC);
    const auto& fn = findFunc(hbc, "makeCounter");
    std::string code = hbc.decompile(fn.index);
    CHECK(contains(code, "count"));
    CHECK(contains(code, "let count"));  // explicit declaration, not just usage
}

// ===========================================================================
// Function Source Table short-circuit ("show source" directive)
// ===========================================================================
// show_source.hbc (seeder/samples/show_source.js): withComment/arrowShow use
// "show source" (real source preserved), hidden/sensitiveFn use "hide
// source"/"sensitive" (entry present but empty - a marker, not real source),
// normal has no directive at all. decompile() must short-circuit ONLY the
// first two, returning the ORIGINAL text (with the banner comment) instead
// of running the normal disasm/CFG pipeline (see the function-table implementation notes).

TEST_CASE("decompile: returns verbatim original source for a \"show source\" function", "[decompiler]") {
    auto hbc = hbc::HBCFile::open(SHOW_SOURCE_HBC);
    const auto& fn = findFunc(hbc, "withComment");
    std::string code = hbc.decompile(fn.index);

    CHECK(contains(code, "ORIGINAL SOURCE"));
    CHECK(contains(code, "NOT decompiled"));
    // The comment survives only if this is the literal original text - the
    // normal decompiler NEVER preserves source comments (it has no way to
    // see them, it only sees bytecode).
    CHECK(contains(code, "// a comment inside the function"));
    CHECK(contains(code, "\"show source\";"));
    // Proves the normal pipeline was skipped, not just that the banner text
    // happens to coexist with it.
    CHECK_FALSE(contains(code, "decompiled by hermit"));
    CHECK_FALSE(contains(code, "r0"));  // no register names -> disasm never ran
}

TEST_CASE("decompile: works on the \"show source\" arrow function too", "[decompiler]") {
    auto hbc = hbc::HBCFile::open(SHOW_SOURCE_HBC);
    const auto& fn = findFunc(hbc, "arrowShow");
    std::string code = hbc.decompile(fn.index);
    CHECK(contains(code, "ORIGINAL SOURCE"));
    CHECK(contains(code, "() => {"));
    CHECK(contains(code, "return 42;"));
}

TEST_CASE("decompile: \"hide source\"/\"sensitive\" functions decompile normally (no real source to show)", "[decompiler]") {
    auto hbc = hbc::HBCFile::open(SHOW_SOURCE_HBC);
    for (const char* name : {"hidden", "sensitiveFn"}) {
        const auto& fn = findFunc(hbc, name);
        std::string code = hbc.decompile(fn.index);
        CHECK(contains(code, "decompiled by hermit"));
        CHECK_FALSE(contains(code, "ORIGINAL SOURCE"));
    }
}

TEST_CASE("decompile: a function with no directive decompiles normally", "[decompiler]") {
    auto hbc = hbc::HBCFile::open(SHOW_SOURCE_HBC);
    const auto& fn = findFunc(hbc, "normal");
    std::string code = hbc.decompile(fn.index);
    CHECK(contains(code, "decompiled by hermit"));
    CHECK_FALSE(contains(code, "ORIGINAL SOURCE"));
}
```

`tests/unit/disassembler/test_disassembler.cpp`:

```cpp
// =============================================================================
// test_disassembler.cpp - Catch2 tests for the Disassembler
// =============================================================================
// All tests use hello.hbc (2 functions: global, greet) and
// control_flow.hbc (max, factorial with conditional jumps).
// The file paths are injected by CMake via HBC_CORPUS_DIR.
// =============================================================================

#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>
#include <catch2/matchers/catch_matchers_string.hpp>

#include "hbc/hbc.h"

#include <string>
#include <vector>

using namespace Catch::Matchers;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Helper: finds the first instruction with a given mnemonic
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
static const hbc::Instruction* findInstr(
    const std::vector<hbc::Instruction>& instrs,
    const std::string& mnemonic)
{
    for (const auto& i : instrs)
        if (i.mnemonic == mnemonic) return &i;
    return nullptr;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Test 1: disasm(0) on hello.hbc is not empty
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
TEST_CASE("disasm returns non-empty for global function", "[disassembler]") {
    auto f = hbc::HBCFile::open(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/hello.hbc");
    auto instrs = f.disasm(f.header().globalCodeIndex);
    REQUIRE(!instrs.empty());
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Test 2: first instruction at offset 0
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
TEST_CASE("first instruction has offset zero", "[disassembler]") {
    auto f = hbc::HBCFile::open(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/hello.hbc");
    auto instrs = f.disasm(f.header().globalCodeIndex);
    REQUIRE(!instrs.empty());
    REQUIRE(instrs.front().offset == 0u);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Test 3: no "???" instruction in hello.hbc (all opcodes known)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
TEST_CASE("no unknown opcodes in hello.hbc", "[disassembler]") {
    auto f = hbc::HBCFile::open(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/hello.hbc");
    for (uint32_t idx = 0; idx < f.header().functionCount; idx++) {
        auto instrs = f.disasm(idx);
        for (const auto& i : instrs) {
            INFO("Function " << idx << " offset 0x" << std::hex << i.offset
                 << ": opcode 0x" << (int)i.opcode);
            REQUIRE(i.mnemonic != "???");
        }
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Test 4: at least one StringID operand resolves to "Hello, " or "!"
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
TEST_CASE("string operands resolve correctly", "[disassembler]") {
    auto f = hbc::HBCFile::open(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/hello.hbc");
    // The greet function (index 1) uses LoadConstString with "Hello, " and "!"
    auto instrs = f.disasm(1);

    bool foundHello = false;
    bool foundBang  = false;
    for (const auto& i : instrs) {
        for (const auto& op : i.operands) {
            if (op.type == hbc::Operand::Type::StringID) {
                if (op.resolvedString.find("Hello, ") != std::string::npos) foundHello = true;
                if (op.resolvedString.find("!")       != std::string::npos) foundBang  = true;
            }
        }
    }
    REQUIRE(foundHello);
    REQUIRE(foundBang);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Test 5: disasm is deterministic (two calls produce the same result)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
TEST_CASE("disasm is deterministic", "[disassembler]") {
    auto f = hbc::HBCFile::open(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/hello.hbc");
    auto a = f.disasm(1);
    auto b = f.disasm(1);
    REQUIRE(a.size() == b.size());
    for (size_t i = 0; i < a.size(); i++) {
        REQUIRE(a[i].mnemonic == b[i].mnemonic);
        REQUIRE(a[i].offset   == b[i].offset);
        REQUIRE(a[i].operands.size() == b[i].operands.size());
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Test 6: greet (index 1) contains at least one LoadParam
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
TEST_CASE("greet function contains LoadParam", "[disassembler]") {
    auto f = hbc::HBCFile::open(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/hello.hbc");
    // greet function: paramCount == 2 (this + name). Must have LoadParam.
    auto instrs = f.disasm(1);
    REQUIRE(findInstr(instrs, "LoadParam") != nullptr);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Test 7: greet ends with Ret
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
TEST_CASE("greet function ends with Ret", "[disassembler]") {
    auto f = hbc::HBCFile::open(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/hello.hbc");
    auto instrs = f.disasm(1);
    REQUIRE(!instrs.empty());
    REQUIRE(instrs.back().mnemonic == "Ret");
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Test 8: control_flow.hbc - max() contains a conditional jump
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
TEST_CASE("control flow function contains conditional jump", "[disassembler]") {
    auto f = hbc::HBCFile::open(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/control_flow.hbc");
    // Search all functions (except the global one) for at least one conditional jump
    // (JmpTrue, JmpFalse, JLess, JGreater, etc. prefixed with J but not plain Jmp)
    bool foundCondJump = false;
    for (uint32_t idx = 0; idx < f.header().functionCount; idx++) {
        auto instrs = f.disasm(idx);
        for (const auto& i : instrs) {
            const std::string& m = i.mnemonic;
            // A conditional jump starts with "J" but isn't "Jmp" or "JmpLong"
            if (m.size() > 1 && m[0] == 'J' &&
                m != "Jmp" && m != "JmpLong") {
                foundCondJump = true;
                break;
            }
        }
        if (foundCondJump) break;
    }
    REQUIRE(foundCondJump);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Test 9: isGenerator gets updated after disasm (stub -> real value)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
TEST_CASE("isGenerator detection via opcode scan", "[disassembler]") {
    // hello.hbc has no generators - functions must have isGenerator=false
    auto f = hbc::HBCFile::open(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/hello.hbc");
    for (uint32_t idx = 0; idx < f.header().functionCount; idx++) {
        f.disasm(idx);  // trigger detection
        REQUIRE_FALSE(f.functions()[idx].isGenerator);
        REQUIRE_FALSE(f.functions()[idx].isAsync);
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Test 10: out-of-range functionIndex throws an exception
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
TEST_CASE("disasm throws on invalid function index", "[disassembler]") {
    auto f = hbc::HBCFile::open(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/hello.hbc");
    REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(f.disasm(999), std::out_of_range);
}
```

`tests/unit/function-table/test_function_table.cpp`:

```cpp
// =============================================================================
// test_function_table.cpp - Catch2 tests for the function table parser
// =============================================================================
// Tests parseFunctionTable() (via HBCFile::functions()) and
// parseStringKinds() (via HBCFile::stringKinds()) on hello.hbc.
//
// hello.hbc is compiled from seeder/samples/hello.ts, which contains:
//   function greet(message: string) { console.log("Hello, " + message); }
//   greet("world");
//
// Expected structure in hello.hbc:
//   - 2 functions: the global function (index = globalCodeIndex) and "greet"
//   - 8 strings: "!", "Hello, ", "global", "hermit", "use strict",
//                 "log", "console", "greet"
//   - String kinds: "log", "console", "greet" -> Identifier; "!" -> String
// =============================================================================

// Catch2 v3: CATCH_CONFIG_MAIN is not needed with Catch2WithMain.
// The `Catch2::Catch2WithMain` CMake target provides main() automatically.
#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>

#include "hbc/hbc.h"   // HBCFile, FunctionInfo, StringKind

#include <algorithm>   // std::find_if
#include <string>

// HBC_CORPUS_DIR is injected by CMake as a preprocessor define:
//   target_compile_definitions(hermit_tests PRIVATE HBC_CORPUS_DIR="...")
// Converting it to std::string lets us use operator+ for paths.
static const std::string HELLO       = std::string(HBC_CORPUS_DIR) + "/hello.hbc";
static const std::string SHOW_SOURCE = std::string(HBC_CORPUS_DIR) + "/show_source.hbc";

static const hbc::FunctionInfo& findFunc(const hbc::HBCFile& f, const std::string& name) {
    auto it = std::find_if(
        f.functions().begin(), f.functions().end(),
        [&](const hbc::FunctionInfo& fi) { return fi.name == name; }
    );
    REQUIRE(it != f.functions().end());
    return *it;
}

// =============================================================================
// Test 1: the function count matches the header
// =============================================================================
TEST_CASE("function count matches header.functionCount", "[function-table][functions]") {
    hbc::HBCFile f = hbc::HBCFile::open(HELLO);
    // functions() must return exactly functionCount elements.
    // If the parser's loop stops too early or too late, this fails.
    REQUIRE(f.functions().size() == f.header().functionCount);
}

// =============================================================================
// Test 2: the global function exists and has a valid offset
// =============================================================================
TEST_CASE("global function exists and has valid offset", "[function-table][functions]") {
    hbc::HBCFile f = hbc::HBCFile::open(HELLO);
    const auto& funcs = f.functions();
    const uint32_t gi = f.header().globalCodeIndex;

    // globalCodeIndex must be a valid index into the vector.
    REQUIRE(gi < funcs.size());

    // The global function's offset must be > 0: the bytecode can't
    // start at offset 0 (that's where the file header is).
    REQUIRE(funcs[gi].offset > 0);

    // The global function has index == globalCodeIndex (sanity check field).
    REQUIRE(funcs[gi].index == gi);
}

// =============================================================================
// Test 3: no function has name == "" (anonymous ones use "anonymous_func_N")
// =============================================================================
TEST_CASE("no function has empty name", "[function-table][functions]") {
    hbc::HBCFile f = hbc::HBCFile::open(HELLO);

    // std::find_if looks for the first element satisfying the predicate.
    // If none satisfies it, it returns end() - which is what we want.
    auto it = std::find_if(
        f.functions().begin(), f.functions().end(),
        [](const hbc::FunctionInfo& fi) { return fi.name.empty(); }
    );
    // Check that no empty name was found.
    REQUIRE(it == f.functions().end());
}

// =============================================================================
// Test 4: hello.hbc contains the function "greet"
// =============================================================================
TEST_CASE("hello.hbc contains function named greet", "[function-table][functions]") {
    hbc::HBCFile f = hbc::HBCFile::open(HELLO);

    auto it = std::find_if(
        f.functions().begin(), f.functions().end(),
        [](const hbc::FunctionInfo& fi) { return fi.name == "greet"; }
    );
    REQUIRE(it != f.functions().end());

    // FINDING: paramCount includes the implicit `this` parameter.
    // greet(message) has 1 JS parameter, but Hermes also counts `this`,
    // so paramCount == 2. To compute the number of user-visible JS
    // parameters: paramCount - 1.
    REQUIRE(it->paramCount == 2);
}

// =============================================================================
// Test 5: functions() is idempotent (the cache works)
// =============================================================================
TEST_CASE("functions() is idempotent (cache)", "[function-table][functions]") {
    hbc::HBCFile f = hbc::HBCFile::open(HELLO);

    // Consecutive calls must return the same object in memory.
    // &a == &b means both const& point to the same vector -
    // the parser didn't re-run parsing, it returned the cache.
    const auto& a = f.functions();
    const auto& b = f.functions();
    REQUIRE(&a == &b);
}

// =============================================================================
// Test 6: stringKinds() has the same size as strings() (parallel vectors)
// =============================================================================
TEST_CASE("stringKinds().size() == strings().size()", "[function-table][stringkinds]") {
    hbc::HBCFile f = hbc::HBCFile::open(HELLO);
    // The two vectors must be parallel: kinds[i] describes strings()[i].
    REQUIRE(f.stringKinds().size() == f.strings().size());
}

// =============================================================================
// Test 7: in hello.hbc, "log", "console", "greet" are Identifier; "!" is String
// =============================================================================
TEST_CASE("string kinds match expected values in hello.hbc", "[function-table][stringkinds]") {
    hbc::HBCFile f = hbc::HBCFile::open(HELLO);
    const auto& strs  = f.strings();
    const auto& kinds = f.stringKinds();

    // Helper lambda: looks up string s and returns its kind.
    // Throws std::logic_error if the string isn't in the bundle - this
    // would fail the test with a clear message.
    auto kind_of = [&](const std::string& s) -> hbc::StringKind {
        for (size_t i = 0; i < strs.size(); ++i) {
            if (strs[i] == s) return kinds[i];
        }
        throw std::logic_error("String not found in bundle: " + s);
    };

    // "log", "console", "greet" are property names -> Identifier.
    REQUIRE(kind_of("log")     == hbc::StringKind::Identifier);
    REQUIRE(kind_of("console") == hbc::StringKind::Identifier);
    REQUIRE(kind_of("greet")   == hbc::StringKind::Identifier);

    // "!" is a runtime string literal -> String.
    REQUIRE(kind_of("!")       == hbc::StringKind::String);
}

// =============================================================================
// Test 8: stringKinds() is idempotent (the cache works)
// =============================================================================
TEST_CASE("stringKinds() is idempotent (cache)", "[function-table][stringkinds]") {
    hbc::HBCFile f = hbc::HBCFile::open(HELLO);
    const auto& a = f.stringKinds();
    const auto& b = f.stringKinds();
    REQUIRE(&a == &b);
}

// =============================================================================
// Function Source Table (header 0x64 functionSourceCount) - addendum found
// while writing thesis chapter 5.6. show_source.hbc is compiled from
// seeder/samples/show_source.js, which exercises Hermes' three
// SourceVisibility directives (opt-in, first statement of the function body,
// same mechanism as "use strict" - see Sema/SemanticResolver.cpp in the
// Hermes source):
//   withComment() { "show source"; ... }   -> real source preserved verbatim
//   arrowShow     = () => { "show source"; ... }  -> same, arrow function
//   hidden()      { "hide source"; ... }   -> entry present, but EMPTY (marker)
//   sensitiveFn() { "sensitive"; ... }     -> same as hide source
//   normal()      { /* no directive */ }   -> NO entry at all (not even empty)
// Verified against `hermes -dump-bytecode` before writing this parser.
// =============================================================================

TEST_CASE("show source: real source is preserved verbatim, directive included", "[function-table][functionsource]") {
    hbc::HBCFile f = hbc::HBCFile::open(SHOW_SOURCE);
    const auto& fi = findFunc(f, "withComment");

    REQUIRE(fi.hasPreservedSource);
    REQUIRE_FALSE(fi.sourceIsHidden);
    // Byte-exact: the directive itself and the comment are part of the
    // preserved text, not stripped - this is NOT a re-serialized AST.
    REQUIRE(fi.preservedSource.find("function withComment()") != std::string::npos);
    REQUIRE(fi.preservedSource.find("\"show source\";") != std::string::npos);
    REQUIRE(fi.preservedSource.find("// a comment inside the function") != std::string::npos);
    REQUIRE(fi.preservedSource.find("return x + 1;") != std::string::npos);
}

TEST_CASE("show source: works on an arrow function too, range excludes the `var` wrapper", "[function-table][functionsource]") {
    hbc::HBCFile f = hbc::HBCFile::open(SHOW_SOURCE);
    const auto& fi = findFunc(f, "arrowShow");

    REQUIRE(fi.hasPreservedSource);
    REQUIRE_FALSE(fi.sourceIsHidden);
    // Starts at the function expression itself, not at "var arrowShow = ".
    REQUIRE(fi.preservedSource.rfind("() => {", 0) == 0);
    REQUIRE(fi.preservedSource.find("return 42;") != std::string::npos);
}

TEST_CASE("hide source / sensitive: entry present but resolves to an empty marker", "[function-table][functionsource]") {
    hbc::HBCFile f = hbc::HBCFile::open(SHOW_SOURCE);

    for (const char* name : {"hidden", "sensitiveFn"}) {
        const auto& fi = findFunc(f, name);
        REQUIRE(fi.hasPreservedSource);
        REQUIRE(fi.sourceIsHidden);
        REQUIRE(fi.preservedSource.empty());
    }
}

TEST_CASE("no directive: no entry at all in the Function Source Table", "[function-table][functionsource]") {
    hbc::HBCFile f = hbc::HBCFile::open(SHOW_SOURCE);
    const auto& fi = findFunc(f, "normal");
    // Not just "empty" like hide source/sensitive - genuinely absent.
    REQUIRE_FALSE(fi.hasPreservedSource);
    REQUIRE_FALSE(fi.sourceIsHidden);
    REQUIRE(fi.preservedSource.empty());
}

TEST_CASE("global function has no Function Source Table entry", "[function-table][functionsource]") {
    // Sanity check: functionSourceCount in show_source.hbc covers exactly the
    // 4 functions with a directive (withComment, hidden, sensitiveFn,
    // arrowShow) - the implicit global wrapper isn't one of them.
    hbc::HBCFile f = hbc::HBCFile::open(SHOW_SOURCE);
    const auto& funcs = f.functions();
    uint32_t withEntry = 0;
    for (const auto& fi : funcs) if (fi.hasPreservedSource) withEntry++;
    REQUIRE(withEntry == f.header().functionSourceCount);
    REQUIRE(withEntry == 4);
}
```

`tests/unit/header/test_header.cpp`:

```cpp
#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>
#include "hbc/hbc.h"
#include "hbc/format.h"

#include <cstdint>
#include <cstring>
#include <filesystem>
#include <fstream>
#include <stdexcept>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

// HBC_CORPUS_DIR is injected by CMake so tests can find corpus files regardless
// of the working directory from which the test binary is run.
#ifndef HBC_CORPUS_DIR
#  error "HBC_CORPUS_DIR must be set by CMake"
#endif

static const std::string HELLO_HBC = std::string(HBC_CORPUS_DIR) + "/hello.hbc";

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Helpers
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// Write a minimal synthetic HBC file with the given magic and version so we
// can test error paths without depending on real HBC files.
static std::string make_synthetic(uint64_t magic, uint32_t version) {
    // Allocate a 128-byte buffer (minimum header size) and fill with zeros.
    std::vector<uint8_t> buf(128, 0);
    std::memcpy(buf.data() + 0, &magic,   sizeof(magic));
    std::memcpy(buf.data() + 8, &version, sizeof(version));

    auto path = std::filesystem::temp_directory_path() /
                ("hermit_test_" + std::to_string(version) + ".hbc");
    std::ofstream f(path, std::ios::binary);
    f.write(reinterpret_cast<const char*>(buf.data()), static_cast<std::streamsize>(buf.size()));
    return path.string();
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Smoke tests - basic open + version
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

TEST_CASE("hello.hbc has the correct magic", "[header][smoke]") {
    auto f = hbc::HBCFile::open(HELLO_HBC);
    REQUIRE(f.header().magic == hbc::HBC_MAGIC);
}

TEST_CASE("hello.hbc has version 96", "[header][smoke]") {
```

`tests/unit/patcher/test_encoder.cpp`:

```cpp
// =============================================================================
// test_encoder.cpp - Catch2 tests for the instruction encoder
// =============================================================================
// hbc::encode_instruction() is the inverse of the disassembler's decodeOperand().
// Strong guarantee: for every "clean" function in the corpus,
//   encode_instruction(version, ins.opcode, values) == the instruction's raw bytes
// The file paths are injected by CMake via HBC_CORPUS_DIR.
// =============================================================================

#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>

#include "hbc/hbc.h"
#include "test_util.h"

#include <cstdint>
#include <stdexcept>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

using hbc::Operand;
using testutil::opValue;

// Round-trip over every eligible function in a file: no "???" opcode and
// no SwitchImm (which has an appended jump table not represented by Instruction).
static void checkRoundTrip(const char* path) {
    auto f = hbc::HBCFile::open(path);
    const uint8_t* base = f.raw_data();
    const uint32_t version = f.version();
    const auto& funcs = f.functions();

    size_t checkedFns = 0, checkedInsns = 0;
    for (uint32_t idx = 0; idx < f.header().functionCount; ++idx) {
        const auto& fi = funcs[idx];
        auto instrs = f.disasm(idx);
        if (instrs.empty()) continue;

        bool clean = true;
        for (const auto& in : instrs) {
            if (in.mnemonic == "???" || in.mnemonic == "SwitchImm") { clean = false; break; }
        }
        if (!clean) continue;

        for (size_t i = 0; i < instrs.size(); ++i) {
            const auto& in = instrs[i];

            std::vector<double> vals;
            vals.reserve(in.operands.size());
            for (const auto& op : in.operands) vals.push_back(opValue(op));

            std::vector<uint8_t> got = hbc::encode_instruction(version, in.opcode, vals);

            INFO(path << " func " << idx << " @0x" << std::hex << in.offset
                      << " " << in.mnemonic);

            // The produced bytes must match the instruction's original ones.
            const uint8_t* p = base + fi.offset + in.offset;
            std::vector<uint8_t> expected(p, p + got.size());
            REQUIRE(got == expected);

            // For every instruction except the last we know the next one's
            // offset: the encoded length must match it exactly.
            if (i + 1 < instrs.size())
                REQUIRE(got.size() == instrs[i + 1].offset - in.offset);

            ++checkedInsns;
        }
        ++checkedFns;
    }
    INFO("functions checked: " << checkedFns << " · instructions: " << checkedInsns);
    REQUIRE(checkedFns > 0);
    REQUIRE(checkedInsns > 0);
}

TEST_CASE("encoder round-trips hello.hbc", "[patcher]") {
    checkRoundTrip(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/hello.hbc");
}

TEST_CASE("encoder round-trips control_flow.hbc", "[patcher]") {
    checkRoundTrip(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/control_flow.hbc");
}

TEST_CASE("encoder round-trips medium.hbc", "[patcher]") {
    checkRoundTrip(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/medium.hbc");
}

// A backward jump (negative Addr8) must re-encode into a single signed
// byte, identical to the original.
TEST_CASE("encoder handles backward Addr8 jump", "[patcher]") {
    auto f = hbc::HBCFile::open(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/control_flow.hbc");
    const uint32_t version = f.version();

    bool found = false;
    for (uint32_t idx = 0; idx < f.header().functionCount && !found; ++idx) {
        for (const auto& in : f.disasm(idx)) {
            int slot = -1;
            for (size_t j = 0; j < in.operands.size(); ++j)
                if (in.operands[j].type == Operand::Type::Addr8 && in.operands[j].i32 < 0)
                    slot = static_cast<int>(j);
            if (slot < 0) continue;

            std::vector<double> vals;
            for (const auto& op : in.operands) vals.push_back(opValue(op));
            auto got = hbc::encode_instruction(version, in.opcode, vals);

            // byte at the Addr8 operand's position: 1 + the offset of the preceding ones
            uint32_t at = 1;
            for (int j = 0; j < slot; ++j) at += hbc::operand_size(in.operands[j].type);
            REQUIRE(static_cast<int8_t>(got[at]) == in.operands[slot].i32);
            found = true;
            break;
        }
    }
    if (!found) WARN("no negative Addr8 operand in the corpus");
    SUCCEED();
}

TEST_CASE("encoder rejects wrong operand count", "[patcher]") {
    auto table = hbc::opcode_table(96);
    REQUIRE_FALSE(table.empty());

    const hbc::OpcodeDesc* one = nullptr;
    for (const auto& d : table)
        if (d.operands.size() == 1) { one = &d; break; }
    REQUIRE(one != nullptr);

    REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(hbc::encode_instruction(96, one->opcode, {}), std::invalid_argument);
}

TEST_CASE("encoder rejects unsupported version", "[patcher]") {
    REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(hbc::encode_instruction(999, 0, {}), std::invalid_argument);
}

TEST_CASE("encoder rejects out-of-range operand", "[patcher]") {
    auto table = hbc::opcode_table(96);
    const hbc::OpcodeDesc* reg = nullptr;
    for (const auto& d : table)
        if (d.operands.size() == 1 && d.operands[0] == Operand::Type::Reg8) { reg = &d; break; }
    REQUIRE(reg != nullptr);

    REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(hbc::encode_instruction(96, reg->opcode, { 999.0 }), std::range_error);
}

// --- HBCFile::from_bytes (re-parsing a patched image) ---------

TEST_CASE("from_bytes matches open", "[patcher]") {
    auto a = hbc::HBCFile::open(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/hello.hbc");
    std::string raw(reinterpret_cast<const char*>(a.raw_data()), a.raw_size());

    auto b = hbc::HBCFile::from_bytes(raw);
    REQUIRE(b.version() == a.version());
    REQUIRE(b.header().fileLength == a.header().fileLength);
    REQUIRE(b.functions().size() == a.functions().size());
    REQUIRE(b.strings() == a.strings());
    REQUIRE(b.serialize() == a.serialize());

    // handles a second round: re-parsing its own serialized bytes
    auto s = b.serialize();
    auto c = hbc::HBCFile::from_bytes(
        std::string(reinterpret_cast<const char*>(s.data()), s.size()));
    REQUIRE(c.serialize() == a.serialize());
}

TEST_CASE("from_bytes rejects garbage", "[patcher]") {
    REQUIRE_THROWS(hbc::HBCFile::from_bytes(std::string(200, '\0')));   // wrong magic
    REQUIRE_THROWS(hbc::HBCFile::from_bytes("short"));                  // too short
}
```

```cpp
// =============================================================================
// test_literals.cpp - literal-buffer sites + buffer accessors
// =============================================================================
// hbc::HBCFile::literal_sites() enumerates the NewArrayWithBuffer[Long] /
// NewObjectWithBuffer[Long] sites (function + bufferIdx). array_buffer() /
// obj_key_buffer() / obj_value_buffer() expose the three buffers' raw bytes
// (the SLP decode/encode lives in Python, cli/literals.py).
// HBC_CORPUS_DIR is injected by CMake.
// =============================================================================

#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>

#include "hbc/hbc.h"
#include "test_util.h"

#include <cstdint>
#include <fstream>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

using testutil::openOrSkip;

static const std::string MEDIUM = std::string(HBC_CORPUS_DIR) + "/medium.hbc";

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

TEST_CASE("literal_sites enumerates New{Array,Object}WithBuffer sites", "[patcher]") {
    auto f = hbc::HBCFile::open(MEDIUM);
    const auto& sites = f.literal_sites();

    REQUIRE(sites.size() == 2);
    bool sawArray = false, sawObject = false;
    for (const auto& s : sites) {
        REQUIRE(s.functionIndex < f.functions().size());
        if (s.isObject) {
            sawObject = true;
            REQUIRE(s.mnemonic == "NewObjectWithBuffer");
            REQUIRE(s.count == 3);
        } else {
            sawArray = true;
            REQUIRE(s.mnemonic == "NewArrayWithBuffer");
            REQUIRE(s.count == 4);
            REQUIRE(s.keyBufferIdx == 0);
        }
    }
    REQUIRE(sawArray);
    REQUIRE(sawObject);
}

TEST_CASE("array_buffer/obj_key_buffer/obj_value_buffer match the raw file bytes", "[patcher]") {
    auto f = hbc::HBCFile::open(MEDIUM);
    const auto& h = f.header();

    REQUIRE(f.array_buffer().size()     == h.arrayBufferSize);
    REQUIRE(f.obj_key_buffer().size()   == h.objKeyBufferSize);
    REQUIRE(f.obj_value_buffer().size() == h.objValueBufferSize);

    const uint8_t* raw = f.raw_data();
    REQUIRE(std::string(reinterpret_cast<const char*>(raw + f.array_buffer_offset()),
                        h.arrayBufferSize) == f.array_buffer());
    REQUIRE(std::string(reinterpret_cast<const char*>(raw + f.obj_key_buffer_offset()),
                        h.objKeyBufferSize) == f.obj_key_buffer());
    REQUIRE(std::string(reinterpret_cast<const char*>(raw + f.obj_value_buffer_offset()),
                        h.objValueBufferSize) == f.obj_value_buffer());
}

    auto f = hbc::HBCFile::open(MEDIUM);
    REQUIRE(&f.literal_sites() == &f.literal_sites());
}

    auto f = hbc::HBCFile::open(MEDIUM);
    auto bytes = f.serialize();
    auto g = hbc::HBCFile::from_bytes(std::string(bytes.begin(), bytes.end()));

    const auto& a = f.literal_sites();

        REQUIRE(a[i].mnemonic          == b[i].mnemonic);

        REQUIRE(a[i].bufferIdx         == b[i].bufferIdx);
        REQUIRE(a[i].keyBufferIdx      == b[i].keyBufferIdx);
```

`tests/unit/patcher/test_module.cpp`:

```cpp
// =============================================================================
// test_module.cpp - structural serializer + relocatable assembler
// =============================================================================
// hbc::Module rebuilds the file after inserting instructions into a
// function; hbc::assemble_function assigns offsets, runs branch relaxation
// (Addr8 -> Addr32) and fills in jump displacements (target given as an index).
// HBC_CORPUS_DIR is injected by CMake.
// =============================================================================

#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>
#include <catch2/matchers/catch_matchers_string.hpp>

#include "hbc/hbc.h"
#include "test_util.h"
#include "hbc/module.h"

#include <cstdint>
#include <cstring>
#include <fstream>
#include <optional>
#include <stdexcept>
#include <string>
#include <unordered_map>
#include <vector>

using hbc::Operand;
using testutil::openOrSkip;
using testutil::opValue;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// Builds the list of AsmInstr for a function, resolving jump targets to
// instruction INDICES.
static std::vector<hbc::AsmInstr> buildIr(const std::vector<hbc::Instruction>& ins) {
    auto tbl = hbc::opcode_table(96);
    std::unordered_map<uint8_t, const hbc::OpcodeDesc*> byOp;
    for (const auto& d : tbl) byOp[d.opcode] = &d;

    std::unordered_map<uint32_t, int32_t> off2idx;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < ins.size(); ++i) off2idx[ins[i].offset] = static_cast<int32_t>(i);

    std::vector<hbc::AsmInstr> ir;
    ir.reserve(ins.size());
    for (const auto& x : ins) {
        hbc::AsmInstr a;
        a.opcode = x.opcode;
        a.origByteOffset = static_cast<int32_t>(x.offset);
        for (const auto& o : x.operands) a.operands.push_back(opValue(o));

        auto it = byOp.find(x.opcode);
        if (it != byOp.end() &&
            (it->second->jumpKind == "Unconditional" || it->second->jumpKind == "Conditional")) {
            a.addrOperandPos = 0;
            uint32_t tgt = static_cast<uint32_t>(
                static_cast<int32_t>(x.offset) + x.operands[0].i32);
            auto ti = off2idx.find(tgt);
            a.jumpTargetIdx = (ti != off2idx.end()) ? ti->second : -1;
        }
        ir.push_back(std::move(a));
    }
    return ir;
}

static uint8_t opcodeOf(const char* mnemonic) {
    for (const auto& d : hbc::opcode_table(96))
        if (d.mnemonic == mnemonic) return d.opcode;
    throw std::runtime_error(std::string("opcode not found: ") + mnemonic);
}

static hbc::HBCFile reparse(const std::vector<uint8_t>& bytes) {
    return hbc::HBCFile::from_bytes(std::string(bytes.begin(), bytes.end()));
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Identity
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

static void checkModuleIdentity(const char* path) {
    auto f = openOrSkip(path);
    auto m = hbc::Module::from(f);
    REQUIRE(m.serialize() == f.serialize());
}

TEST_CASE("Module identity serialize", "[patcher]") {
    checkModuleIdentity(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/loop_sum_g0.hbc");
    checkModuleIdentity(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/try_catch_g0.hbc");   // with EH
    checkModuleIdentity(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/control_flow_g0.hbc");
    checkModuleIdentity(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/hello.hbc");          // -g1: debug blob
    checkModuleIdentity(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/control_flow.hbc");   // -g1
}

TEST_CASE("assemble_function is an identity when nothing is inserted", "[patcher]") {
    auto f = openOrSkip(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/control_flow_g0.hbc");
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < f.header().functionCount; ++i) {
        auto ins = f.disasm(i);
        bool skip = false;
        for (const auto& x : ins) if (x.mnemonic == "SwitchImm" || x.mnemonic == "???") skip = true;
        if (skip) continue;

        auto r = hbc::assemble_function(96, buildIr(ins));
        const auto& fi = f.functions()[i];
        std::vector<uint8_t> orig(f.raw_data() + fi.offset,
                                   f.raw_data() + fi.offset + fi.bytecodeSizeInBytes);
        INFO("function " << i << " " << f.functions()[i].name);
        REQUIRE(r.bytecode == orig);
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Insertion
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// Inserts `Mov r0,r0` (no-op) at `atIdx` in function `name`, re-serializes and
// returns the re-parsed file. `deltaOut` = bytes added.
static hbc::HBCFile insertNop(const char* path, const char* name, size_t atIdx,
                              size_t count, uint32_t* newSizeOut) {
    auto f = openOrSkip(path);
    uint32_t fidx = 0;
    for (const auto& fn : f.functions()) if (fn.name == name) fidx = fn.index;
    const auto& fi = f.functions()[fidx];

    auto ir = buildIr(f.disasm(fidx));
    for (auto& a : ir)
        if (a.jumpTargetIdx >= static_cast<int32_t>(atIdx))
            a.jumpTargetIdx += static_cast<int32_t>(count);

    hbc::AsmInstr nop;
    nop.opcode = opcodeOf("Mov");
    nop.operands = {0.0, 0.0};
    for (size_t k = 0; k < count; ++k) ir.insert(ir.begin() + atIdx, nop);

    auto m = hbc::Module::from(f);
    m.set_function_body(fidx, ir, fi.frameSize);
    auto out = m.serialize();
    *newSizeOut = 0;
    auto g = reparse(out);
    *newSizeOut = g.functions()[fidx].bytecodeSizeInBytes;
    return g;
}

TEST_CASE("insert a no-op grows the function and shifts later ones", "[patcher]") {
    auto f0 = openOrSkip(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/control_flow_g0.hbc");
    uint32_t maxIdx = 0, sumIdx = 0;
    for (const auto& fn : f0.functions()) {
        if (fn.name == "max")  maxIdx = fn.index;
        if (fn.name == "sumTo") sumIdx = fn.index;
    }
    uint32_t oldMax = f0.functions()[maxIdx].bytecodeSizeInBytes;
    uint32_t oldSumOff = f0.functions()[sumIdx].offset;

    uint32_t newSize = 0;
    auto g = insertNop(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/control_flow_g0.hbc", "max", 1, 1, &newSize);

    REQUIRE(newSize == oldMax + 3);                       // Mov = 1 + Reg8 + Reg8
    REQUIRE(g.functions()[sumIdx].offset == oldSumOff + 3);
    // disasm of the patched function: +1 instruction, all known
    auto ins = g.disasm(maxIdx);
    for (const auto& x : ins) REQUIRE(x.mnemonic != "???");
}

TEST_CASE("backward jump target is preserved after an insertion before it", "[patcher]") {
    // sumTo: idx 9 = backward JLessEqual (-10 -> 0x11). We insert right before it.
    auto f0 = openOrSkip(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/control_flow_g0.hbc");
    uint32_t sumIdx = 0;
    for (const auto& fn : f0.functions()) if (fn.name == "sumTo") sumIdx = fn.index;
    auto before = f0.disasm(sumIdx);
    // find the index of the backward jump
    int jIdx = -1;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < before.size(); ++i)
        if (!before[i].operands.empty() && before[i].mnemonic.rfind("J", 0) == 0 &&
            before[i].operands[0].i32 < 0)
            jIdx = static_cast<int>(i);
    REQUIRE(jIdx > 0);
    uint32_t origTargetByte =
        static_cast<uint32_t>(static_cast<int32_t>(before[jIdx].offset) + before[jIdx].operands[0].i32);

    uint32_t newSize = 0;
    auto g = insertNop(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/control_flow_g0.hbc", "sumTo",
                       static_cast<size_t>(jIdx), 1, &newSize);
    auto after = g.disasm(sumIdx);
    // the jump is now at jIdx+1; its absolute target must be the instruction
    // that used to be at origTargetByte (unchanged, it precedes the insertion point).
    const auto& j2 = after[static_cast<size_t>(jIdx) + 1];
    REQUIRE(j2.mnemonic.rfind("J", 0) == 0);
    uint32_t newTargetByte =
        static_cast<uint32_t>(static_cast<int32_t>(j2.offset) + j2.operands[0].i32);
    REQUIRE(newTargetByte == origTargetByte);
}

TEST_CASE("branch relaxation promotes a short jump to Long", "[patcher]") {
    // sumTo idx 5 = JmpFalse (Addr8). We insert 60 no-ops between the jump and the target.
    auto f0 = openOrSkip(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/control_flow_g0.hbc");
    uint32_t sumIdx = 0;
    for (const auto& fn : f0.functions()) if (fn.name == "sumTo") sumIdx = fn.index;

    uint32_t newSize = 0;
    auto g = insertNop(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/control_flow_g0.hbc", "sumTo", 6, 60, &newSize);
    auto ins = g.disasm(sumIdx);
    bool foundLong = false;
    for (const auto& x : ins) if (x.mnemonic == "JmpFalseLong") foundLong = true;
    REQUIRE(foundLong);
    REQUIRE(newSize == 33 + 60 * 3 + 3);   // 60*Mov(3) + relaxation (Addr8->Addr32 = +3)
}

TEST_CASE("exception handler offsets are relocated", "[patcher]") {
    auto f0 = openOrSkip(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/try_catch_g0.hbc");
    uint32_t rIdx = 0;
    for (const auto& fn : f0.functions()) if (fn.name == "risky") rIdx = fn.index;
    auto eh0 = f0.functions()[rIdx].exceptionHandlers;
    REQUIRE(eh0.size() >= 1);

    uint32_t newSize = 0;
    auto g = insertNop(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/try_catch_g0.hbc", "risky", 1, 1, &newSize);  // +3 bytes at idx 1 (offset > start)
    auto eh1 = g.functions()[rIdx].exceptionHandlers;
    REQUIRE(eh1.size() == eh0.size());
    for (size_t i = 0; i < eh0.size(); ++i) {
        REQUIRE(eh1[i].start  == eh0[i].start  + 3);
        REQUIRE(eh1[i].end    == eh0[i].end    + 3);
        REQUIRE(eh1[i].target == eh0[i].target + 3);
    }
}

// Removes instruction `atIdx` (must not be a jump target), re-serializes.
static hbc::HBCFile deleteInstr(const char* path, const char* name, size_t atIdx,
                                uint32_t* newSizeOut) {
    auto f = openOrSkip(path);
    uint32_t fidx = 0;
    for (const auto& fn : f.functions()) if (fn.name == name) fidx = fn.index;

    auto ir = buildIr(f.disasm(fidx));
    for (auto& a : ir) {
        REQUIRE(a.jumpTargetIdx != static_cast<int32_t>(atIdx));   // isn't a target
        if (a.jumpTargetIdx > static_cast<int32_t>(atIdx)) a.jumpTargetIdx -= 1;
    }
    ir.erase(ir.begin() + atIdx);

    auto m = hbc::Module::from(f);
    m.set_function_body(fidx, ir, f.functions()[fidx].frameSize);
    auto g = reparse(m.serialize());
    *newSizeOut = g.functions()[fidx].bytecodeSizeInBytes;
    return g;
}

TEST_CASE("delete an instruction shrinks the function and shifts later ones back", "[patcher]") {
    auto f0 = openOrSkip(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/control_flow_g0.hbc");
    uint32_t facIdx = 0, sumIdx = 0;
    for (const auto& fn : f0.functions()) {
        if (fn.name == "factorial") facIdx = fn.index;
        if (fn.name == "sumTo")     sumIdx = fn.index;
    }
    uint32_t oldFac    = f0.functions()[facIdx].bytecodeSizeInBytes;
    uint32_t oldSumOff = f0.functions()[sumIdx].offset;

    // factorial idx 3 = GetGlobalObject (not a jump, not a target): 2 bytes.
    auto ins3 = f0.disasm(facIdx)[3];
    REQUIRE(ins3.mnemonic == "GetGlobalObject");

    uint32_t newSize = 0;
    auto g = deleteInstr(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/control_flow_g0.hbc", "factorial", 3, &newSize);

    REQUIRE(newSize == oldFac - 2);
    REQUIRE(g.functions()[sumIdx].offset == oldSumOff - 2);
    for (const auto& x : g.disasm(facIdx)) REQUIRE(x.mnemonic != "???");
}

TEST_CASE("delete before a forward jump keeps its target", "[patcher]") {
    auto f0 = openOrSkip(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/control_flow_g0.hbc");
    uint32_t facIdx = 0;
    for (const auto& fn : f0.functions()) if (fn.name == "factorial") facIdx = fn.index;
    auto before = f0.disasm(facIdx);
    // idx 2 = forward JLessEqual; target = last instruction (Ret 0).
    REQUIRE(before[2].mnemonic.rfind("J", 0) == 0);
    uint32_t origTargetByte = static_cast<uint32_t>(
        static_cast<int32_t>(before[2].offset) + before[2].operands[0].i32);
    std::string tgtMnem;
    for (const auto& x : before) if (x.offset == origTargetByte) tgtMnem = x.mnemonic;
    REQUIRE(tgtMnem == "Ret");

    uint32_t newSize = 0;
    auto g = deleteInstr(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/control_flow_g0.hbc", "factorial", 3, &newSize);
    auto after = g.disasm(facIdx);
    const auto& j = after[2];
    uint32_t newTargetByte = static_cast<uint32_t>(
        static_cast<int32_t>(j.offset) + j.operands[0].i32);
    // the target must still be a Ret (the instruction itself wasn't touched)
    std::string m;
    for (const auto& x : after) if (x.offset == newTargetByte) m = x.mnemonic;
    REQUIRE(m == "Ret");
    REQUIRE(newTargetByte == origTargetByte - 2);   // the target moved by -2
}

TEST_CASE("frameSize bump is refused on a function with exception handlers", "[patcher]") {
    auto f = openOrSkip(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/try_catch_g0.hbc");
    uint32_t rIdx = 0;
    for (const auto& fn : f.functions()) if (fn.name == "risky") rIdx = fn.index;
    uint32_t frame = f.functions()[rIdx].frameSize;

    auto ir = buildIr(f.disasm(rIdx));
    hbc::AsmInstr nop; nop.opcode = opcodeOf("Mov"); nop.operands = {0.0, 0.0};
    ir.insert(ir.begin() + 1, nop);

    auto m = hbc::Module::from(f);
    REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(m.set_function_body(rIdx, ir, frame + 1), std::runtime_error);
    // same frameSize: ok
    REQUIRE_NOTHROW(m.set_function_body(rIdx, ir, frame));
}

TEST_CASE("Module refuses switch functions", "[patcher]") {
    try {
        auto f = hbc::HBCFile::open(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/switch.hbc");
        int swIdx = -1;
        for (uint32_t i = 0; i < f.header().functionCount; ++i)
            for (const auto& x : f.disasm(i))
                if (x.mnemonic == "SwitchImm") swIdx = static_cast<int>(i);
        if (swIdx >= 0) {
            auto m = hbc::Module::from(f);
            auto ir = buildIr(f.disasm(static_cast<uint32_t>(swIdx)));
            REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(
                m.set_function_body(static_cast<uint32_t>(swIdx), ir,
                                    f.functions()[static_cast<uint32_t>(swIdx)].frameSize),
                std::runtime_error);
        }
    } catch (const std::exception&) {
        // switch.hbc missing / has no SwitchImm - ok
    }
}

TEST_CASE("Module identity on a real bundle (overflow + non-monotonic + shared)", "[patcher]") {
    auto f = openOrSkip(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/ridemovi.hbc");   // 12.7 MB, gitignored
    auto m = hbc::Module::from(f);
    REQUIRE(m.serialize() == f.serialize());
}

TEST_CASE("Module identity on overflow_func.hbc", "[patcher]") {
    auto f = openOrSkip(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/overflow_func.hbc");
    auto m = hbc::Module::from(f);
    REQUIRE(m.serialize() == f.serialize());

// hermitvault.hbc - the thesis demo app, a real React Native bundle compiled
// as RN ships it (HBC 96, ~1.4 MB, Hermes V1 disabled). Gitignored: rebuild
// with `npm run build:hbc` in hermit-vault/. Unlike the toy samples it carries the
// full structure of a shipped bundle (Metro module system, many functions,
// UTF-16/CESU-8 strings), so proving the structural serializer reproduces it
// byte-for-byte anchors the round-trip claim on the application it is meant to
// analyse.
TEST_CASE("Module identity on hermitvault.hbc (demo app bundle)", "[patcher]") {
    auto f = openOrSkip(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/hermitvault.hbc");
    REQUIRE(f.version() == 96);

    // HBCFile baseline: the serialized copy equals the bytes on disk.
    auto raw = f.serialize();
    REQUIRE(raw.size() == f.header().fileLength);
    REQUIRE(raw.size() == f.raw_size());
    REQUIRE(std::memcmp(raw.data(), f.raw_data(), f.raw_size()) == 0);

    // Structural serializer: dismantle into sections and rebuild from scratch,
    // recomputing every offset. The result must be byte-identical.
    auto m = hbc::Module::from(f);
    REQUIRE(m.serialize() == f.serialize());
}

TEST_CASE("edit an overflowed function (same size, EH preserved)", "[patcher]") {
    auto f = openOrSkip(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/overflow_func.hbc");
    uint32_t ovIdx = 0;
    bool found = false;
    for (const auto& fn : f.functions())
        if (fn.overflowed) { ovIdx = fn.index; found = true; }
    REQUIRE(found);
    const auto& fi = f.functions()[ovIdx];
    REQUIRE(fi.frameSize > 127);   // precisely because it's overflowed

    auto ins = f.disasm(ovIdx);
    int row = -1;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < ins.size(); ++i)
        if (ins[i].mnemonic == "LoadConstUndefined") { row = static_cast<int>(i); break; }
    REQUIRE(row >= 0);

    auto ir = buildIr(ins);
    ir[static_cast<size_t>(row)].opcode = opcodeOf("LoadConstNull");   // same signature {Reg8}

    auto m = hbc::Module::from(f);
    m.set_function_body(ovIdx, ir, fi.frameSize);
    auto g = reparse(m.serialize());
    const auto& gi = g.functions()[ovIdx];
    REQUIRE(gi.overflowed);
    REQUIRE(gi.bytecodeSizeInBytes == fi.bytecodeSizeInBytes);
    REQUIRE(gi.frameSize == fi.frameSize);
    REQUIRE(g.disasm(ovIdx)[static_cast<size_t>(row)].mnemonic == "LoadConstNull");
    for (const auto& x : g.disasm(ovIdx)) REQUIRE(x.mnemonic != "???");
}

TEST_CASE("insert into an overflowed function relocates EH and largeOff", "[patcher]") {
    auto f = openOrSkip(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/overflow_func.hbc");
    uint32_t ovIdx = 0;
    for (const auto& fn : f.functions()) if (fn.overflowed) ovIdx = fn.index;
    const auto& fi = f.functions()[ovIdx];
    auto eh0 = fi.exceptionHandlers;
    REQUIRE(eh0.size() >= 1);

    auto ir = buildIr(f.disasm(ovIdx));
    hbc::AsmInstr nop; nop.opcode = opcodeOf("Mov"); nop.operands = {0.0, 0.0};
    for (auto& a : ir) if (a.jumpTargetIdx >= 1) a.jumpTargetIdx += 1;
    ir.insert(ir.begin() + 1, nop);                  // +3 bytes at instruction 1's offset

    auto m = hbc::Module::from(f);
    m.set_function_body(ovIdx, ir, fi.frameSize);
    auto g = reparse(m.serialize());
    const auto& gi = g.functions()[ovIdx];
    REQUIRE(gi.overflowed);
    REQUIRE(gi.bytecodeSizeInBytes == fi.bytecodeSizeInBytes + 3);
    auto eh1 = gi.exceptionHandlers;
    REQUIRE(eh1.size() == eh0.size());
    for (size_t i = 0; i < eh0.size(); ++i) {
        REQUIRE(eh1[i].start  == eh0[i].start  + 3);
        REQUIRE(eh1[i].end    == eh0[i].end    + 3);
        REQUIRE(eh1[i].target == eh0[i].target + 3);
    }
    for (const auto& x : g.disasm(ovIdx)) REQUIRE(x.mnemonic != "???");
}

TEST_CASE("shared bytecode: refuse without editAll, apply with editAll", "[patcher]") {
    auto f = openOrSkip(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/ridemovi.hbc");
    const auto& funcs = f.functions();
    // a function with shared body, not overflow, without EH
    int sIdx = -1;
    for (const auto& fn : funcs)
        if (fn.shared && !fn.overflowed && !fn.hasExceptionHandler) { sIdx = static_cast<int>(fn.index); break; }
    REQUIRE(sIdx >= 0);
    const auto& sfi = funcs[static_cast<uint32_t>(sIdx)];
    REQUIRE(sfi.shareCount >= 2);

    auto ir = buildIr(f.disasm(static_cast<uint32_t>(sIdx)));   // identical re-encode

    {
        auto m = hbc::Module::from(f);
        REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(
            m.set_function_body(static_cast<uint32_t>(sIdx), ir, sfi.frameSize, /*editAll=*/false),
            std::runtime_error);
    }
    {
        auto m = hbc::Module::from(f);
        m.set_function_body(static_cast<uint32_t>(sIdx), ir, sfi.frameSize, /*editAll=*/true);
        // identical re-encode -> byte-identical file
        REQUIRE(m.serialize() == f.serialize());
    }
}

// Inserts `Mov r0,r0` before instruction 1 of `fidx` and applies it with
// editAll to the whole shared group. Every EH boundary other than 0 is at or
// after instruction 1, so it must move by exactly +3.
static std::vector<hbc::AsmInstr> nopAt1(const hbc::HBCFile& f, uint32_t fidx) {
    auto ir = buildIr(f.disasm(fidx));
    for (auto& a : ir) if (a.jumpTargetIdx >= 1) a.jumpTargetIdx += 1;
    hbc::AsmInstr nop; nop.opcode = opcodeOf("Mov"); nop.operands = {0.0, 0.0};
    ir.insert(ir.begin() + 1, nop);
    return ir;
}

static void requireEhShifted(const std::vector<hbc::ExceptionHandlerInfo>& eh0,
                             const std::vector<hbc::ExceptionHandlerInfo>& eh1) {
    auto moved = [](uint32_t v) { return v == 0 ? 0u : v + 3; };
    REQUIRE(eh1.size() == eh0.size());
    for (size_t i = 0; i < eh0.size(); ++i) {
        REQUIRE(eh1[i].start  == moved(eh0[i].start));
        REQUIRE(eh1[i].end    == moved(eh0[i].end));
        REQUIRE(eh1[i].target == moved(eh0[i].target));
    }
}

TEST_CASE("editAll relocates the EH table of every member of the group (real bundle)", "[patcher]") {
    // ridemovi.hbc has shared groups whose members ALL carry an exception
    // handler (identical bodies with try/catch -> identical EH tables, one per
    // entry). Editing through any member must relocate every member's table.
    auto f = openOrSkip(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/ridemovi.hbc");
    const auto& funcs = f.functions();

    std::unordered_map<uint32_t, std::vector<uint32_t>> byOff;
    for (const auto& fn : funcs) byOff[fn.offset].push_back(fn.index);

    std::vector<uint32_t> group;
    for (const auto& [off, members] : byOff) {
        if (members.size() < 2) continue;
        bool ok = true;
        for (uint32_t i : members)
            if (!funcs[i].hasExceptionHandler || funcs[i].overflowed) ok = false;
        if (!ok) continue;
        for (const auto& x : f.disasm(members[0]))
            if (x.mnemonic == "SwitchImm" || x.mnemonic.rfind("SaveGenerator", 0) == 0 ||
                x.mnemonic == "???") ok = false;
        if (ok) { group = members; break; }
    }
    if (group.empty()) SKIP("no shared group with EH on every member in ridemovi.hbc");

    // edit through the first and through the last member: the result must not
    // depend on which member of the group was opened
    for (uint32_t dirtyIdx : {group.front(), group.back()}) {
        INFO("editing through function " << dirtyIdx);
        auto m = hbc::Module::from(f);
        m.set_function_body(dirtyIdx, nopAt1(f, dirtyIdx), funcs[dirtyIdx].frameSize, /*editAll=*/true);
        auto g = reparse(m.serialize());
        for (uint32_t i : group) {
            INFO("member " << i);
            REQUIRE(g.functions()[i].bytecodeSizeInBytes == funcs[i].bytecodeSizeInBytes + 3);
            REQUIRE(g.functions()[i].offset == g.functions()[group.front()].offset);
            requireEhShifted(funcs[i].exceptionHandlers, g.functions()[i].exceptionHandlers);
        }
    }
}

// Builds a mixed shared group on try_catch_g0.hbc: function `other` (no EH) is
// repointed at the body of `risky` (EH). No real file has such a group, but
// it is the case where the EH member is NOT the function being edited.
static std::string mixedSharedGroup(const hbc::HBCFile& f, uint32_t riskyIdx, uint32_t otherIdx) {
    std::string bytes(reinterpret_cast<const char*>(f.raw_data()), f.raw_size());
    auto* fh = reinterpret_cast<hbc::SmallFuncHeader*>(bytes.data() + sizeof(hbc::HBCFileHeader));
    fh[otherIdx].offset              = fh[riskyIdx].offset;
    fh[otherIdx].bytecodeSizeInBytes = fh[riskyIdx].bytecodeSizeInBytes;
    return bytes;
}

TEST_CASE("editAll through a member without EH relocates the EH of another member", "[patcher]") {
    auto f0 = openOrSkip(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/try_catch_g0.hbc");
    int rIdx = -1, oIdx = -1;
    for (const auto& fn : f0.functions()) {
        if (fn.name == "risky") rIdx = static_cast<int>(fn.index);
        else if (!fn.hasExceptionHandler && !fn.overflowed && oIdx < 0) oIdx = static_cast<int>(fn.index);
    }
    REQUIRE(rIdx >= 0);
    REQUIRE(oIdx >= 0);
    const auto r = static_cast<uint32_t>(rIdx), o = static_cast<uint32_t>(oIdx);

    auto f = hbc::HBCFile::from_bytes(mixedSharedGroup(f0, r, o));
    REQUIRE(f.functions()[o].shared);
    REQUIRE(f.functions()[r].shared);
    REQUIRE_FALSE(f.functions()[o].hasExceptionHandler);
    const uint32_t frame = f.functions()[o].frameSize;
    auto ir = nopAt1(f, o);

    auto m = hbc::Module::from(f);
    m.set_function_body(o, ir, frame, /*editAll=*/true);
    auto g = reparse(m.serialize());

    for (uint32_t i : {r, o})
        REQUIRE(g.functions()[i].bytecodeSizeInBytes == f.functions()[i].bytecodeSizeInBytes + 3);
    REQUIRE(g.functions()[r].offset == g.functions()[o].offset);
    requireEhShifted(f.functions()[r].exceptionHandlers, g.functions()[r].exceptionHandlers);
    for (const auto& x : g.disasm(r)) REQUIRE(x.mnemonic != "???");
}

TEST_CASE("editAll refuses a frameSize bump if any member of the group has EH", "[patcher]") {
    auto f0 = openOrSkip(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/try_catch_g0.hbc");
    int rIdx = -1, oIdx = -1;
    for (const auto& fn : f0.functions()) {
        if (fn.name == "risky") rIdx = static_cast<int>(fn.index);
        else if (!fn.hasExceptionHandler && !fn.overflowed && oIdx < 0) oIdx = static_cast<int>(fn.index);
    }
    REQUIRE(rIdx >= 0);
    REQUIRE(oIdx >= 0);
    const auto r = static_cast<uint32_t>(rIdx), o = static_cast<uint32_t>(oIdx);

    auto f = hbc::HBCFile::from_bytes(mixedSharedGroup(f0, r, o));
    const uint32_t frame = f.functions()[o].frameSize;
    auto ir = nopAt1(f, o);

    auto m = hbc::Module::from(f);
    // the opened function has no EH, but `risky` in the same group does:
    // the new frameSize would be written on it too
    REQUIRE_THROWS_WITH(m.set_function_body(o, ir, frame + 1, /*editAll=*/true),
                        Catch::Matchers::ContainsSubstring("exception handler"));
    // same frameSize: ok
    REQUIRE_NOTHROW(m.set_function_body(o, ir, frame, /*editAll=*/true));
}

TEST_CASE("editing a function with a lower offset than a lower-index one is local", "[patcher]") {
    auto f = openOrSkip(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/ridemovi.hbc");
    const auto& funcs = f.functions();
    // find i, j with i < j but offset[j] < offset[i]  (non-monotonic layout)
    int hi = -1, lo = -1;
    for (uint32_t k = 1; k < funcs.size(); ++k)
        if (funcs[k].offset < funcs[k - 1].offset &&
            !funcs[k].overflowed && !funcs[k - 1].overflowed) {
            hi = static_cast<int>(k - 1);   // lower index, higher offset
            lo = static_cast<int>(k);       // higher index, lower offset
            break;
        }
    REQUIRE(lo >= 0);
    REQUIRE(funcs[static_cast<uint32_t>(lo)].offset < funcs[static_cast<uint32_t>(hi)].offset);

    auto irLo = buildIr(f.disasm(static_cast<uint32_t>(lo)));
    auto m = hbc::Module::from(f);
    m.set_function_body(static_cast<uint32_t>(lo), irLo,
                        funcs[static_cast<uint32_t>(lo)].frameSize,
                        funcs[static_cast<uint32_t>(lo)].shared);
    auto g = reparse(m.serialize());

    // function hi (higher offset) wasn't touched by the disasm
    auto a = f.disasm(static_cast<uint32_t>(hi));
    auto b = g.disasm(static_cast<uint32_t>(hi));
    REQUIRE(a.size() == b.size());
    for (size_t i = 0; i < a.size(); ++i) REQUIRE(a[i].mnemonic == b[i].mnemonic);
}

// =========================================================================
// add_string + multi-section rebuild
// =========================================================================

// Compares the disasm (mnemonic + operands) of every function between two files:
// add_string moves bodies as blocks, it doesn't resize them.
static void requireAllFunctionsUnchanged(hbc::HBCFile& a, hbc::HBCFile& b) {
    REQUIRE(a.functions().size() == b.functions().size());
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < a.functions().size(); ++i) {
        auto x = a.disasm(i);
        auto y = b.disasm(i);
        REQUIRE(x.size() == y.size());
        for (size_t k = 0; k < x.size(); ++k) {
            REQUIRE(x[k].mnemonic == y[k].mnemonic);
            REQUIRE(x[k].operands.size() == y[k].operands.size());
            for (size_t o = 0; o < x[k].operands.size(); ++o)
                REQUIRE(opValue(x[k].operands[o]) == opValue(y[k].operands[o]));
        }
    }
}

TEST_CASE("Module identity holds on a file with literal buffers (align fix)", "[patcher]") {
    // medium.hbc has non-empty array/object buffers: before section_map's fix
    // (align 1 -> 4 on the buffers) the per-section re-layout lost the padding
    // before "array buffer" and shifted the bytecode by 4.
    auto f = openOrSkip(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/medium.hbc");
    REQUIRE(f.header().arrayBufferSize + f.header().objKeyBufferSize +
            f.header().objValueBufferSize > 0);
    auto m = hbc::Module::from(f);
    REQUIRE(m.serialize() == f.serialize());
}

TEST_CASE("add_string appends a String and shifts everything after", "[patcher]") {
    auto f = hbc::HBCFile::open(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/hello.hbc");
    const auto  h0     = f.header();
    const auto  n0     = h0.stringCount;
    const auto  store0 = h0.stringStorageSize;
    const auto  kinds0 = h0.stringKindCount;

    auto m   = hbc::Module::from(f);
    uint32_t idx = m.add_string("hi");
    REQUIRE(idx == n0);
    auto g = reparse(m.serialize());

    REQUIRE(g.header().stringCount        == n0 + 1);
    REQUIRE(g.header().stringStorageSize  == store0 + 2);
    REQUIRE(g.header().overflowStringCount == h0.overflowStringCount);
    // hello.hbc ends with an Identifier run -> a new String run is needed
    REQUIRE(g.header().stringKindCount    == kinds0 + 1);
    REQUIRE(g.header().fileLength         == m.serialize().size());
    REQUIRE(g.strings().at(idx) == "hi");
    REQUIRE(g.stringKinds().at(idx) == hbc::StringKind::String);
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < n0; ++i) {
        REQUIRE(g.strings()[i]     == f.strings()[i]);
        REQUIRE(g.stringKinds()[i] == f.stringKinds()[i]);
    }
    requireAllFunctionsUnchanged(f, g);
}

TEST_CASE("add_string with >= 255 chars uses the overflow table", "[patcher]") {
    auto f = hbc::HBCFile::open(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/hello.hbc");
    const std::string big(300, 'x');
    auto m = hbc::Module::from(f);
    uint32_t idx = m.add_string(big);
    auto g = reparse(m.serialize());

    REQUIRE(g.header().overflowStringCount == f.header().overflowStringCount + 1);
    REQUIRE(g.header().stringStorageSize   == f.header().stringStorageSize + 300);
    REQUIRE(g.strings().at(idx) == big);
}

TEST_CASE("two add_string calls get consecutive indices and one String run", "[patcher]") {
    auto f = hbc::HBCFile::open(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/hello.hbc");
    const auto n0 = f.header().stringCount;
    auto m = hbc::Module::from(f);
    REQUIRE(m.add_string("aaa") == n0);
    REQUIRE(m.add_string("bbbb") == n0 + 1);
    auto g = reparse(m.serialize());

    REQUIRE(g.header().stringCount == n0 + 2);
    REQUIRE(g.strings().at(n0)     == "aaa");
    REQUIRE(g.strings().at(n0 + 1) == "bbbb");
    // two contiguous Strings -> only one run added
    REQUIRE(g.header().stringKindCount == f.header().stringKindCount + 1);
}

TEST_CASE("add_string on a real bundle with overflow functions", "[patcher]") {
    auto f = openOrSkip(HBC_CORPUS_DIR "/ridemovi.hbc");
    const auto n0 = f.header().stringCount;
    uint32_t ovFuncs0 = 0;
    for (const auto& fn : f.functions()) if (fn.overflowed) ++ovFuncs0;
    REQUIRE(ovFuncs0 > 0);

    auto m = hbc::Module::from(f);
    uint32_t idx = m.add_string("hermit-was-here");
    auto g = reparse(m.serialize());

    REQUIRE(g.header().stringCount == n0 + 1);
    REQUIRE(g.strings().at(idx) == "hermit-was-here");
    uint32_t ovFuncs1 = 0;
    for (const auto& fn : g.functions()) if (fn.overflowed) ++ovFuncs1;
    REQUIRE(ovFuncs1 == ovFuncs0);
    // a sample of functions (start / end / middle) disassembles with no ???
    for (uint32_t i : {0u, g.header().functionCount / 2, g.header().functionCount - 1}) {
        auto ins = g.disasm(i);
        for (const auto& x : ins) REQUIRE(x.mnemonic != "???");
    }
}

TEST_CASE("add_string rejects non-ASCII and empty", "[patcher]") {
```
